CADCraft web design system

Foundations

  • Colors (.md): One base colour at an alpha ladder over a few near-black surfaces in dark, mirrored in light: colour is a signal, never decoration.
  • Icons (.md): Every icon is drawn in code as an SVG path on a 24×24 grid and takes its colour from the surrounding ink (currentColor); no icon font, sp...
  • Motion (.md): Four durations and three easings: motion is fast, short and never decorative — it confirms a state change and gets out of the way.
  • Radius (.md): The corner ladder (2–5px for controls, 12 and 14px for the assistant's blocks and popovers, full round for pills), the one hairline width...
  • Spacing (.md): One gap scale in even steps and one control-height ladder: every inset, gap and control size in the chrome is a token from these two ladd...
  • Typography (.md): Two families (the system UI stack and the mono stack) and one scale of four sizes on screen: 11px for section labels, counts and key caps...

Components

  • Button (.md): It runs one action the moment its label says so: it never navigates and never holds a value.
  • Checkbox (.md): It holds one yes-or-no value the caller owns, and can say that the things it stands for disagree.
  • Chip (.md): It shows one compact fact, a keyword or a suggestion, and it only acts when the caller gives it a handler.
  • Dialog (.md): It holds one task over the page until the task is finished or put away: a titled box of fields with its actions in a footer, while the pa...
  • Field (.md): It takes one line of text and hands every keystroke back to the caller, who owns the value.
  • IconButton (.md): It runs one action drawn as a single glyph, and its title is both its accessible name and the hint a sighted person reads.
  • Kbd (.md): It shows the key or shortcut that runs the action beside it, as a fact to read and never as a control.
  • Row (.md): It is the full-width clickable band of a list: a layer, a command in a listbox or an item of a menu, marked current when it is the select...
  • SectionLabel (.md): It names a panel's section as a real heading, so a screen reader can jump between the sections by heading.
  • Select (.md): It lets the user pick one value from a short, known list, and hands the pick back to the caller, who owns the value.
  • Tab (.md): It brings one view of a strip to the front: a layout over the drawing or a chat in the assistant, marked selected when it is the one show...
  • TextArea (.md): It takes several lines of text, grows to hold them up to a limit, and hands every edit back to the caller, who owns the text.
  • Toggle (.md): It switches one setting on or off in place, under a name that never changes, and says which it is through its pressed state.
  • Tooltip (.md): It is the layer's one hint: a small box beside a control under the pointer or under keyboard focus, saying what the control does not alre...

Rules

  • Rules (.md): every trap and rule ID, the page that answers it and the check that enforces it

Other

  • The web system's design decisions (.md): The lock for the SolidJS UI (apps/ui), taken in the design-system run of 2026-10-28.

Check command: cd apps/ui && bun run check. Machine index: llms.txt.

Colors

Description

One base colour at an alpha ladder over a few near-black surfaces in dark, mirrored in light: colour is a signal, never decoration. This page is the token list, the role of each token, and the measured contrast of every pair; the values themselves live in src/tokens.css (measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22, the run's research notes).

Tokens

Dark is the default (:root); light restates only the roles that change, under :root[data-theme="light"], and inherits the rest.

Each specimen is drawn with the token itself, never a copied value.

  • Icons on --chrome: <span style="background:var(--chrome);color:var(--icon);padding:2px 8px">icon</span>.
  • Action fills: <span style="display:inline-block;width:72px;height:20px;background:var(--accent);vertical-align:middle"></span> <span style="display:inline-block;width:72px;height:20px;background:var(--accent-hover);vertical-align:middle"></span> <span style="display:inline-block;width:72px;height:20px;background:var(--accent-pressed);vertical-align:middle"></span> <span style="display:inline-block;width:72px;height:20px;background:var(--accent-soft);vertical-align:middle"></span> — accent, hover, pressed, soft.

Usage

  • Reach for a role, never a hue: --accent for the one action, --error for a failure, --warn for a caution, because a second meaning per hue makes the interface unreadable at a glance. A setting that is on is not a hue at all: it is the full ink on the faintest fill (Toggle's word, IconButton's selected), or a glyph of its own (Toggle's glyph), and the current layer is the selected fill and the accent bar. --toggle-on is the engine badge's dot and nothing else.
  • Hover and selection are fills, not colour changes — --hover, --fill-active, --fill-pressed over whatever surface the control sits on — because a hue swap changes a control's meaning, while a fill step only moves it.
  • Disabled is a lighter ink (--text-disabled) on an unchanged fill (--fill-disabled), because a disabled control should read as unavailable, not as a different control.
  • On an accent fill the label is --on-accent, never --text, because the fill is the same in both themes' buttons and the ink must stay readable on it; on the error fill it is --on-error, because the dark error fill is darker than the dark accent and the accent's ink misses 4.5 on it.
  • Accent-coloured text is --text-accent, never --accent, because the accent is tuned as a fill and a stroke (3:1) and in light it misses 4.5 as text on every surface but the lightest.
  • A focus ring is --focus-ring, never --accent, because a ring crosses the selected and hover fills and the light accent drops under 3:1 against them. The one exception is the ring on the drawing, --canvas-focus-ring, because the canvas is dark in both themes and a theme ink would fail on it in light.
  • The accent itself stays for fills and strokes that are not focus: the primary button, the current layer's bar, the text caret, a ticked box, the selection tint.
  • The drawing area keeps its own colours (--canvas, --grid-*, --axis-*) in both themes, because a drawing's paper should not change when the chrome's theme does.
  • --text-faint is the lowest ink a reader must still read; anything quieter is --text-disabled, which only disabled controls carry, because an enabled control a reader cannot read is a bug, not a hierarchy.

Accessibility

Contrast, measured by node scripts/contrast-report.mjs (run from the app folder), WCAG 2.x. Every cell is the foreground composited over that surface: ratio, then ✓ at the token's threshold (4.5:1 text, 3:1 icons, borders and the focus ring), ✗ below it, · for the fills, which carry no threshold — their cell shows how visible the step is against the surface. The drawing keeps one dark surface in both themes, so it is not a column: the strokes drawn over it are listed under each grid.

The app's pairs

The inks of src/styles.css, src/interaction.css and src/palette.css, measured in the running app on 2026-11-11 from the browser's computed colours (WCAG 2.x), each over the surface it is drawn on: the sidebar with one layer frozen, one locked and one off; everything selected, so the properties show fields and mixed values; a refused value; a running command with keyword chips; an unknown command; the palette with a query. A hovered or current-row pair is the same computed ink over that row's fill. Text needs 4.5:1; a glyph, a state mark, an edge and a focus ring need 3:1. The layer keys' and the status toggles' inks are Toggle's since that evening (src/ui/ui.css, the tones); the computed colours were compared key by key, state by state, and are the same.

Not tokens

  • The wasm canvas draws its primitives' colours from the tokens through src/canvas.ts; its fallback literals (#181818, #202020, …) only apply when a token is missing, and the palette it reads is the token list above.
  • The axis-x/axis-y hues and the layer glyph colours are fixed in both themes on purpose: they identify canvas objects, not chrome roles.

Icons

Description

Every icon is drawn in code as an SVG path on a 24×24 grid and takes its colour from the surrounding ink (currentColor); no icon font, sprite or third-party artwork ships. The paths live in src/icons.ts, the sizes and inks in src/tokens.css.

Tokens

Sizes

TokenValueRole
--icon-size-sm12pxThe small step: a chip's glyph, a row's trailing action.
--icon-size-md14pxThe default: an icon button's face, a menu row's glyph.
--icon-size-lg16pxThe large step: a tool strip key's glyph, a dialog's header glyph.

Ink

TokenValueRole
--iconvar(--text-dim): dark rgba(240,240,240,.74) / light rgba(20,20,20,.74)The default glyph ink: the secondary text ink. Cursor's measured .66 sat between .74 and .60, three steps no eye told apart, and folded into .74 (src/tokens.css).
--icon-layer-off#8a8a5aA layer switched off.
--icon-layer-frozen#9fd4ffA frozen layer.
--icon-locked#e6b43cA locked layer.

Specimens

  • Sizes, drawn with the tokens: <span style="display:inline-block;width:var(--icon-size-sm);height:var(--icon-size-sm);background:var(--icon);vertical-align:middle"></span> sm 12 <span style="display:inline-block;width:var(--icon-size-md);height:var(--icon-size-md);background:var(--icon);vertical-align:middle"></span> md 14 <span style="display:inline-block;width:var(--icon-size-lg);height:var(--icon-size-lg);background:var(--icon);vertical-align:middle"></span> lg 16
  • Ink on --chrome: <span style="background:var(--chrome);color:var(--icon);padding:2px 6px">icon</span> <span style="background:var(--chrome);color:var(--icon-layer-off);padding:2px 6px">layer-off</span> <span style="background:var(--chrome);color:var(--icon-layer-frozen);padding:2px 6px">frozen</span> <span style="background:var(--chrome);color:var(--icon-locked);padding:2px 6px">locked</span>

The drawn set (ICON_PATHS in src/icons.ts, 24×24, one 1.25px stroke at every size, round caps and joins):

GroupIds
Filenew, open, save
Historyu, redo
Drawline, polyline, circle, arc, rectangle, hatch, text
Modifymove, copy-objects, rotate, mirror, offset, trim, fillet, erase
Annotatedimension-linear
Viewzoom.extents, zoom.window, pan
Inspectproperties, ui.dialog.layers, dist
Outputplot
Assistantsend, stop, plus, close, chevron-right, chevron-down, copy, retry, pick, assistant, eye, eye-off, attach
Shelllayer.on, layer.off, layer.frozen, layer.thawed, layer.locked, layer.unlocked, search, layout.bottom, ui.toggle.palettes, list

The tool strip's glyphs, each drawn at the strip's size and at the two control sizes in the default ink. A glyph is the geometry of what its tool does: a ring of radius 2 is a point the tool takes, a smaller dot a vertex, a centre or a corner that was, and dashes the part a tool removes or the line it reflects about. Each has one idea that is still there in the ten pixels a 16px glyph leaves it, and no two share a silhouette.

The masked value's pair (eye: a pointed lens of two arcs with a ring for the pupil, a masked value is showing; eye-off: the empty lens struck through, the value is masked):

  • eye: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.25" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="width:var(--icon-size-md);height:var(--icon-size-md);color:var(--icon);vertical-align:middle"><path vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke" d="M3 12a10.5 10.5 0 0 1 18 0a10.5 10.5 0 0 1-18 0z M12 9a3 3 0 1 0 0 6a3 3 0 1 0 0-6z"/></svg> md 14 <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.25" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="width:var(--icon-size-sm);height:var(--icon-size-sm);color:var(--icon);vertical-align:middle"><path vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke" d="M3 12a10.5 10.5 0 0 1 18 0a10.5 10.5 0 0 1-18 0z M12 9a3 3 0 1 0 0 6a3 3 0 1 0 0-6z"/></svg> sm 12
  • eye-off: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.25" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="width:var(--icon-size-md);height:var(--icon-size-md);color:var(--icon);vertical-align:middle"><path vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke" d="M3 12a10.5 10.5 0 0 1 18 0a10.5 10.5 0 0 1-18 0z M5.5 4.5l13 15"/></svg> md 14 <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.25" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="width:var(--icon-size-sm);height:var(--icon-size-sm);color:var(--icon);vertical-align:middle"><path vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke" d="M3 12a10.5 10.5 0 0 1 18 0a10.5 10.5 0 0 1-18 0z M5.5 4.5l13 15"/></svg> sm 12

Usage

  • A glyph is currentColor; its container sets the ink (--icon at rest, --text hovered or selected, --text-disabled blocked, --text-accent or --warn for a signal), because an icon must follow the state its control is in.
  • Three sizes only (12/14/16), matched to the control ladder, because a fourth size is a different control. The tool strip's keys draw at 16 in the 24px key, because the drafting glyphs carry grips, dashes and arrowheads that close up at 14; every other icon button draws at 14, and the strip's overflow menu rows with it.
  • One stroke weight at every size: 1.25px on the screen at 12, 14 and 16 (vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke on the path, STROKE in src/icons.ts), because a width on the 24 grid thins with the glyph (the old 1.5 drew 0.75px at 12, 0.875px at 14 and 1px at 16) and a sub-pixel stroke at the glyph ink reads faint.
  • Icons are drawn, never imported: every path is original code on the 24×24 grid, because third-party icon sets carry licences and a foreign stroke grammar.
  • A glyph that means the same thing keeps its id everywhere (save is the floppy, zoom.extents the four corners), because two drawings for one action is a bug a reader reads as two actions. The three eyes are three meanings, so their own ids: layer.on and layer.off are a layer's visibility, eye and eye-off a masked value shown and hidden. The two copies are two meanings too: copy is the clipboard's, copy-objects the drafting tool's.
  • A strip glyph's horizontal and vertical strokes lie on a pixel's middle at 16: on the 24 grid that is 0.75 plus a multiple of 1.5 (3.75, 5.25 … 20.25), never a multiple of 1.5, because a 1.25px stroke on a pixel's middle is one sharp pixel at ratio 1 and between two pixels it is a soft pair twice as wide. text and pan keep a stem on the box's centre line, which an even size has no pixel for (src/icons.test.ts names them and fails on a third).
  • A strip glyph's longer side is 16 to 19 of the 24, its strokes' middles stay 2 clear of the box's edge, and it is at most six strokes (src/icons.test.ts), because a glyph that fills less reads a size smaller than its neighbour and one with more closes up at 16.
  • Tools a drafter picks between at a glance are built differently, not drawn differently: the offset is a pair of strokes and the fillet one stroke with a dot at the corner it rounded; the copy carries a plus on a twin and the window zoom a magnifier on a dragged window; the line is straight between its grips and the polyline bends twice, because two glyphs that differ only in a detail are one glyph at 16.
  • A new glyph keeps the set's grammar: it fills the box from about 3 to 21, lines end and meet round, nothing is filled, a point the tool takes is a ring of radius 2, and what the tool removes or reflects about is dashed, because a glyph in another grammar reads as a foreign control.
  • A path no surface draws is deleted, not kept in reserve (src/icons.test.ts fails on an orphan), because an unused drawing is never looked at and drifts from the set.
  • Status glyphs take the layer colours (--icon-layer-*, --icon-locked) on the dark surfaces and the theme's own stepped inks on the light ones, through Toggle's tone, because the pale layer colours measure under 3:1 on a light row and a state must be seen in both themes.

Accessibility

  • Icons are never the only label: an icon-only control carries aria-label in its component (src/ui/IconButton.tsx), and the check cannot see the rendered accessibility tree, so the browser review covers it.
  • Contrast: --icon measures 9.2:1 over --chrome in dark and 7.7:1 in light, and never under 8.2:1 (dark, --control-hover) or 7.1:1 (light, --control-hover) over any surface (node scripts/contrast-report.mjs, 2026-11-11); the layer inks are exempt as state markers on the canvas. The Colors page carries the full measured grid from scripts/contrast-report.mjs.
  • The 1.25px stroke is the same on the screen at 12, 14 and 16, so a glyph does not thin as it shrinks; the densest glyphs (save, attach) keep their counters open at 12.

Not tokens

  • The 24×24 viewBox and the 1.25 stroke (STROKE) are drawing constants in src/icons.ts, not tokens, because they are the glyphs' own geometry rather than chrome scale.
  • The assistant's COMPOSER_ICONS list and the shell's PANEL_ICONS list are subset markers (the ids no toolbar entry draws, which src/icons.test.ts checks against the map), not a second icon set.

Motion

Description

Four durations and three easings: motion is fast, short and never decorative — it confirms a state change and gets out of the way. The values live in src/tokens.css, measured from Cursor 3.27.22 (durations 50/100/150/200ms; ease on every state transition, ease-out and a strong out-quint on the moves).

Tokens

TokenValueRole
--dur-press0.05sThe measured transform channel: the icon button's press scale.
--dur-fast0.1sThe default, and the measured state transition: a control's fill, its ink, a border colour change.
--dur-med0.15sA panel or a popover appearing.
--dur-slow0.2sThe largest move the chrome makes (a dialog, the assistant panel). Reserved: it is the duration of the "panel / larger change" preset in decisions.md, and no panel moves yet.
--ease-standardeaseThe measured state easing: hover, press and focus feedback on every control (Cursor's .1s ease).
--ease-outcubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)The easing of a move: a surface closing, a panel changing; fast out, settled at the end.
--ease-out-quintcubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)A stronger deceleration for the larger moves (a panel sliding in).

Specimens

Each preset, drawn with its token (hover or focus the bars to replay):

  • <span style="display:inline-block;padding:2px 10px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-control);transition:background var(--dur-press) var(--ease-standard)" onmouseover="this.style.background='var(--fill-active)'" onmouseout="this.style.background='var(--control)'">--dur-press 50ms</span>
  • <span style="display:inline-block;padding:2px 10px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-control);transition:background var(--dur-fast) var(--ease-out)" onmouseover="this.style.background='var(--fill-active)'" onmouseout="this.style.background='var(--control)'">--dur-fast 100ms</span>
  • <span style="display:inline-block;padding:2px 10px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-control);transition:background var(--dur-med) var(--ease-out)" onmouseover="this.style.background='var(--fill-active)'" onmouseout="this.style.background='var(--control)'">--dur-med 150ms</span>
  • <span style="display:inline-block;padding:2px 10px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-control);transition:background var(--dur-slow) var(--ease-out-quint)" onmouseover="this.style.background='var(--fill-active)'" onmouseout="this.style.background='var(--control)'">--dur-slow 200ms</span>

Usage

  • Feedback under the pointer is the fastest (--dur-press for the press scale, --dur-fast for a fill or an ink) and a panel is the slowest (--dur-med–--dur-slow), because feedback under the pointer must beat the eye, while a panel's arrival can take a beat.
  • One easing per job: --ease-standard for a control's state feedback (hover, press, focus), --ease-out for a surface that moves or closes and --ease-out-quint for the largest moves, because each is the curve measured for that job and a curve picked by taste is a preference, not a system.
  • A control's hover and focus feedback is --dur-fast with --ease-standard, on every component of src/ui/, because that is the measured .1s ease and two controls easing differently under one pointer read as two systems.
  • Only background-color, border-color, color, opacity and transform transition, because anything else animates layout and drops frames.
  • Nothing loops, nothing bounces, nothing moves on its own: motion is only ever the consequence of an input, because ambient motion steals attention from the drawing.
  • Exit may be faster than enter, never slower, because a dismissed surface should leave before the eye returns to the canvas. The hint is the limit case: it arrives over --dur-fast and leaves at once, and the next hint along a row arrives at once too (no fade restarts under a moving pointer). Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce it never fades, by its own media query in src/ui/ui.css as well as by the shell's attribute.
  • The hint waits before it shows, and the wait is script, not a token: 0.4s under a resting pointer, none on keyboard focus, none for 0.3s after another hint went away (HINT_DELAY_MS and HINT_WARM_MS in src/ui/Tooltip.tsx), because a box that appears under every passing pointer is noise, and one that makes a keyboard user wait is a delay with no pointer to settle.

Accessibility

  • prefers-reduced-motion is honoured: the shell's animation choice defaults to system (src/app.tsx), which reads the media query live and sets :root[data-animations="off"]; src/styles.css kills every transition and animation under that attribute, so states still change and nothing moves between them.
  • The behaviour under the media query is part of the browser review; the check cannot see rendered motion, and this page does not claim more than the stylesheet shows.
  • Motion here is state feedback only (a fill, a fade, a small slide); there is no parallax, no autoplay and no repeating animation to reduce.

Not tokens

  • The assistant's "turn running" dot pulse is component-local (src/assistant.css), because it is a progress indicator with its own cadence, not a chrome transition.
  • The canvas's repaint cadence is the engine's, not the chrome's, and it does not use these tokens.

Radius

Description

The corner ladder (2–5px for controls, 12 and 14px for the assistant's blocks and popovers, full round for pills), the one hairline width, and the focus ring's stroke: every box in the chrome takes its corner and stroke from these tokens. The values live in src/tokens.css; the roles are the measured Cursor 3.27.22 recipes.

Tokens

Radius

TokenValueRole
--radius-control2pxButtons and inputs: the measured control corner.
--radius-small3pxChips and small wells: one step off the control.
--radius-card4pxCards and list rows.
--radius-composer5pxThe composer's box.
--radius-block12pxThe transcript's message bubble and code block, and the docked composer card (measured).
--radius-popover14pxThe measured popover: the model menu (Cursor §8).
--radius-round9999pxThe pill/circle radius (Chip, IconButton; Cursor §2).

Strokes and elevation

TokenValueRole
--hairline1pxThe one border width: every stroke in the chrome.
--focus-outline-w1pxThe focus ring's stroke.
--focus-outline-offset-1pxThe ring sits inside the control's box, so it never shifts the layout.
--shadow-popover0 3px 8px, 0 2px 5px, 0 1px 1px, each rgba(0,0,0,.12)The measured three-layer shadow under a menu or a popover (Cursor §8).
--tooltip-shadow0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.4) dark / rgba(0,0,0,.16) lightThe measured single layer under the hint (Cursor §8).

Surface levels (which surface a floating thing sits on) are the colour tokens --chrome, --control, --panel and --surface-elevated; their ladder is on the Colors page.

Specimens

  • Radius ladder: <span style="display:inline-block;width:64px;height:24px;background:var(--control);border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:var(--radius-control);vertical-align:middle"></span> control 2 <span style="display:inline-block;width:64px;height:24px;background:var(--control);border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:var(--radius-small);vertical-align:middle"></span> small 3 <span style="display:inline-block;width:64px;height:24px;background:var(--control);border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:var(--radius-card);vertical-align:middle"></span> card 4 <span style="display:inline-block;width:64px;height:24px;background:var(--control);border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:var(--radius-composer);vertical-align:middle"></span> composer 5
  • Round: <span style="display:inline-block;width:48px;height:20px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-round);vertical-align:middle"></span> round
  • Focus ring: <span style="display:inline-block;padding:2px 10px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-control);outline:var(--focus-outline-w) solid var(--accent);outline-offset:var(--focus-outline-offset)">focused</span>
  • The popover's shadow, on --surface-elevated: <span style="display:inline-block;padding:4px 12px;background:var(--surface-elevated);border-radius:var(--radius-card);box-shadow:var(--shadow-popover)">floating</span>

Usage

  • Corners are ladder steps, never eyeballed: a control is --radius-control, a chip --radius-small or --radius-round, a card --radius-card, because mixed corners read as mixed components.
  • A state fill that stays (a selected icon button, an on word of a text toggle) takes --radius-control, because the round fill is the pointer's passing hover and a fill that says on must be a shape of its own.
  • The largest corner is the popover's 14px (--radius-popover), because the large radius is what marks a surface that floats. The assistant's composer is docked in its panel, so its card takes --radius-block, the corner of the prompt bubble and of the stack that sits on it. The 20px --radius-elevated was removed on 2026-11-11: nothing had drawn it since the composer docked.
  • One stroke width: every border is --hairline; a heavier stroke is a different control, not a different border, because a 2px border reads as focus.
  • The focus ring is 1px, inset (--focus-outline-offset: -1px), in --accent, because an outset ring shifts a row and an inset ring never does.
  • One shadow per floating kind, one direction: a menu or a popover casts --shadow-popover and the hint --tooltip-shadow; nothing else casts one, because a shadow on a docked surface invents an elevation it does not have.
  • A pill shape takes --radius-round, because at the chip's 20px height any radius past 10px draws the same pill, and one token for it leaves no second pill to drift.

Accessibility

  • The focus ring is 1px in --accent, offset -1px (inset). Its contrast against every surface level is covered by the Colors page's measured grid: --accent measures 6.0:1 over --control in dark, 3.8:1 in light (above the 3:1 non-text threshold).
  • The ring is never removed without a replacement: the components' :focus-visible styles in src/ui/ui.css carry it, and the check cannot see focus behavior, so the browser review covers it.

Not tokens

  • SVG stroke widths inside icon paths are drawing values (1.5 on the 24×24 grid in src/icons.ts), not box strokes, because an icon's stroke must stay proportional to its viewBox.
  • The canvas's selection stroke width is an engine constant, not chrome, for the same reason.

Spacing

Description

One gap scale in even steps and one control-height ladder: every inset, gap and control size in the chrome is a token from these two ladders, so density stays constant across panels. The values live in src/tokens.css; the roles are the measured Cursor 3.27.22 recipes.

Specimens

The scale as bars, each drawn with its own token:

  • <span style="display:inline-block;width:2px;height:14px;background:var(--accent);vertical-align:middle"></span> --gap-2
  • <span style="display:inline-block;width:4px;height:14px;background:var(--accent);vertical-align:middle"></span> --gap-4
  • <span style="display:inline-block;width:8px;height:14px;background:var(--accent);vertical-align:middle"></span> --gap-8
  • <span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:14px;background:var(--accent);vertical-align:middle"></span> --gap-12
  • <span style="display:inline-block;width:16px;height:14px;background:var(--accent);vertical-align:middle"></span> --gap-16

Control ladder, each at its token height: <span style="display:inline-block;height:var(--control-h-chip);padding:0 8px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-round);vertical-align:middle">chip 20</span> <span style="display:inline-block;height:var(--control-h-row);padding:0 8px;background:var(--control);vertical-align:middle">row 22</span> <span style="display:inline-block;height:var(--control-h-input);padding:0 8px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-control);vertical-align:middle">input 24</span> <span style="display:inline-block;height:var(--control-h-button);padding:0 8px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-control);vertical-align:middle">button 28</span> <span style="display:inline-block;height:var(--control-h-tab);padding:0 8px;background:var(--control);vertical-align:middle">tab 35</span>

Usage

  • Pick the step, never the pixel: a gap is one of the scale's values, because a one-off 7px is how two panels drift apart.
  • --gap-4 is the default; reach past it only when this page's table names the case, because an unnamed gap is a missing decision.
  • Insets come from the padding tokens, not the gap tokens, because a padding is part of a control's box and must survive a border change.
  • Controls stand on the height ladder (20/22/24/28/35), because two controls in one row align by their boxes, not their text.
  • Density never changes with the viewport; the canvas takes the space, because a chrome that scales steals the drawing's room.

Accessibility

  • Target sizes: the ladder's smallest box is the 20px chip; the button is 28px tall and the icon button 24px, all measured from src/tokens.css. The 24px minimum recommended by WCAG 2.5.8 is met by buttons and icon buttons; chips are not interactive targets on their own.
  • Reflow at 320px: not measured this run. The fixed 260px rail and the toolbar are the risk this review should cover first.

Not tokens

  • The canvas's own metrics (world units, line widths) are engine values, not chrome spacing; src/canvas.ts maps them, and they never appear as chrome gaps.
  • One-off optical nudges inside an icon's own SVG viewBox stay raw in src/icons.ts, because they are drawing coordinates, not layout.

Typography

Description

Two families (the system UI stack and the mono stack) and one scale of four sizes on screen: 11px for section labels, counts and key caps, 12px for secondary text, 13px for everything read or typed, and the 12px mono. Text never takes a size outside this scale, and sizes never scale with the viewport. The values live in src/tokens.css. They were measured from Cursor 3.27.22, which gave six sizes (its composer is 15px on a 24px line, its button 14px, its small text 11.5px); on 2026-11-11 the shell's 13px scale won and those three folded into it (decisions.md, "One type scale").

Tokens

TokenValueRole

--font-family-mono"Hack", ui-monospace, "Cascadia Mono", Consolas, monospaceThe monospace family: coordinates, command input, code in messages.

  • Chip: <span style="font-family:var(--font-family);font-size:var(--font-chip)">Bodycam</span>

Usage

  • One size per role, never per surface: a button is --font-button wherever it sits, because a control that changes size between panels reads as a different control.
  • Pick the size by what the text is for, from three: 13px if it is read or typed, 12px if it is secondary to something beside it, 11px if it is a label, a count or a key cap, because a fourth sans size is a second scale: the assistant at 15px beside a 13px shell read as another product.
  • The mono family is for machine text only — coordinates, commands, code — because mixing the families inside one sentence makes both harder to scan.
  • Uppercase belongs to the heading of a section (SectionLabel) and to the status bar's drafting toggles, never to a sentence, because capitals on a sentence read as shouting. A section label adds no letter-spacing: the measured header is 11px at weight 700 in capitals at the face's own spacing (research §2, the sidebar's section header), and the bold weight already separates the letters. This line asked for 0.05em–0.06em until 2026-11-11; the measurement and src/ui/ui.css had none, and the page was the side that moved (src/ui/recipe.test.ts holds the recipe to it).
  • The smallest size is --font-chip at 11px; nothing in the chrome goes below it, because below 11px the stroke font's glyphs start to blur at 100%.
  • Sizes do not scale with the viewport; the app's chrome keeps its density and the canvas handles scale, because a zoomed chrome wastes the drawing's space.

Leading

A line height is a token, or it is a box height by a rule written here. Until 2026-11-11 the layer's lines were 1, var(--gap-16) and the face's own normal, which is 17px for 13px type in Segoe UI and another height in another face, so a label sat where each platform's font put it.

  • In the layer (src/ui/ui.css) every component that draws text sets line-height: var(--leading-ui), 16px, for all three sizes of the scale, because one line under 11, 12 and 13px type keeps a key cap, a shortcut and a label on one centre in the same row.
  • A control of one line takes its height from a control token (--control-h-*), never from its line, because the box is what the grid of a bar or a list is built from; the box is at least 20px and centres the 16px line. Changing the line cannot change a box.
  • Text that wraps (a checkbox's label, a text area, the hint) stacks on the same 16px line, because a wrapped label beside a one-line control must start on that control's line.
  • Prose that is read, not scanned, takes --composer-leading (20px): the assistant's composer and transcript.
  • The exceptions, each stated in src/ui/ui.css where it is and held by src/ui/recipe.test.ts: the bare text area inherits its card's line; a key cap inside the hint is calc(var(--leading-ui) - var(--hairline) * 2), so the hint is one line tall with or without a shortcut; a text area under a coarse pointer is calc(var(--leading-ui) * 1.25) (20px) for its 16px type; and SectionLabel sets no line.
  • SectionLabel is the one component whose line is not the token: it has no height and no padding, so its line is its box, and the 16px line would make every section heading 1px taller. It stays the face's own (15px in Segoe UI) until its box is given a height of its own.

What each component's line was and is (boxes measured in the browser before and after: none changed; the text of a tab, a text toggle and a listbox option moved by half a pixel, and a capture of the whole shell before and after differed in no pixel of text):

ComponentWasIsBox, unchanged

Outside the layer the shell still sets lines of its own, and they are not one system yet: the status bar's line (its box, 21px), a layer's name (--control-h-row, its box), the menu's typed name (--menu-row-h, its box), the command history (1.45), the assistant's and the palette's 1.5 and 1.4 blocks (19.5px and 18px at 13px), and var(--gap-16) used as a 16px line in src/styles.css and src/assistant.css. Those sheets take --leading-ui where they mean the layer's line and --composer-leading where they mean prose.

Accessibility

  • The smallest type in use is 11px (--font-chip), measured from src/tokens.css; every other role is larger, up to 13px (--font-body). Under a coarse pointer a field, a text area and the palette's input are at least 16px, so a phone does not zoom into them.
  • Body copy sits at 13px; the assistant's messages and composer are on a 20px line (1.54), the command history on 1.45.
  • Zoom to 200% without clipping: not measured this run. The fixed-width chrome (the 252px sidebar) is the risk this review should cover first.

Not tokens

  • Font weight is set per component in src/ui/ui.css and src/styles.css, because it only matters for the roles named in the composite table above; a weight token would be a second scale for one value. The line is a token in the layer ("Leading" above) and still set per rule in the shell's own sheets.
  • The mono family names Hack first, but no font file ships with the app: the stack falls through to the platform's mono when it is absent, so nothing is embedded and nothing is licensed.

Button

Description

It runs one action the moment its label says so: it never navigates and never holds a value.

Variants

variant

  • primary: the one action of the pane or dialog; the accent fill. Used at 1 call site in the assistant (the setup sheet's Save), and the dialog's OK.
  • secondary: the default action; the .08 fill that Cursor's own default button draws. Used at 3 call sites (the title bar's command centre, the setup sheet's Check connection and the changes row's Keep).
  • ghost: a quiet action on a tool bar or in a list; no resting fill, the full ink. Used at 7 call sites (the transcript's Show earlier, the setup sheet's Cancel, the two Stop buttons of a running turn, the changes row's Undo all, and the dialog's Select all and Clear all).
  • quiet: an action that must not compete with what it stands beside, a title it changes or a line it follows; no resting fill and the secondary ink (--text-dim), waking to the full ink on ghost's own fills under the pointer and the press, as the ghost IconButton does. Measured on the setup sheet, dark and light: the label 9.17 and 7.82 at rest, 13.35 and 15.24 on the .08 hover fill, 11.12 and 13.37 on the .14 pressed fill; the ring 6.43 and 6.60 against the sheet; the disabled label 3.08 and 2.30, the layer's one disabled ink, which no contrast rule binds. Until 2026-11-12 the sheet dimmed a ghost from its own stylesheet, a colour set on a layer component from outside. Used at 1 call site (the setup sheet's Change).
  • danger: a destructive action; the error fill. Used at 0 call sites.

Example: A blocked action at the disabled ink and fill. (docs/system/examples/button/disabled.tsx)

import { Button } from "../../../../src/ui/Button";

/** Disabled, and still reachable: the `title` says why, in the hint and as the description. */
export default function Disabled() {
  return (
    <Button variant="primary" disabled title="To save, choose a provider or type a base URL.">
      Save
    </Button>
  );
}

State precedence

  • Hover and Focused: Focused wins. The ring stays drawn while the pointer is over the button; hover only steps the fill.
  • Hover and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled button keeps its resting fill under the pointer and takes no click.
  • Pressed and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn while the button is held down; the quiet fill stays on the hover rung.
  • Pressed and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled button never takes the pressed fill.
  • Focused and Disabled: both show. A disabled button takes focus and the ring, so a keyboard user can reach its hint; Enter and Space do nothing.
  • Hinted and Hover: both show. The hint follows the hover after its delay.
  • Hinted and Focused: both show. The hint arrives with the ring, with no delay.
  • Hinted and Pressed: Pressed wins. The press puts the hint away.
  • Hinted and Disabled: both show. The hint is how a disabled button says why it is blocked.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
The pointer enters or leavesinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-colorThe fill changes at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition.
The pointer presses downinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-colorThe fill changes at once, by the same rule.
The pointer enters, leaves or presses a quiet buttoninputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-color, colorThe fill and the ink change at once, by the same rule.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
ariaLabel?stringThe accessible name, when the visible label is a value rather than the action (the command centre shows the drawing's name and is the "Search commands" button).
children?ElementThe label.
controls?stringThe id of the region a disclosure shows and hides: sets aria-controls.
disabled?booleanBlocks the click, drops the label to the disabled ink and the fill to the disabled step.
expanded?booleanA disclosure: the button shows and hides a region of the page and says whether it is showing now (aria-expanded).
onClick?((event: MouseEvent) => void)Runs on click.
shortcut?stringThe shortcut that runs the same action, as the user reads it ("Ctrl+Shift+P"): a key cap in the hint and aria-keyshortcuts on the button.
size?ButtonSizeThe control size.
title?stringThe hint: what the label leaves out, or why the button is disabled.
type?"button" | "submit" | "reset"The native type.
variant?ButtonVariantThe purpose of the action.
  • variant: the purpose of the action; the token layer picks the look. Defaults to secondary.
  • size: the control height; md is 28px and sm is 24px. It never changes the label's size.
  • type: defaults to button so a button inside a form never submits by accident.
  • disabled: blocks the click and drops the ink to the disabled step. It sets aria-disabled="true", never the native disabled, so the button stays in the Tab order and under the pointer and its hint can say why.
  • title: the hint, shown in the layer's hint box and tied to the button as its accessible description (aria-describedby). It is what the label leaves out, or why the button is disabled; it is never the name, and no native title attribute is rendered. A title equal to the label draws no hint and adds no description.
  • shortcut: the shortcut that runs the same action, as the user reads it (Ctrl+Shift+P): a key cap after the hint's text, and aria-keyshortcuts on the button. A title that ends in the shortcut in brackets still draws the cap, without the attribute.
  • ariaLabel: the accessible name, only for a button whose visible label is a value rather than its action.
  • expanded, controls: a disclosure. The button shows and hides a region (the piece's passing checks, src/components/PiecePanel.tsx) and says whether it is showing now (aria-expanded) and which region it is (aria-controls, the region's id). Its label says what is folded ("All 4 checks pass"), never "Show".
  • onClick: runs on click; a disabled button never fires it.

Usage

When to use

  • The user runs one action and expects it to happen now: saving, closing, deleting, opening a dialog.
  • The action is the pane's or dialog's main one, and there is exactly one of it: the primary variant.

When not to use

  • The control is a glyph with no label. Use IconButton instead.
  • The text is a status or a value rather than an action. Use Chip instead.
  • The clickable band is a list item rather than an action. Use Row instead.

Rules

  • rule/button-variant-purpose: When a surface needs a button, pick variant by the action's purpose — 1 primary per view, secondary for the default, ghost for a quiet action, quiet for one that stands beside a title or a line and must read after it, danger for a destructive one — because two accent fills in one row leave no single action and Cursor's own default button is the quiet one. Evidence: app 5/5 variants, docs/system/decisions.md. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: <Button variant="primary">Cancel</Button>
  • Do: <Button>Cancel</Button>
  • rule/button-quiet-not-dimmed: When an action must read after the text beside it, pass variant="quiet" and leave every ink and fill of a Button to the layer, because an ink set from a surface's stylesheet reaches 1 state: the dimmed ghost kept the secondary ink on the .14 pressed fill, and a disabled one would have kept it too. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:1033, the setup sheet's Change, dimmed until 2026-11-12 by .assistant-setup-change .ui-button. Check: test src/ui/recipe.test.ts.
  • Don't: .assistant-setup-change .ui-button { color: var(--text-dim) }
  • Do: <Button variant="quiet" size="sm" title="Choose another provider">Change</Button>
  • rule/button-state-ladder: When a button is hovered, step the fill one rung — .08 to .14 — and hold that rung while pressed, because the measured glass button adds no third step and a fill step reads as feedback without moving the label or the box. Evidence: measured .08/.14/.14, docs/system/decisions.md. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: .my-button:hover { color: var(--accent) } — a colour change instead of a fill step.
  • Do: .ui-button--secondary:hover { background: var(--fill-active) }
  • rule/button-disabled-reason: When a button is disabled by something the user can fix, pass the reason as title in 1 short sentence, because a disabled button stays focusable and hoverable for exactly this and a dead button with 0 words leaves the user guessing what to fill in. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:804, the setup sheet's Save with title={blocker() ?? undefined}. Check: test src/ui/Button.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Button variant="primary" disabled={blocker() !== null}>Save</Button>
  • Do: <Button variant="primary" disabled={blocker() !== null} title={blocker() ?? undefined}>Save</Button>
  • rule/button-title-adds: When a button takes title, write what the label leaves out and 0 words that repeat it, because the label is the name and the hint is announced after it as the description: "Save, button, Save" says the same thing twice, and the layer draws no box for a repeat. Evidence: single use src/components/TopBar.tsx:59, the command centre's "Command palette" hint over a name that already says "Search commands". Check: test src/ui/Button.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Button title="Save">Save</Button>
  • Do: <Button title="Check the address and the key">Check connection</Button>

Content

  • rule/button-label-verb: When the label is written, use a verb the user recognizes in sentence case — Save, Delete, Undo all — because the label is the action's name and the accessible name comes from it. Evidence: app 5/6 labels are verbs or verb phrases, src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:1046, the label "Undo all" (the sixth, the command centre, is labelled with the drawing's name and names its action in its title). Check: review src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.
  • Don't: <Button>SAVE</Button>
  • Do: <Button>Save</Button>
  • rule/button-aria-label-value: When a button's visible label is a value rather than its action, pass ariaLabel starting with the action and holding the visible text, and pass it on 0 other buttons, because a drawing's name alone is announced as "Bracket, button" with no action in it, while an aria-label over a verb label hides the word a speech-input user says to press it. Evidence: single use src/components/TopBar.tsx:59, the command centre labelled with the drawing's name. Check: test src/ui/Button.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Button ariaLabel="Store the drawing">Save</Button>
  • Do: <Button size="sm" ariaLabel={"Search commands, " + title()}>{title()}</Button>

Anti-slop

  • rule/button-canonical-element: When a surface needs a button, render Button rather than a raw <button> with its own class, because the replaced classes paint 6 different hover fills and 3 different radii by hand. Evidence: app 22/22 lines across assistant.css and AssistantPane.tsx, rg -c "assistant-send|assistant-save|assistant-ghost|assistant-preset" src. Check: review src/ui/Button.tsx.
  • Don't: <button class="assistant-ghost" onClick={save}>Save</button>
  • Do: <Button variant="ghost" onClick={save}>Save</Button>

Limits

  • rule/button-row-limit: When one row or dialog footer holds more than 3 buttons, move the rest into a menu, because the measured composer toolbar holds 3 actions at 24px each and a fourth starts competing with the input. Evidence: measured 3 actions at 24px, docs/system/decisions.md. Check: review src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.
  • Don't: 5 buttons side by side in the pane's toolbar row.
  • Do: 2 buttons in the row and the rest inside a menu.

Accessibility

Rests on the native <button> element: role, Enter and Space, and form behaviour come from the platform. Disabled is the layer's own: aria-disabled="true" with the click refused on the button itself (refuseWhenDisabled in src/ui/Button.tsx), because the native disabled takes a button out of the Tab order and, in some of the system webviews the desktop app runs in, out of the pointer's reach, and a control nobody can reach cannot say why it is blocked (docs/system/decisions.md, "Disabled controls"). The hint is the description, never the name.

Keyboard

Related

  • IconButton: when the action is one glyph with a tooltip and no label.
  • Row: when the clickable band is a list item rather than an action.
  • Chip: when the text is a fact or a value, not an action.
  • Field: when the control holds an editable value rather than performing an action.
  • SectionLabel: when the text names a group rather than performing an action.
  • Tab: when the control brings one view of a strip to the front rather than running an action.
  • Kbd: when the text is the key that runs an action beside the button, not the action itself.
  • Tooltip: the hint box a button's title shows in; never wrap a button in one.
  • Checkbox: when the control holds a yes or no rather than running an action.

Checkbox

Description

It holds one yes-or-no value the caller owns, and can say that the things it stands for disagree.

import { Checkbox } from "../../../../src/ui/Checkbox";, source src/ui/Checkbox.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/native-control, trap/field-label, trap/label-unbound, trap/field-error-link (n/a: a tick has no refused state, and a line of help is tied by describedBy), trap/toggle-switch-submit, trap/toggle-indeterminate, trap/touch-hover-flash, trap/hover-unguarded, trap/touch-tap-highlight, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/disabled-still-hovers, trap/color-only-status.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — a native <input type="checkbox"> drawn from the layer's tokens (the accent fill and its --on-accent ink are the primary Button's measured pair, docs/system/decisions.md), and no registry item ships it.

Examples

<Checkbox checked={snap()} onChange={setSnap}>Snap to grid</Checkbox> — a setting with its label; the whole label is the target.

Real uses, 4 call sites (rg -c "<Checkbox" src/components → src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:2, src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:1):

  • src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:108 — the Drafting Settings dialog's switches (Snap on, Grid on, Polar tracking on, and the rest), each with its label as children and a refusal tied by describedBy.
  • src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:222 — the dialog's box per object snap: the label is the snap's marker and its name.
  • src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:191 — the palette's yes-or-no rows: named by the row's label, mixed when the picked objects disagree.

Variants

Not applicable

Not applicable: no variant axes — a checkbox is one 14px box with or without a label; ticked, mixed and disabled are states.

import { Checkbox } from "../../../../src/ui/Checkbox";

export default function Checked() {
  return <Checkbox checked onChange={() => undefined}>Show the grid</Checkbox>;
}

Example: Objects that disagree: the dash. (docs/system/examples/checkbox/mixed.tsx)

import { Checkbox } from "../../../../src/ui/Checkbox";

  return <Checkbox checked disabled>Plot this layer</Checkbox>;
}

State precedence

  • Mixed and Checked: Mixed wins. The dash shows whatever checked says, and the element reports not checked.
  • Hover and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn while the box takes the hover fill.
  • Hover and Checked: both show. The tick stays on the accent's hover step.
  • Pressed and Hover: Pressed wins. The pressed fill replaces the hover fill while the pointer is down.
  • Pressed and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn while the box is held down.
  • Focused and Checked: both show. The ring stands a hairline off the filled box, so it is never the accent on the accent.
  • Focused and Mixed: both show. The ring stands off the filled box as it does when ticked.
  • Disabled and Hover: Disabled wins. A disabled box takes no fill under the pointer.
  • Disabled and Checked: both show. The tick stays, at the disabled ink on the disabled fill.
  • Disabled and Mixed: both show. The dash stays, at the disabled ink on the disabled fill.
  • Disabled and Focused: Not applicable: a natively disabled box takes no focus.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
The value changes, or the pointer enters, presses or leavesinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-color, border-colorThe fill and the stroke change at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition. The mark appears at once in every setting.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
ariaLabel?stringThe accessible name when the box has no visible label.
checked?booleanWhether the box is ticked.
children?ElementThe visible label.
describedBy?stringThe id of a line of help beside the box (several, space-separated): sets aria-describedby.
disabled?booleanBlocks the press and drops the box and the label to the disabled ink.
id?stringThe box's id, for a visible <label for> that stands apart from it (a row's own label in another column): that label is then the name, and no ariaLabel is passed.
mixed?booleanThe box stands for values that disagree: the dash, indeterminate and aria-checked="mixed".
onChange?((checked: boolean) => void)Runs when the user presses the box or its label, with the state the press asks for.
  • checked: whether the box is ticked; the caller holds it.
  • onChange: runs with the state a press asks for. The box then shows what checked and mixed say, so a change the caller refuses does not stay drawn.
  • mixed: the box stands for values that disagree; sets indeterminate and aria-checked="mixed".
  • disabled: the native attribute; blocks the press and drops the ink.
  • ariaLabel: the accessible name when the box has no visible label.
  • id: the box's id, for a visible <label for> that stands apart from it (a row's own label in another column); that label is then the name and no ariaLabel is passed. A label passed as children needs none: it wraps the box. Used at 0 call sites.
  • describedBy: the id of a line of help (several, space-separated); sets aria-describedby.
  • children: the visible label. The whole of it is clickable.

Usage

When to use

  • A setting is on or off and is read as a fact about the thing beside it: Closed, Annotative, Show the grid.
  • One box stands for several objects, which may disagree.

When not to use

  • The control runs an action rather than holding a value. Use Button instead.
  • The value is 1 of 3 or more choices. Use Select instead.
  • The control is a glyph that switches a mode on a tool bar. Use IconButton with selected instead.

Rules

  • rule/checkbox-name: When a checkbox is rendered, give it a visible label as its children or, where the row already shows the name, an ariaLabel, because a box with neither is announced as 1 unnamed check box. Evidence: single use src/ui/Checkbox.tsx:57, the aria-label the prop sets beside the wrapping <label>. Check: test src/ui/Checkbox.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Checkbox checked={closed()} onChange={setClosed} />
  • Do: <Checkbox ariaLabel="Closed" checked={closed()} onChange={setClosed} />
  • rule/checkbox-label-inside: When a checkbox has a visible label, pass the words as the children of Checkbox rather than as a sibling element, because the component's <label> wraps the box and the words, which makes all of them 1 target, and a sibling <span> leaves a dead gap that reads as broken. Evidence: single use src/ui/Checkbox.tsx:50, the wrapping <label>. Check: test src/ui/Checkbox.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Checkbox checked={grid()} onChange={setGrid} /><span>Show the grid</span>
  • Do: <Checkbox checked={grid()} onChange={setGrid}>Show the grid</Checkbox>
  • rule/checkbox-mixed-three-states: When one box stands for several objects, pass mixed while they disagree and set it to false in onChange, because the first press on a mixed box asks for ticked and all 3 states must be reachable: mixed to ticked, ticked to empty, empty to ticked. Evidence: single use src/ui/Checkbox.tsx:45, the indeterminate property the prop sets. Check: test src/ui/Checkbox.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Checkbox checked={false} ariaLabel="Annotative" onChange={setAll} /> for objects that disagree.
  • Do: <Checkbox mixed={disagree()} checked={all()} ariaLabel="Annotative" onChange={setAll} />
  • rule/checkbox-owns-nothing: When onChange runs, set the caller's own value from its argument (or refuse it), because the box redraws from checked and mixed after every press and keeps 0 state of its own. Evidence: single use src/ui/Checkbox.tsx:63, the redraw after the caller has heard the press. Check: test src/ui/Checkbox.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Checkbox onChange={() => save()}>Snap</Checkbox> with no checked.
  • Do: <Checkbox checked={snap()} onChange={setSnap}>Snap</Checkbox>

Content

  • rule/checkbox-label-positive: When a checkbox's label is written, name what is true when the box is ticked, in 1 to 4 words in the positive form (Show the grid), because a ticked box beside a negative label has to be read twice. Evidence: single use src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:192, the palette's yes-or-no rows, labelled by the property's name. Check: review src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <Checkbox checked={!grid()} onChange={(off) => setGrid(!off)}>Do not show the grid</Checkbox>
  • Do: <Checkbox checked={grid()} onChange={setGrid}>Show the grid</Checkbox>

Anti-slop

  • rule/checkbox-canonical-element: When a surface needs a tick box, render Checkbox rather than a raw <input type="checkbox"> with accent-color, because the platform draws that box in its own shape, size and tick in each of the 3 system webviews the desktop app runs in. Evidence: single use src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:192, which replaced .prop-check with accent-color. Check: review src/ui/Checkbox.tsx.
  • Don't: <input class="prop-check" type="checkbox" checked={on} aria-label="Closed" />
  • Do: <Checkbox ariaLabel="Closed" checked={on} onChange={setOn} />

Limits

  • rule/checkbox-touch-target: When checkboxes without labels stack in rows, keep the rows at least 24px apart centre to centre under a coarse pointer, because each 14px box takes a 24px target around its middle there and two targets in rows 22px apart overlap by 2px. Evidence: measured 14px box and a 24px by 24px target on its label under the coarse rules, in the browser, 2026-11-11. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: .my-row { height: var(--control-h-row) } around a bare <Checkbox ariaLabel="Closed" /> on a touch screen.
  • Do: @media (pointer: coarse) { .my-row { min-height: var(--control-h-input) } }

Accessibility

Rests on the native <input type="checkbox"> inside a <label>: role, Space, the label's click, form participation and disabled come from the platform. The drawn mark is aria-hidden.

Related

  • Select: when the value is one of several rather than yes or no.
  • IconButton: when the switch is a glyph on a tool bar (selected).

Chip

Description

It shows one compact fact, a keyword or a suggestion, and it only acts when the caller gives it a handler.

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the pill radius, the 20px height and the accent tint are measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (docs/system/decisions.md and §5), and no registry item ships it.

<Chip>26 objects</Chip> — the selection count as a static fact.

  • src/components/InlineAsk.tsx — the inline ask's selection (neutral, static): how many objects on the drawing go with the message ("3 selected"), with a hint that says so. Added 2026-11-12.
  • src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:763 — the setup sheet's model chips: one per model the connection check listed, click to put it in the Model field; the one in the field takes tone="accent", the rest neutral.
  • src/components/CommandLine.tsx:60 — the command line's keyword row (tone="accent"): one chip per keyword the open command offers, click to submit it.

Variants

tone

  • neutral: a quiet fact or a value; transparent, at the faint ink. Used at 1 call site (the setup sheet's model chips that are not the chosen one).
  • accent: a keyword or a suggestion the user can pick; the accent-tinted fill. Used at 2 call sites (the command line's keyword chip, and the setup sheet's chosen model).

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
StaticThe caller passes no handler.Read it. It is a <span>: no tab stop, no pointer.The pill's text; no cursor change.test
RestThe caller passes onClick.Click it, or Tab to it.The pill is a <button>; the cursor is a pointer.test
HoverThe pointer is over the interactive chip, on a device with a hover pointer.Click it.The .08 fill.by hand
PressedThe pointer is held down.Release to run the handler.The .14 fill; an accent chip holds the .08 hover fill, where its ink still reads.by hand
FocusedKeyboard focus arrives by Tab.Enter or Space runs the handler.The 1px ring in the focus ink at offset -1, following the pill.by hand

State precedence

  • Static and Hover: Not applicable: a static chip is a <span> and takes no pointer or hover styles.
  • Hover and Focused: Focused wins. The ring stays drawn while the pointer is over the chip; hover only adds the fill.
  • Pressed and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn while the chip is held down.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
The pointer enters or leaves an interactive chipinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-colorThe fill changes at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
children?ElementThe chip's text.
onClick?((event: MouseEvent) => void)When present the chip is interactive and renders as a <button>; without it, a <span>.
title?stringThe hint: what the chip's text leaves out.
tone?ChipToneThe tone.
  • tone: neutral or accent; defaults to neutral.
  • onClick: when present the chip renders as a <button>; without it, as a <span>.
  • title: the hint, shown in the layer's hint box after 0.4s under a mouse or a pen and at once when a key moves focus onto an interactive chip; no native title attribute is rendered. The chip's text is its name; on the interactive form the title is tied to the button as its accessible description (aria-describedby), and on the static form it is for the eye only, so nothing a screen-reader user needs goes there. A title equal to the text draws no hint. A chip a surface clips shows its full text in the hint by itself.
  • children: the chip's text: a noun or a short value, never a sentence.

Usage

When to use

  • A value or a status needs a compact, non-editable shape: the selection count, the current units, a keyword.
  • A list of keywords or suggestions can be picked one at a time, and each pick runs an action.

When not to use

  • The user runs an action that needs a label. Use Button instead.
  • The control is a glyph with a tooltip. Use IconButton instead.
  • The value is editable. Use Field instead.

Rules

  • rule/chip-interactive-only-with-handler: When a chip runs an action, pass onClick so it renders as a <button>; when it is a fact, pass nothing so it stays a <span>, because a fact in the tab order adds a stop that does nothing. Evidence: app 2/2 chip surfaces — 1 interactive and 1 static — src/components/CommandLine.tsx:61 and src/components/StatusBar.tsx:109 (the status bar's current-layer item, a static fact). Check: test src/ui/Chip.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Chip>26 objects</Chip> inside an onClick wrapper div.
  • Do: <Chip onClick={() => pick("line")}>line</Chip>
  • rule/chip-tone-meaning: When a chip's tone is picked, use accent only for a keyword the user can pick and neutral for a value, because the accent tint is the app's signal for the accent role and 2 tinted chips in one row read as 2 selections. Evidence: app 2/2 chips, accent only on the keyword row, src/components/CommandLine.tsx:60. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: <Chip tone="accent">26 objects</Chip>
  • Do: <Chip>26 objects</Chip>

Content

  • rule/chip-text-short: When a chip's text is written, keep it to 1 word or a number plus its unit (26 objects, line, mm), because the pill is 20px tall and a third word starts wrapping the row. Evidence: single use src/components/CommandLine.tsx:60, the label "line". Check: review src/components/CommandLine.tsx.
  • Don't: <Chip>The current drawing has 26 objects</Chip>
  • Do: <Chip>26 objects</Chip>

Anti-slop

  • rule/chip-canonical-element: When a surface needs a chip, render Chip rather than a styled <span> or <button> with its own pill, because the replaced class hard-codes its own radius and hover and skips the static/interactive split. Evidence: app 4/4 lines in src/interaction.css, rg -c "keyword-chip" src. Check: review src/ui/Chip.tsx.
  • Don't: <span class="keyword-chip">line</span> with a click handler on the row.
  • Do: <Chip tone="accent" onClick={() => pick("line")}>line</Chip>

Limits

  • rule/chip-row-limit: When a chip row holds more than 6 chips, wrap the row or move the rest behind a "More" chip, because the measured chip is 20px tall with 8px side padding and a 608px composer row fits 6 of them before the row wraps. Evidence: measured 20px chip and 608px composer, docs/system/decisions.md. Check: review src/components/CommandLine.tsx.
  • Don't: 9 chips in one unwrapped row.
  • Do: 6 chips and a "More" chip that opens the rest.
  • rule/chip-touch-target: When interactive chips sit in a row, keep at least 4px between them and between 2 rows of them, because under a coarse pointer each 20px pill keeps its drawn size and takes a 24px target from an invisible ::after 2px past every edge, and closer pills overlap their targets. Evidence: measured 20px pill with a 24px ::after target, src/ui/ui.css:1558. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: .my-chips { display: flex; gap: 0 }
  • Do: .my-chips { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--gap-4) }

Accessibility

Rests on the native element each form renders: a <span> for the static chip, a <button> for the interactive one.

Keyboard

EnterThe focused chip.Runs the handler.Stays on the chip.test
SpaceThe focused chip.Runs the handler on release, exactly once.Stays on the chip.by hand

Related

  • Button: when the action needs a label and a full control height.
  • IconButton: when the action is a glyph.
  • Field: when the value is editable.
  • SectionLabel: when the text names a group rather than a value.
  • Tab: when the control brings one view of a strip to the front rather than stating a fact.
  • Kbd: when the text is the key that runs an action rather than a value or a keyword.
  • Tooltip: the hint box a chip's title and its clipped label show in; never wrap a chip in one.
  • TextArea: when the text is written by the person over several lines.

Dialog

Description

It holds one task over the page until the task is finished or put away: a titled box of fields with its actions in a footer, while the page behind takes no input.

import { Dialog } from "../../../../src/ui/Dialog";, source src/ui/Dialog.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/overlay-conditional-render, trap/native-control, trap/button-div, trap/role-button, trap/button-icon-name, trap/button-type, trap/field-form-enter, trap/touch-autofocus, trap/viewport-height, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/overflow-scrollbar, trap/label-unbound (n/a: the dialog draws no label; a caller's fields bring their own), trap/motion-ease-in-enter (n/a: the dialog arrives and leaves without motion), trap/hover-unguarded (n/a: the box has no hover state; its close key is an IconButton).

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — a native <dialog> opened with showModal() (src/ui/Dialog.tsx:103), so the focus trap, Escape, the inert page and the top layer are the platform's. The box is the command palette's recipe (--surface-elevated, --border, --radius-block, --shadow-popover, src/palette.css:37), and no registry item ships it. It replaces nothing: the web interface had no dialog before it (docs/system/decisions.md, "A task over the page").

Parts

  • The title bar: the title, an <h2> that is the dialog's accessible name, and the close key, an IconButton.
  • The body: the caller's children, in a box that scrolls by itself.
  • The footer: the caller's Buttons, drawn only when footer is passed.
  • TabPanels (src/ui/Tab.tsx, documented in tab.md) is the layer's composition for a dialog with pages.

Examples

<Dialog open={open()} title="Rename Layout" size="sm" onClose={() => setOpen(false)} footer={…}>…</Dialog> — one field and its two actions (docs/system/examples/dialog/default.tsx).

Real uses, 6 call sites (rg -c "<Dialog" src → src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:1, src/components/JewelryDialog.tsx:2, src/components/LayerManager.tsx:1):

  • src/components/JewelryDialog.tsx — the Ring and Gem dialogs (Draw ▸ Ring, Draw ▸ Gem and the tool strip's keys): a form of the piece's numbers, a read-out of what the engine says about them, Cancel and OK in the footer; a refusal from the engine stays in the dialog beside the field it names. Added 2026-11-12.
  • src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:237 — Drafting Settings (size="md"): three pages on TabPanels, Cancel and OK in the footer, dismissOnBackdrop true only while the form is untouched, describedBy naming the line that says what OK did when the engine refused a value. The component is exported and not mounted yet: the shell's lines are in the coordinator's hands.
  • The command palette (src/components/CommandPalette.tsx) stays a native <dialog> of its own: it has no title bar, no dimmed page and no footer, it hangs from the title bar instead of standing in the middle, and it keeps the keyboard in one field (docs/system/decisions.md, "A task over the page").

Example: A dialog with one field and its two actions; the caller holds open. (docs/system/examples/dialog/default.tsx)

import { createSignal } from "solid-js";
import { Button } from "../../../../src/ui/Button";
import { Dialog } from "../../../../src/ui/Dialog";
import { Field } from "../../../../src/ui/Field";

export default function Default() {
  const [open, setOpen] = createSignal(false);
  const [name, setName] = createSignal("Layout1");
  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Rename layout</Button>
      <Dialog
        open={open()}
        title="Rename Layout"
        size="sm"
        onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
        footer={
          <>
            <Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button>
            <Button variant="primary" type="submit" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
              Rename
            </Button>
          </>
        }
      >
        <Field ariaLabel="Layout name" value={name()} onInput={setName} selectOnFocus />
      </Dialog>
    </>
  );
}

Example: Drafting Settings: pages on TabPanels, a refused value said beside its field, OK as the form's submit. (docs/system/examples/dialog/in-drafting-settings.tsx)

import { createSignal } from "solid-js";
import { Button } from "../../../../src/ui/Button";
import { Checkbox } from "../../../../src/ui/Checkbox";
import { Dialog } from "../../../../src/ui/Dialog";
import { Field } from "../../../../src/ui/Field";
import { TabPanels } from "../../../../src/ui/Tab";

export default function InDraftingSettings() {
  const [tab, setTab] = createSignal("snap-grid");
  const [spacing, setSpacing] = createSignal("0");
  const refused = (): boolean => !(Number(spacing()) > 0);
  return (
    <Dialog
      open
      title="Drafting Settings"
      dismissOnBackdrop={spacing() === "0.5"}
      onClose={() => undefined}
      footer={
        <>
          <Button>Cancel</Button>
          <Button variant="primary" type="submit">
            OK
          </Button>
        </>
      }
    >
      <TabPanels
        ariaLabel="Drafting settings"
        selected={tab()}
        onChange={setTab}
        panels={[
          {
            id: "snap-grid",
            label: "Snap and Grid",
            content: () => (
              <div>
                <Checkbox checked onChange={() => undefined}>
                  Snap on
                </Checkbox>
                <p>
                  <label for="example-snap-x">Snap X spacing</label>{" "}
                  <Field id="example-snap-x" align="end" inputMode="decimal" value={spacing()} invalid={refused()} describedBy={refused() ? "example-snap-x-error" : undefined} onInput={setSpacing} />
                </p>
                {refused() ? <p id="example-snap-x-error">Snap spacing must be more than 0.</p> : null}
              </div>
            ),
          },
          { id: "polar", label: "Polar Tracking", content: () => <Checkbox checked onChange={() => undefined}>Polar tracking on</Checkbox> },
          { id: "osnap", label: "Object Snap", content: () => <Checkbox checked onChange={() => undefined}>Object snap on</Checkbox> },
        ]}
      />
    </Dialog>
  );
}

Variants

size

  • sm: a question or one field; 52ch, measured 364px at 13px type. Used at 0 call sites.
  • md: a form in one column; the default; 76ch (the command palette's measure), measured 533px. Used at 1 call site (Drafting Settings).
  • lg: a form with a table or two columns; 104ch, measured 729px. Used at 0 call sites.

Every size is capped to the window less 16px on each side, and to the dynamic viewport's height less the same; at 560px wide and under, every size is the bottom sheet (States).

Example: An open dialog: the page behind is dimmed and inert, and the first field has the focus. (docs/system/examples/dialog/open.tsx)

import { Button } from "../../../../src/ui/Button";
import { Dialog } from "../../../../src/ui/Dialog";
import { Field } from "../../../../src/ui/Field";

export default function Open() {
  return (
    <Dialog
      open
      title="Rename Layout"
      size="sm"
      onClose={() => undefined}
      footer={
        <>
          <Button>Cancel</Button>
          <Button variant="primary" type="submit">
            Rename

        </>
      }
    >
      <Field ariaLabel="Layout name" value="Layout1" onInput={() => undefined} />
