State precedence

  • Open and Closed: Not applicable: the caller's open is one or the other.
  • Open and Scrolling: both show. A dialog taller than the window is an open dialog whose body scrolls.
  • Open and Sheet: both show. The sheet is the open dialog's shape in a narrow window.
  • Sheet and Scrolling: both show. The sheet stops a tab strip's height (35px) under the window's top and its body scrolls.
  • Focused (the box) and Open: both show. The ring is drawn on the open box until the focus moves into it.
  • Backdrop held and Open: both show. Escape and the close key still ask to close.

Motion

Not applicable: no motion — the dialog arrives and leaves at once (docs/system/decisions.md, "A task over the page"); its close key and the caller's controls carry their own.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
onClose(reason: DialogCloseReason) => voidThe dialog asks to be closed, and says why.
openbooleanWhether the dialog is showing.
titlestringThe title bar's text and the dialog's accessible name.
children?ElementThe body: it scrolls when it is taller than the window allows, under a title bar and a footer that stay.
describedBy?stringThe id of a line inside the dialog that says what it is for (several, space-separated): sets aria-describedby.
dismissOnBackdrop?booleanWhether a press outside the box asks to close.
footer?Element | ((done: () => void) => Element)The actions, drawn in a bar under the body: the layer's Buttons, the primary one type="submit".
initialFocus?DialogInitialFocusWhere the focus goes on opening.
size?DialogSizeThe box's width.
  • open: whether the dialog is showing; the caller holds it.
  • onClose: the dialog asks to be closed, with the reason: escape, backdrop, close or action. The dialog never closes by itself.
  • title: the title bar's text and the accessible name.
  • size: sm, md or lg; defaults to md.
  • describedBy: the id of a line inside the dialog that says what it is for (several, space-separated); sets aria-describedby. The layer's name for this tie on every component (docs/system/decisions.md, "Prop vocabulary").
  • initialFocus: a selector inside the dialog, an element, or a function returning one. Defaults to the first field of the body that is showing; never the close key.
  • footer: the actions, or a function handed done, which asks to close with the reason action.
  • dismissOnBackdrop: whether a press outside asks to close; defaults to true.
  • children: the body.

Usage

When to use

  • A command needs several values before it can run, and the page must wait for them: drafting settings, drawing units, a rename.
  • A question must be answered before work goes on: discard the changes, delete the layout.

When not to use

  • The list is of commands to run or values to pick, and it closes on the pick. Use Row in a menu or a listbox instead.
  • One value is edited where it stands, in a panel beside the drawing. Use Field or Select with variant="inline" instead.
  • A control needs one line of explanation. Use Tooltip instead.
  • A setting is switched on or off in place. Use Toggle instead.

Rules

  • rule/dialog-mounted-open: When a surface has a dialog, render Dialog once and pass open, rather than mounting it by a condition, because the focus goes back to its opener only while the element outlives its 1 closing, and the caller's answer to onClose is read from the same instance. Evidence: single use src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:237. Check: lint trap/overlay-conditional-render.
  • Don't: {open() && <Dialog open title="Drawing Units" onClose={close} />}
  • Do: <Dialog open={open()} title="Drawing Units" onClose={close} />
  • rule/dialog-close-answered: When onClose runs, set the caller's open to false in it, or leave it true on purpose, because the dialog closes 0 times by itself: Escape, the close key and a press outside only ask, and an unanswered ask leaves it open. Evidence: single use src/ui/Dialog.tsx:122, the one function every way of closing goes through. Check: test src/ui/Dialog.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Dialog open={open()} title="Drawing Units" onClose={() => undefined} />
  • Do: <Dialog open={open()} title="Drawing Units" onClose={() => setOpen(false)} />
  • rule/dialog-primary-submit: When a footer has a primary action, make it 1 Button with type="submit" and run the action from its onClick, because Enter in a single-line field presses the form's first submit button and no other, and a second submit button is never reached by the key. Evidence: single use src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:247. Check: test src/ui/Dialog.test.tsx.
  • Don't: footer={<Button variant="primary" onClick={save}>Save</Button>}
  • Do: footer={<Button variant="primary" type="submit" onClick={save}>Save</Button>}
  • rule/dialog-initial-focus: When typing should start somewhere other than the body's first field, pass initialFocus with that control's selector, because the default is the first of the 3 field kinds (input, select, textarea) that is showing, and the close key is never a starting point: a dialog whose first Enter closes it has lost the task. Evidence: single use src/ui/Dialog.tsx:95. Check: test src/ui/Dialog.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Dialog open title="Find"><Checkbox>Match case</Checkbox><Field ariaLabel="Find what" /></Dialog>
  • Do: <Dialog open title="Find" initialFocus="[aria-label='Find what']"><Checkbox>Match case</Checkbox><Field ariaLabel="Find what" /></Dialog>
  • rule/dialog-backdrop-work: When closing would throw away what was typed, pass dismissOnBackdrop as false, or as a value that is false once the form is touched, because 1 press outside the box is a slip of the hand as often as a decision, and Escape and Cancel remain for the decision. Evidence: single use src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:242. Check: test src/ui/Dialog.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Dialog open title="Drafting Settings" onClose={close}> around a form with typed values.
  • Do: <Dialog open title="Drafting Settings" dismissOnBackdrop={untouched()} onClose={close}>
  • rule/dialog-refusal-beside-field: When an action cannot take a value, keep the dialog open, mark the field invalid, tie 1 line of words to it with describedBy and move the focus to it, because a dialog that closes on a refused value reports nothing and one that only colours the field tells a screen reader nothing. Evidence: single use src/drafting-edit.ts:89. Check: review src/drafting-edit.ts.
  • Don't: onClick={() => { facade.execute("setvar", { name: "POLARANG", value }); close(); }}
  • Do: onClick={() => { const refused = runCalls(facade, plan.calls); if (Object.keys(refused).length === 0) close(); else mark(refused); }}

Content

  • rule/dialog-title-names-task: When a title is written, use the menu item that opens the dialog less its ellipsis, in 1 to 4 words, because the row "Drafting Settings..." promised a dialog of that name and the title is what a screen reader says on opening. Evidence: single use src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:239. Check: review src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx.
  • Don't: <Dialog title="Please configure your drafting options">
  • Do: <Dialog title="Drafting Settings">
  • rule/dialog-action-labels: When a footer's 2 actions are written, label the one that changes nothing "Cancel" and put the primary action last, named by its verb where the dialog does 1 thing (Rename, Delete) and "OK" where it applies a form of several settings, because one verb cannot name several settings and "OK" beside "Cancel" is the pair a drafter already reads without reading. Evidence: single use src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:246. Check: review src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx.
  • Don't: footer={<><Button variant="primary" type="submit">Yes</Button><Button>No</Button></>}
  • Do: footer={<><Button>Cancel</Button><Button variant="primary" type="submit">OK</Button></>}

Anti-slop

  • rule/dialog-canonical-element: When a surface needs a modal, render Dialog rather than a <div role="dialog"> with a hand-built focus trap, or a raw <dialog> with its own box, because showModal() gives the trap, Escape, the inert page and the top layer the same way in the 3 system webviews the desktop app runs in, and a hand-built one has to re-earn each. Evidence: single use src/ui/Dialog.tsx:103. Check: review src/ui/Dialog.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="modal" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" onKeyDown={trapFocus}>
  • Do: <Dialog open={open()} title="Drawing Units" onClose={close}>
  • rule/dialog-no-page-landmarks: When content is put in a dialog, use plain boxes rather than <header>, <footer> or <main>, because inside a dialog those 3 elements are announced as the page's own landmarks. Evidence: measured in the browser's accessibility tree, 2026-11-11: a <header> in the dialog read as banner, src/ui/Dialog.tsx:176. Check: test src/ui/Dialog.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Dialog open title="Units"><header>Length</header></Dialog>
  • Do: <Dialog open title="Units"><SectionLabel>Length</SectionLabel></Dialog>

Limits

  • Follows rule/button-row-limit.
  • rule/dialog-size-by-content: When a dialog holds 1 column of fields, use md (or sm for a question or a single field) and keep lg for 2 columns or a table, because a column of labels and values stretched to lg leaves each label 500px from its value. Evidence: measured 364px, 533px and 729px boxes for sm, md and lg at 1280px, src/ui/ui.css:1309. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: <Dialog size="lg" title="Rename Layout"><Field ariaLabel="Layout name" /></Dialog>
  • Do: <Dialog size="sm" title="Rename Layout"><Field ariaLabel="Layout name" /></Dialog>
  • rule/dialog-narrow-one-column: When a dialog's body is laid out, let it fall to 1 column at 358px, because at a window of 560px or less the dialog is a sheet as wide as the window and its body is the window less 16px on each side. Evidence: measured 390px sheet with a 358px body at 390 by 700, src/ui/ui.css:1421. Check: review src/dialogs.css.
  • Don't: .my-form { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 240px 240px }
  • Do: .my-form { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(24ch, 1fr)) }

Accessibility

Rests on the native <dialog> element shown with showModal(): the dialog role, the modal state, the focus trap, the inert page and Escape's close request come from the platform. The body and the footer are one <form>, so Enter's press of the primary action is the platform's implicit submission.

Related

  • Button: the footer's actions; the primary one is type="submit".
  • IconButton: the close key; and, with popup="dialog", a key that opens a small popover of fields beside itself, which is not this component.
  • Tab: TabPanels gives a dialog its pages.
  • Field, Select, Checkbox, TextArea: what a dialog's body is made of; each is tied to its visible label by id, or named by ariaLabel.
  • Row: when the task is picking one command or value from a list.
  • Tooltip: the hint a control inside a dialog shows is drawn inside the dialog, because the top layer covers the page.

Field

Description

It takes one line of text and hands every keystroke back to the caller, who owns the value.

import { Field } from "../../../../src/ui/Field";, source src/ui/Field.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/native-control, trap/control-height, trap/field-label, trap/field-input-type, trap/touch-input-zoom, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/disabled-still-hovers.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the 24px height, the hairline stroke and the focus border are measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (docs/system/decisions.md), and no registry item ships it.

  • src/components/InlineAsk.tsx — the line over the drawing that asks the assistant (Ctrl+K): variant="bare" in the box the surface draws (the palette's box), the assistant's mark as its start adornment, the chat's own draft as its value, Enter and Escape on onKeyDown. Added 2026-11-12.
  • src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:87 — the dialog's typed numbers (align="end", inputMode="decimal", selectOnFocus), each named by a visible <label for> through id, marked invalid with its refusal tied by describedBy.
  • src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:179 — the dialog's additional angles, a list typed in one field under its label, with a line of help tied by describedBy.
  • src/components/AssistantPane.tsx — the setup sheet's Base URL, API key and Model. The API key carries the show and hide key as its end adornment (<IconButton size="sm">): until 2026-11-12 a wrapper of the sheet's own placed that key over the field on a patch of the field's fill, and the last characters of a long key, and the caret after them, lay under the patch.
  • src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx — the palette's typed values: variant="inline" size="sm" align="end", mixed for *VARIES*, invalid while a value is refused, committing on Enter and on leaving the field.
  • src/components/CommandField.tsx — the command line's typed line: variant="bare" inside the panel's own strip, which draws the edge and the focus and sets the mono face; the prompt mark is the start adornment. The field takes no value: the history writes the element's own through ref, so nothing is assigned back during an input method's composition. Moved on 2026-11-12 from a hand-drawn <input class="cmd-input">.
  • src/components/CommandPalette.tsx — the search field: variant="bare" in the palette's header, role="combobox" with expanded, controls, activeDescendant and autocompleteKind="list", autocapitalize="off", the lens as its start adornment. Moved on 2026-11-12 from a hand-drawn <input class="palette-input">.

Example: The typed line: a bare field in a strip, the prompt mark in the start. (docs/system/examples/field/in-command-line.tsx)

import { createSignal } from "solid-js";
import { Field } from "../../../../src/ui/Field";

export default function InCommandLine() {
  const [focused, setFocused] = createSignal(false);
  const [sent, setSent] = createSignal<string[]>([]);
  let input: HTMLInputElement | undefined;
  return (
    <section class="cmdline" aria-label="Command line">
      <div class="cmd-output" role="log" aria-label="Command history">
        {sent().map((line) => (
          <div class="cmd-line">{line}</div>
        ))}
      </div>
      <div class="cmd-entry">
        <div class="cmd-field" classList={{ "is-focused": focused() }}>
          <Field
            variant="bare"
            ref={(el) => {
              input = el;
            }}
            ariaLabel="Command line"
            placeholder="Command:"
            spellcheck={false}
            autocomplete="off"
            onFocus={() => setFocused(true)}
            onBlur={() => setFocused(false)}
            onKeyDown={(event) => {
              if (event.key !== "Enter" || input === undefined) return;
              event.preventDefault();
              setSent([...sent(), input.value]);
              input.value = "";
            }}
            start={
              <span class="cmd-caret" aria-hidden="true">
                ›
              </span>
            }
          />
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}

Example: A value row of the properties palette: commits on Enter and on leaving, Escape restores. (docs/system/examples/field/in-properties-panel.tsx)

import { createSignal } from "solid-js";
import { Field } from "../../../../src/ui/Field";

export default function InPropertiesPanel() {
  const [radius, setRadius] = createSignal("12.5");
  const [draft, setDraft] = createSignal(radius());
  const [refused, setRefused] = createSignal(false);
  const commit = (leaving: boolean): void => {
    if (Number.isFinite(Number(draft())) && draft().trim() !== "") {
      setRadius(draft());
      setRefused(false);
    } else if (leaving) {
      setDraft(radius());
      setRefused(false);
    } else {
      setRefused(true);
    }
  };
  return (
    <div class="prop-row" role="listitem">
      <span class="prop-label">Radius</span>
      <span class="prop-value">
        <span class="prop-field">
          <Field
            variant="inline"
            size="sm"
            align="end"
            value={draft()}
            ariaLabel="Radius"
            inputMode="decimal"
            spellcheck={false}
            autocomplete="off"
            selectOnFocus
            invalid={refused()}
            onInput={(value) => {
              setRefused(false);
              setDraft(value);
            }}
            onKeyDown={(event) => {
              if (event.key === "Enter") {
                event.preventDefault();
                commit(false);
              } else if (event.key === "Escape" && (draft() !== radius() || refused())) {
                event.preventDefault();
                event.stopPropagation();
                setDraft(radius());
                setRefused(false);
              }
            }}
            onBlur={() => commit(true)}
          />
        </span>
      </span>
    </div>
  );
}

  • text: the default single-line field. Used at 7 call sites, and at the eighth while the API key is shown.

  • search: adds the search keyboard and a clear affordance. Used at 0 call sites.
  • password: masks the value. Used at 1 call site (the setup sheet's API key, until its show key is pressed).

variant

  • field: the default; the form control, stroked and filled at rest. The stroke is an ink of the field's own (--ui-field-edge): the hairline stroke (--border-soft) on the dark surfaces, where it measures 1.34 against the pane and 1.24 against the field's fill, and the default stroke (--border) on the light ones, 1.39 and 1.28. With the hairline stroke the light field measured 1.27 and 1.18 and read as a grey slab with no edge (#F3F3F3 on #FCFCFC). The theme sets the ink, never border-color, so the inline, focused and refused strokes still win; Select reads the same ink. Used at 3 call sites (the provider form).
  • inline: a value in a dense list row; no stroke and no fill until the pointer or the keyboard is on it, as Select variant="inline". Used at 1 call site (the properties palette's value rows).
  • bare: the one line inside a box a surface draws itself; no stroke, no fill, no inset and no ring, in the surface's own face and size, as TextArea variant="bare". The surface shows the focus. It keeps the control's 24px height and the layer's 16px line, so the value is centred wherever the surface puts it. Used at 2 call sites (the command line's strip, the command palette's header).

size

  • md: the default 24px box. Used at 7 call sites.
  • sm: the 20px box that fits a 22px list row, on the row's 4px inset; 24px under a coarse pointer, as Select size="sm". Used at 1 call site (the properties palette).

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestThe field is empty or holds a value.Type, select, paste, Tab away.The value at the full ink; the placeholder at the faint ink.test
HoverThe pointer is over the field, on a device with a hover pointer.Click to place the caret.Nothing beyond the text cursor: the stroke stays at the hairline.by hand
FocusedThe field takes focus by click or Tab.Type; Tab away.The stroke takes the focus ink and the 1px ring draws in it at offset -1.by hand
FilledThe value is not empty.Edit it.The value at the full ink; the placeholder is gone.test
InvalidThe caller passes invalid: it refuses the value.Correct the value; the caller clears invalid when it accepts it.aria-invalid="true", and the caller's error line, tied to the input by describedBy; the stroke takes the error ink.test
DisabledThe caller passes disabled.Nothing: no typing, no focus.The value at the disabled ink; no focus ring.test
MixedThe caller passes mixed: the field stands for several things whose values differ.Type a value, which replaces them all.The stand-in the caller passes as the value ("*VARIES*") in the quiet ink.test
Read-onlyThe caller passes readOnly.Focus it, select and copy; no typing.The value at the full ink with no caret; it stays a Tab stop.test
AdornedThe caller passes start or end.Type as in any field; press a control in the adornment, or Tab to it after the input. A press on a glyph lands on the input.The adornment inside the box's end, and the value ending before it: the input's padding on that side is the adornment's measured width.test

Example: A locked field at the disabled ink. (docs/system/examples/field/disabled.tsx)

import { Field } from "../../../../src/ui/Field";

export default function Disabled() {
  return <Field value="0,0" ariaLabel="Base point" disabled />;
}

Example: A refused address at the error stroke, with the line that says why. (docs/system/examples/field/invalid.tsx)

import { Field } from "../../../../src/ui/Field";

export default function Invalid() {
  return (
    <div>
      <Field value="127.0.0.1:11434" ariaLabel="Base URL" invalid describedBy="base-url-error" autocomplete="off" spellcheck={false} />
      <span id="base-url-error">Start the address with http:// or https://</span>
    </div>

}

Example: A key field with its show and hide key inside the end. (docs/system/examples/field/adornment-end.tsx)

import { createSignal } from "solid-js";
import { Field } from "../../../../src/ui/Field";
import { IconButton } from "../../../../src/ui/IconButton";

export default function AdornmentEnd() {
  const [key, setKey] = createSignal("sk-0000");
  const [shown, setShown] = createSignal(false);
  return (
    <div>
      <Field
        type={shown() ? "text" : "password"}
        value={key()}
        ariaLabel="API key"
        autocomplete="off"
        spellcheck={false}
        describedBy="key-help"
        onInput={setKey}
        end={<IconButton icon={shown() ? "eye" : "eye-off"} size="sm" title={shown() ? "Hide the key" : "Show the key"} onClick={() => setShown(!shown())} />}
      />
      <span id="key-help">Stored in this browser, not encrypted.</span>
    </div>
  );
}

Example: A search field with its lens inside the start. (docs/system/examples/field/adornment-start.tsx)

import { createSignal } from "solid-js";
import { ToolIcon } from "../../../../src/icons";
import { Field } from "../../../../src/ui/Field";

export default function AdornmentStart() {
  const [query, setQuery] = createSignal("");
  // The lens is a glyph, hidden from assistive tech by `ToolIcon`: a press on it lands on the input.
  return <Field type="search" value={query()} ariaLabel="Search layers" placeholder="Walls" spellcheck={false} onInput={setQuery} start={<ToolIcon id="search" />} />;
}

Example: A value several objects disagree on, in the quiet ink. (docs/system/examples/field/mixed.tsx)

import { Field } from "../../../../src/ui/Field";

export default function Mixed() {
  return <Field mixed variant="inline" size="sm" align="end" value="*VARIES*" ariaLabel="Radius" onInput={() => undefined} />;
}

Example: A value to select and copy, not to change. (docs/system/examples/field/read-only.tsx)

import { Field } from "../../../../src/ui/Field";

export default function ReadOnly() {
  return <Field readOnly value="6F2A-11C0" ariaLabel="Handle" />;
}

State precedence

  • Focused and Hover: Focused wins. The accent stroke and the ring stay while the pointer is over the field.
  • Filled and Focused: both show. The accent stroke and ring draw over the filled value.
  • Disabled and Hover: Disabled wins. A disabled field takes no hover and no ring.
  • Disabled and Filled: Disabled wins. The value stays visible at the disabled ink.
  • Invalid and Focused: both show. The stroke keeps the error ink and the ring draws in the focus ink one line inside it.
  • Invalid and Filled: both show. The refused value stays at the full ink inside the error stroke.
  • Invalid and Hover: Invalid wins. The stroke keeps the error ink under the pointer.
  • Mixed and Focused: both show. The stand-in stays quiet until the first keystroke, when the caller clears mixed.
  • Mixed and Invalid: Invalid wins. A typed value the caller refuses is no longer the stand-in, so the caller clears mixed with the first keystroke.
  • Read-only and Focused: both show. The ring draws; the value does not change.
  • Read-only and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled field takes no focus at all.
  • Invalid and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled field cannot be corrected, so the caller clears invalid before it locks the field.
  • Adorned and Focused: both show. The stroke and the ring are the input's, and the input is the whole box, so they go around the adornment; a control in the adornment draws its own ring while it has the focus, and the box draws none then.
  • Adorned and Invalid: both show. The error stroke goes around the adornment.
  • Adorned and Disabled: Disabled wins for a glyph, which takes the disabled ink. A control in the adornment is the caller's to disable.
  • Adorned and Filled: both show. A value longer than the room between the adornments ends in an ellipsis at rest and scrolls under the caret while edited; it never runs under an adornment.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
Focus arrives or leaves; the pointer enters or leaves an inline fieldinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)border-color, background-colorThe stroke changes at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose

ariaLabel?stringThe accessible name when no visible <label> is tied to the input.
autocapitalize?"none" | "off" | "sentences" | "words" | "characters"The native autocapitalize: off for a command, a code or a name a phone's keyboard must not capitalise.
autocomplete?stringThe native autofill hint: off for a value no form should remember (an API key), or a token the platform knows (email, url, current-password).
autocompleteKind?AutocompleteKindA combobox: what its list does with the typed text (aria-autocomplete).

describedBy?stringThe id of the help line or the error line under the field (several, space-separated): sets aria-describedby.

id?stringThe input's id, for a visible <label for> beside it: the label is then the name, and no ariaLabel is passed.

invalid?booleanThe value is refused: sets aria-invalid and the error stroke.
maxLength?numberThe most characters the field takes.

onFocus?((event: FocusEvent) => void)Focus arrived.
onInput?((value: string) => void)Runs on every keystroke with the new value.
onKeyDown?((event: KeyboardEvent) => void)A key went down in the field, outside an input method's composition.

readOnly?booleanThe value can be selected and copied, not changed.

role?"combobox"The field drives a list of matches and keeps the keyboard: combobox.
selectOnFocus?booleanSelect the whole value when focus arrives, by key or by click, so typing replaces it.
size?FieldSizeThe box size.
spellcheck?booleanWhether the platform's spelling checker runs.
start?ElementAn adornment inside the field's leading end: a glyph that says what the value is.

variant?FieldVariantThe look.
  • value: the current value; the caller holds it and passes the new one back.
  • onInput: runs on every keystroke with the new value.
  • placeholder: the hint; never the only name.
  • ariaLabel: the accessible name when no visible label is tied to the input.
  • id: the input's id, for a visible <label for> beside it; the label is then the name and no ariaLabel is passed.
  • type: the native input type; defaults to text.
  • disabled: blocks typing and drops the ink to the disabled step.
  • title: the hint (a value the box cuts short shows in full above it, whether or not there is a title, except a password's), shown in the layer's hint box (after 0.4s under a mouse or a pen, at once when a key moves focus in, away at the first keystroke) and added to the field's accessible description after describedBy. It is never the name (pass ariaLabel), and no native title attribute is rendered. Used at 0 call sites; a line of help under the field, tied by describedBy, is the usual pick because it stays on the page.
  • autoFocus: focuses the field when it mounts.
  • autocomplete: the native autofill hint; off for a value no form should remember, or a token the platform knows (email, url, current-password). Unset leaves it to the platform.
  • spellcheck: switches the platform's spelling checker. Unset leaves it to the platform, except type="password", which is never checked.
  • invalid: the value is refused; sets aria-invalid="true" and the error stroke.
  • describedBy: the id of the help line or the error line under the field (several, space-separated); sets aria-describedby.
  • variant: field, inline or bare; defaults to field.
  • size: sm or md; defaults to md.
  • align: start or end; defaults to start.
  • mixed: the value is a stand-in for several that differ; it reads in the quiet ink.
  • readOnly: the value can be selected and copied, not changed; the field stays a Tab stop.
  • maxLength: the most characters the field takes.
  • inputMode: the keyboard a phone shows where type does not say: decimal, numeric, tel, search, email, url, text or none.
  • selectOnFocus: selects the whole value when focus arrives, by key or by click, so typing replaces it; the second click places the caret.
  • onKeyDown: a key went down, outside an input method's composition; the caller may preventDefault it.
  • onFocus: focus arrived.
  • onBlur: focus left.
  • ref: hands the <input> to the caller.
  • role: combobox, on a field that drives a list of matches and keeps the keyboard.
  • expanded: a combobox's list is showing (aria-expanded).
  • controls: the id of a combobox's list (aria-controls).
  • activeDescendant: the id of the option the arrow keys are on (aria-activedescendant); unset when none is.
  • autocompleteKind: what the list does with the typed text (aria-autocomplete): list, inline, both or none.
  • autocapitalize: the native attribute, passed through; off for a command, a code or a name a phone's keyboard must not capitalise. Unset leaves it to the platform. Used at 1 call site (the command palette).
  • start: an adornment inside the field's leading end, before the input in the box: a glyph that says what the value is. Used at 2 call sites (the command line's prompt mark, the palette's lens).
  • end: an adornment inside the field's trailing end, after the input in the box and in the Tab order: a glyph, or one <IconButton size="sm"> that acts on the value. Used at 1 call site (the API key's show and hide key).

Usage

When to use

  • The user types or edits 1 line of text: a name, a coordinate, a keyword.
  • The value is owned by a surface above the field, which needs every keystroke.

When not to use

  • The value is picked from a set rather than typed. Use Select instead.
  • The text runs to more than 1 line. Use TextArea instead.
  • The control is an action rather than a value. Use Button instead.
  • The text is a fact to read. Use Chip instead.

Rules

  • rule/field-label-bound: When a field is rendered without a visible <label>, pass ariaLabel, because a placeholder disappears as soon as the user types and the field is left nameless. Evidence: app 3/3 single-line inputs are named by their row, rg -c "assistant-input|cmd-input|prop-input" src. Check: test src/ui/Field.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Field placeholder="Layer name" /> alone in a row.
  • Do: <Field ariaLabel="Layer name" placeholder="Layer name" />
  • rule/field-type-native: When a field takes an email, a search term or a password, pass type so the native keyboard and autofill follow, because type="text" on an email field shows the wrong phone keyboard and blocks autofill. Evidence: app 4/4 types defined in src/ui/Field.tsx. Check: test src/ui/Field.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Field type="text" ariaLabel="Email" />
  • Do: <Field type="email" ariaLabel="Email" />
  • rule/field-described-by: When a line of help or an error sits under a field, give the line an id and pass it as describedBy, and pass invalid while the value is refused, because a line that only sits near the input is read 0 times by a screen reader that lands on the input by Tab. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:867, the API key's "Stored in this browser" line, untied today. Check: test src/ui/Field.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Field ariaLabel="API key" /><span class="hint">Stored in this browser, not encrypted.</span>
  • Do: <Field ariaLabel="API key" describedBy="key-help" /><span id="key-help">Stored in this browser, not encrypted.</span>
  • rule/field-secret-not-remembered: When a field holds a key, a token or a password, pass autocomplete="off" and spellcheck={false} for every type it takes, because a secret shown with type="text" is 1 ordinary text value to the platform, which offers it to autofill and sends it to the spelling checker. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:781, the API key field, which sets autocomplete from outside through a wrapper ref. Check: test src/ui/Field.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Field type={shown() ? "text" : "password"} ariaLabel="API key" />
  • Do: <Field type={shown() ? "text" : "password"} ariaLabel="API key" autocomplete="off" spellcheck={false} />
  • rule/field-inline-in-row: When a typed value sits in a dense list row beside its label, pass variant="inline" size="sm", and align="end" when the rows form a column of values, because a stroked 24px field in each of 8 rows of 22px draws 8 boxes where the row should read as text, and pushes every row 2px taller. Evidence: measured 20px box at 1px from the top of a 22px row, the same box the palette's hand-drawn input measured, in the browser 2026-11-11, docs/system/decisions.md. Check: test src/ui/Field.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Field value={radius} ariaLabel="Radius" /> in a 22px property row.
  • Do: <Field variant="inline" size="sm" align="end" value={radius} ariaLabel="Radius" />
  • rule/field-commit-in-caller: When a value is applied on Enter and on leaving the field rather than on every keystroke, keep the draft in the caller and commit from onKeyDown and onBlur, and restore the old value on Escape, because the field reports 1 event per keystroke and a value applied on each would move the drawing while "12.5" is still "1". Evidence: measured 2 onInput calls for the 2 keystrokes of "12", src/ui/Field.test.tsx. Check: test src/ui/Field.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Field value={radius} onInput={(value) => setRadius(Number(value))} />
  • Do: <Field value={draft} onInput={setDraft} onKeyDown={(e) => e.key === "Enter" && commit()} onBlur={commit} />
  • rule/field-combobox-complete: When a field drives a list of matches, pass role="combobox" with expanded, controls and activeDescendant together, and none of them on any other field, because a combobox with 0 of the three is announced as one and then leads nowhere, and aria-activedescendant on a plain text field is ignored. Evidence: app 5/5 combobox props defined together in src/ui/Field.tsx. Check: test src/ui/Field.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Field ariaLabel="Search commands" role="combobox" />
  • Do: <Field ariaLabel="Search commands" role="combobox" expanded={open} controls="palette-list" activeDescendant={activeId} autocompleteKind="list" />
  • rule/field-adornment-slot: When a glyph or a key belongs inside a field's end, pass it as start or end, so the field holds it, because the input makes room only for an adornment it holds: placed over the field from a wrapper, the show key covered the last 3 characters of a 203-character key and the caret after them. Evidence: measured 24px of end padding on the adopted key field against 6px under the wrapper's patch, the eye at the same 1237, 240 before and after, in the browser 2026-11-12 (the captures wE14-setup-longkey-before and wE14-setup-longkey-after), docs/system/decisions.md. Check: test src/ui/Field.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="key-box"><Field ariaLabel="API key" /><span class="key-end"><IconButton icon="eye" size="sm" title="Show the key" /></span></div>
  • Do: <Field ariaLabel="API key" end={<IconButton icon="eye" size="sm" title="Show the key" onClick={toggle} />} />
  • rule/field-adornment-one-control: When an adornment acts on the value, make it 1 IconButton size="sm" with a name of its own, and keep a glyph that only decorates hidden from assistive tech, because the box is a <span> with no role: a screen reader meets the text field and then whatever stands in the slot, and 2 controls in a 24px end leave no room for the value. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:1071, the API key's show and hide key, named "Show the key" and "Hide the key". Check: test src/ui/Field.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Field ariaLabel="API key" end={<span onClick={toggle}>show</span>} />
  • Do: <Field ariaLabel="API key" end={<IconButton icon="eye" size="sm" title="Show the key" onClick={toggle} />} />
  • rule/field-bare-surface-focus: When a field is bare, draw the focus on the surface around it and give that surface the edge and the fill, because the bare field draws 0 rings and 0 strokes: with nothing around it a keyboard user cannot see where the caret is. Evidence: app 2/2 bare fields sit in a surface that shows the focus (the command line's strip takes the ring through is-focused, and the palette's field never loses the focus while its dialog is open), src/styles.css, src/palette.css. Check: review src/styles.css.
  • Don't: <Field variant="bare" ariaLabel="Command line" /> alone on a pane.
  • Do: <div class="cmd-field" classList={{ "is-focused": focused() }}><Field variant="bare" ariaLabel="Command line" onFocus={() => setFocused(true)} onBlur={() => setFocused(false)} /></div>

Content

  • rule/field-placeholder-example: When a placeholder is written, show a real example value rather than an instruction (0,0 — not "Enter a point"), because the placeholder is read as the value's shape, and the instruction belongs in a label. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:741, the provider popover's Base URL placeholder. Check: review src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.
  • Don't: <Field placeholder="Type your point here" />
  • Do: <Field ariaLabel="Base point" placeholder="0,0" />

Anti-slop

  • rule/field-canonical-element: When a surface needs a single-line input, render Field rather than a raw <input> with its own class, because the replaced classes paint 3 different heights and borders by hand. Evidence: app 9/9 lines across src/styles.css, src/interaction.css and src/assistant.css, rg -c "assistant-input|cmd-input|prop-input" src. Check: review src/ui/Field.tsx.
  • Don't: <input class="prop-input" value={x} onInput={...} />
  • Do: <Field value={x} onInput={setX} ariaLabel="Name" />

Limits

  • rule/field-width-limit: When a field sits in a form row beside other controls, give it at least 96px or let it fill the row, because the measured palette input is 6px-padded inside a 260px sidebar and a narrower field clips a 4-character value like "0,0". Evidence: measured 6px padding and 260px sidebar, docs/system/decisions.md. Check: review src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: a 40px-wide field in the properties row.
  • Do: a field that fills the row's remaining width.

Accessibility

Rests on the native <input> element: typing, selection, IME and autofill come from the platform.

Related

  • TextArea: when the text runs to several lines.
  • Select: when the value is picked from a list rather than typed.
  • Chip: when the text is a fact rather than an editable value.
  • Row: when the value is picked from a list rather than typed.
  • Button: when the field's value is submitted.
  • Tooltip: the hint box a field's title shows in; never wrap a field in one.
  • Dialog: the surface that holds a form of several fields with its actions.

IconButton

Description

It runs one action drawn as a single glyph, and its title is both its accessible name and the hint a sighted person reads.

import { IconButton } from "../../../../src/ui/IconButton";, source src/ui/IconButton.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/button-div, trap/role-button, trap/native-control, trap/button-icon-name, trap/icon-optical-size, trap/icon-optical-align, trap/control-height, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/disabled-still-hovers, trap/touch-hover-flash, trap/hover-unguarded, trap/touch-tap-highlight.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the circle, the .08 hover fill and the 14px glyph are measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (docs/system/decisions.md), and the glyphs are the app's own src/icons.ts paths.

Examples

<IconButton icon="close" title="Close the panel" /> — the panel's close control.

Real uses, 36 call sites (rg -c "<IconButton" src → src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:18, src/components/BenchPanel.tsx:1, src/components/InlineAsk.tsx:1, src/components/LayerManager.tsx:1, src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:1, src/components/Menu.tsx:1, src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:1, src/components/ToolStrip.tsx:1, src/components/TopBar.tsx:3):

  • src/components/BenchPanel.tsx — the bench section's fold key (sm, expanded, controls), as the layers' and the properties' sections fold. Added 2026-11-12.

On a wider window a tool is the ghost Button with its glyph over its label.

Variants

variant

  • ghost: the transparent circle for a tool bar; the default. Used at 21 call sites (the assistant header's New chat and Close, the setup sheet's show-or-hide key beside the API key, the narrow window's Main menu key, the sidebar sections' fold and unfold (the layers and the properties), the title bar's sidebar and command-line keys, the changes row's show and hide, an attachment chip's remove, the selection chip's remove, the turn's copy, a tool's code copy, a reply's code copy, a failed request's Try again, a queued message's send and remove, the composer's attach, every tool in the tool strip, and the top bar's assistant key).
  • soft: the resting .08 fill, for a tool that is currently on. Used at 1 call site (the transcript's jump-to-latest key).
  • inverted: the ink-coloured circle with the accent-surface glyph, for the one primary action. Used at 2 call sites (the composer's stop and send).

size

  • sm: the 20px circle with the 12px glyph, for a chip row. Used at 14 call sites (the setup sheet's show-or-hide key beside the API key, the sidebar sections' fold and unfold (the layers and the properties), the changes row's show and hide, an attachment chip's remove, the selection chip's remove, the turn's copy, a tool's code copy, a reply's code copy, a failed request's Try again, and a queued message's send and remove).
  • md: the 24px circle with the 14px glyph, the composer's size. Used at 11 call sites (the assistant header's New chat and Close, the narrow window's Main menu key, the composer's attach, stop and send, the transcript's jump-to-latest key, every tool in the tool strip, and the title bar's sidebar, command-line and assistant keys).

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestNothing is over the circle.Click it, or Tab to it.The variant's resting fill, or none on ghost.by hand
HoverThe pointer is over the circle, on a device with a hover pointer.Click it.The fill steps up one rung; the cursor is a pointer.by hand
PressedThe pointer is held down.Release to run the action.The next fill rung up.by hand
FocusedKeyboard focus arrives by Tab.Enter or Space runs the action.The 1px ring in the focus ink at offset -1, following the circle; on inverted, the ring is the glyph's ink drawn 3px inside the edge.by hand
SelectedThe caller passes selected (a toggle).Click it again to turn the tool off.The .08 fill squared to the control radius (a resting key has no fill and a hovered one a round fill), the full ink, and aria-pressed="true".test
ExpandedThe caller passes expanded (a fold key), with controls naming the region.Click it to fold the region away; click again to bring it back.aria-expanded="true" while the region shows and "false" while it is folded, and aria-controls holding the region's id; the look is the variant's own.test
HintedA mouse or a pen rests on the circle for 0.4s (at once when another hint was up within the last 0.3s), or keyboard focus arrives. Never a finger.Read the name; a press, a click or Escape puts the box away, and it stays away until the pointer or the focus moves to another control.The layer's hint box holding the title, its shortcut as a key cap and the description on a second line, below the circle (above it at the window's foot), held inside the window's edges.test
DisabledThe caller's condition is false.Tab to it and read its hint: the name, and why it is blocked when the caller passes description. No click by pointer, Enter or Space, and no hover fill.The glyph drops to the disabled ink; the fill to the disabled step; aria-disabled="true".test

export default function Expanded() {
  return (

State precedence

  • Hover and Focused: Focused wins. The ring stays drawn while the pointer is over the circle; hover only steps the fill.
  • Hover and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled circle keeps its resting look under the pointer and takes no click.
  • Selected and Hover: both show. The squared .08 selected fill stays under the pointer; hover adds the pointer cursor and nothing to the fill.
  • Selected and Expanded: Not applicable: a key is a toggle or a fold key, never both; the caller passes one of the two props.
  • Expanded and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled fold key keeps aria-expanded and takes no click.
  • Selected and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled toggle drops to the disabled ink and takes no click.
  • Pressed and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn while the circle is held down.
  • Hinted and Pressed: Pressed wins. The press puts the hint away.
  • Hinted and Hover: both show. The hint follows the hover after its delay.
  • Hinted and Focused: both show. The hint arrives with the ring, with no delay.
  • Hinted and Selected: both show. The hint names a toggle whatever its state.
  • Hinted and Expanded: both show on a fold key, until the click that folds puts the hint away; on a key with popup, Expanded wins, and the hint stays away while the key's own menu or dialog is open.
  • Hinted and Disabled: both show. A disabled key still says what it is, and why it is blocked when it has a description.
  • Focused and Disabled: both show. A disabled key takes focus and the ring, so a keyboard user can reach its hint; Enter and Space do nothing.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
The pointer enters or leavesinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-color, colorThe fill and the ink change at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition.
The pointer is held downinputpress (--dur-press + --ease-standard)transformThe circle stays at rest: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition.
The pointer presses downinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-colorThe fill changes at once, by the same rule.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
iconstringThe id from ../icons.ts; the glyph is drawn in code.
titlestringThe accessible name (aria-label) and the hint's text.
controls?stringThe id of the region a fold key shows and hides: sets aria-controls.
description?stringA second line under the name in the hint, and the key's accessible description: why it is disabled ("Type a message first"), what it will do.
disabled?booleanBlocks the click and drops the glyph to the disabled ink.
expanded?booleanA fold key: sets aria-expanded to whether the region it folds is showing now.
onClick?((event: MouseEvent) => void)Runs on click.
popup?IconButtonPopupThe key opens a popup of this kind: sets aria-haspopup.
selected?booleanA toggle-style icon button: sets aria-pressed, and while on draws the full ink on the .08 fill, squared to the control radius (not the round .14 disc it was until 2026-11-11).
shortcut?stringThe shortcut that runs the same action, as the user reads it ("Ctrl+Z", "F9"): a key cap in the hint and aria-keyshortcuts on the button.
size?IconButtonSizeThe box size.
variant?IconButtonVariantThe look.
  • icon: the id from src/icons.ts; the glyph is drawn in code, never an image.
  • title: the accessible name (aria-label) and the text of the layer's hint; an icon alone has no name without it. No native title attribute is rendered.
  • variant: the look; defaults to ghost.
  • size: the circle; md is 24px with a 14px glyph, sm is 20px with a 12px glyph.
  • selected: sets aria-pressed and the selected look: the full ink on the .08 fill, squared to --radius-control. It is the one selected recipe, in every variant; until 2026-11-11 it was the .14 fill at the round radius, which in the title bar (its 3 call sites, 2 on at rest) drew filled discs louder than the title (docs/system/decisions.md, "The quiet pass"). A soft button rests on the same .08 fill, so a selected soft one is told by its square corner and its ink alone: pick ghost for a key that toggles.
  • expanded: a fold key; sets aria-expanded to whether the region it folds is showing.
  • controls: the id of the region a fold key shows and hides, or of the popup a key opens; sets aria-controls.
  • popup: the key opens a popup of this kind; sets aria-haspopup. menu for a list of actions, listbox for a list of values to pick one from, dialog for a popover holding fields or other controls.
  • shortcut: the shortcut that runs the same action, as the user reads it (Ctrl+Z, F9): a key cap after the name in the hint, and aria-keyshortcuts on the button. A title that ends in the shortcut in brackets ("Undo (Ctrl+Z)") still draws the cap; its name keeps the bracket, so no aria-keyshortcuts repeats it.
  • description: a second line under the name in the hint, tied to the button as its accessible description (aria-describedby): why the key is disabled, what it will do. Never the name.
  • disabled: blocks the click and drops the glyph to the disabled ink. It sets aria-disabled="true", never the native disabled, so the key stays in the Tab order and under the pointer and its hint still shows.
  • onClick: runs on click; a disabled circle never fires it.

Usage

When to use

  • The action is one glyph a tooltip can name: close, attach, send, stop, add.
  • The control sits in a tool bar, a panel header or a toolbar row where a label would crowd the row.

When not to use

  • The action needs a label to be understood. Use Button instead.
  • The control is a list item with a name. Use Row instead.
  • The glyph is a status rather than an action. Use Chip instead.

Rules

  • rule/icon-button-name: When an icon button is rendered, pass title for every use, because the glyph alone leaves the accessible name empty and a screen reader announces "button". Evidence: app 3/3 composer icon buttons, src/components/AssistantPane.tsx. Check: test src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <IconButton icon="close" /> — no name.
  • Do: <IconButton icon="close" title="Close the panel" />
  • rule/icon-button-one-inverted: When a toolbar row holds icon buttons, keep at most 1 inverted circle, because the ink-coloured circle is the row's primary action and a second one splits the eye. Evidence: measured 1 inverted send button in the composer toolbar, docs/system/decisions.md. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: two variant="inverted" circles in the composer row.
  • Do: 1 inverted send and ghost for attach and stop.
  • rule/icon-button-fold-expanded: When an icon button folds and unfolds a region, pass expanded with the region's state and controls with the region's id, and leave selected unset, because a title that flips between Show and Hide is the only signal otherwise, and a screen reader hears 2 unrelated buttons where there is 1 key that is collapsed or expanded. Evidence: app 3/3 fold keys (the layers, the properties, the changes row), src/components/LayersPanel.tsx. Check: test src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <IconButton icon="chevron-down" size="sm" title={open() ? "Hide the layers" : "Show the layers"} selected={open()} />
  • Do: <IconButton icon="chevron-down" size="sm" title={open() ? "Hide the layers" : "Show the layers"} expanded={open()} controls="layers-body" />
  • rule/icon-button-popup-kind: When an icon button opens something that floats over the page, pass popup with its kind (1 of menu, listbox, dialog, matching the role of what opens), expanded with whether it is open, and controls with its id while it is rendered, and leave selected unset, because a key with no aria-haspopup is announced as a plain button and the menu it opens arrives unannounced. Evidence: single use src/components/MenuBar.tsx:206, the narrow window's Main menu key, which sets the attribute from outside on mount. Check: test src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <IconButton icon="list" title="Main menu" expanded={open()} /> with setAttribute("aria-haspopup", "menu") on mount.
  • Do: <IconButton icon="list" title="Main menu" popup="menu" expanded={open()} controls={open() ? "main-menu" : undefined} />
  • rule/icon-button-no-native-title: When an icon button is styled or wrapped, add 0 hints of its own (no title attribute set from outside, no Tooltip around it), because the component already shows its title in the layer's hint box and a second hint stacks on the first. Evidence: app 31/31 icon buttons in the running shell render no title attribute, measured in the browser 2026-11-11. Check: test src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tooltip text="Close"><IconButton icon="close" title="Close" /></Tooltip>
  • Do: <IconButton icon="close" title="Close the panel" />
  • rule/icon-button-shortcut-prop: When an icon button's action has a shortcut, pass it as shortcut and keep it out of title, because the hint draws it as 1 key cap and the button says it through aria-keyshortcuts, while a bracket in the title puts "(Ctrl+Z)" into the accessible name a speech-input user has to say; the parsed bracket form stays for a caller that has not moved, and no call site in the app uses it now (the tool strip's five, the title bar's three and the composer's send and stop pass shortcut). Evidence: app 9/31 icon buttons in the running shell carry a shortcut in brackets in their name, measured in the browser 2026-11-11. Check: test src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <IconButton icon="undo" title="Undo (Ctrl+Z)" />
  • Do: <IconButton icon="undo" title="Undo" shortcut="Ctrl+Z" />
  • rule/icon-button-disabled-reason: When an icon button is disabled by something the user can fix, pass the reason as description in 1 short sentence, because the disabled key stays focusable and hoverable for exactly this, and its name alone says what it is and 0 words about why it is dead. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:976, the composer's send key, disabled while the message is empty with no reason given. Check: test src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <IconButton icon="send" title="Send" disabled={empty()} />
  • Do: <IconButton icon="send" title="Send" disabled={empty()} description={empty() ? "Type a message first" : undefined} />

Content

  • rule/icon-button-title-sentence: When title is written, name the action in sentence case with no full stop (Close the panel, Send, Stop), because the same string is the hint and the accessible name. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:892, the "Attach a picture (or paste, or drop one)" label. Check: review src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.
  • Don't: title="close panel."
  • Do: title="Close the panel"

Anti-slop

  • rule/icon-button-canonical-element: When a surface needs an icon action, render IconButton rather than a raw <button> with a hand-sized glyph, because the replaced classes hard-code 3 different box sizes and their own hover opacities. Evidence: app 10/10 lines across src/assistant.css and src/components/AssistantPane.tsx, rg -c "assistant-icon|assistant-attachment-x" src. Check: review src/ui/IconButton.tsx.
  • Don't: <button class="assistant-icon" onClick={stop}>…</button>
  • Do: <IconButton icon="stop" title="Stop" onClick={stop} />

Limits

  • rule/icon-button-row-limit: When a toolbar row holds more than 5 icon buttons, move the rest into a menu, because the measured composer row holds 3 at 24px each with 4px gaps and the row starts crowding the input past 5. Evidence: measured 3 actions at 24px with 4px gaps, docs/system/decisions.md. Check: review src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.
  • Don't: 6 circles in the composer's toolbar row.
  • Do: 3 circles in the row and the rest inside a menu.
  • rule/icon-button-touch-target: When 2 sm icon buttons sit side by side, keep at least 4px between them, because under a coarse pointer each 20px circle keeps its drawn size and takes a 24px target from an invisible ::after 2px past every edge, and closer circles overlap their targets. Evidence: measured 20px circle with a 24px ::after target, src/ui/ui.css:1558. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: .my-row .ui-icon-button--sm + .ui-icon-button--sm { margin-left: 0 } — two 24px targets on a 20px pitch.
  • Do: .my-row { display: flex; gap: var(--gap-4) }

Accessibility

Rests on the native <button> element, with the drawn glyph hidden from assistive tech. Disabled is the layer's own, shared with Button: aria-disabled="true" with the click refused on the button itself, because the native disabled takes a key out of the Tab order and, in some of the system webviews the desktop app runs in, out of the pointer's reach, and a key nobody can reach cannot say what it is or why it is blocked (docs/system/decisions.md, "Disabled controls").

Keyboard

KeyWhere focus isEffectFocus afterChecked by
TabThe circle, in document order.Moves focus to it; the accent ring draws and the hint shows at once.On the circle.by hand
EnterThe focused circle.Runs the action.Stays on the circle.test
SpaceThe focused circle.Runs the action on release, exactly once.Stays on the circle.by hand
Tab (disabled)A disabled circle, in document order.Moves focus to it, as to any key; the ring draws and its hint shows at once.On the circle.by hand
Enter or Space (disabled)The focused disabled circle.Nothing: the click is refused before any handler hears it.Stays on the circle.test
EscapeThe focused or hovered circle, its hint showing.Puts the hint away; the key is not consumed, so a surface that closes on Escape still closes.Stays on the circle.test

Related

  • Button: when the action needs a visible label.
  • Chip: when the glyph and the text are a fact rather than an action.
  • Row: when the clickable band is a list item.
  • Tab: when the control brings one view of a strip to the front rather than toggling a setting; a closable tab draws its own close key.
  • Tooltip: the hint box this component shows by itself; wrap another control in it, never this one.
  • Kbd: the key cap the hint draws for a shortcut.
  • Checkbox: when the on/off belongs to a form's value rather than to a tool.
  • Toggle: when a setting is switched in place under a fixed name, its state drawn by the glyph and never by a fill: a list row's state keys, a bar's drafting settings.

Kbd

Description

It shows the key or shortcut that runs the action beside it, as a fact to read and never as a control.

import { Kbd } from "../../../../src/ui/Kbd";, source src/ui/Kbd.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/button-div (n/a: a cap takes no handler), trap/role-button (n/a: a cap has no role beyond the native <kbd>), trap/control-height (n/a: a cap is text on a hairline, not a control; its 18px box comes from the 16px line and the two hairlines).

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — a native <kbd> on one recipe. It replaces two hand-built caps, and the recipe kept is the command palette's (.palette-key): the UI face, the quiet ink --text-faint, the chip type size and a 16px line. The assistant's (.assistant-key: the mono face at the disabled ink --text-disabled, no line height) lost, because the disabled ink marks a control that cannot be used and a shortcut can, and because the palette's shortcuts are combinations ("Ctrl+Shift+S") that read as words in the UI face.

Examples

<Kbd>esc</Kbd> — the key that stops a running request, beside Stop.

Real uses, 6 call sites (rg -c "<Kbd" src → src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:1, src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:4, src/components/DynamicInput.tsx:1):

  • src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:267 — each command's shortcut at the end of its palette row, written by shortcutLabel for the platform; a command with no shortcut draws no cap.
  • src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:288 — the palette footer's three caps (Enter, Tab, Esc) beside Run, Complete and Close.

Variants

Not applicable

Not applicable: no variant axes — a cap is one recipe; its text is the only thing that changes.

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestThe cap is rendered.Read it, then press the key it names. It takes no focus and no click.The key's text inside a hairline box with a 3px radius; a native <kbd>.test

State precedence

Not applicable: a cap has one state, so no two states can hold at once.

Motion

Not applicable: no motion.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
children?ElementThe key or shortcut as the user reads it: esc, Ctrl+Shift+P.
  • children: the key or shortcut as the user reads it: esc, Ctrl+Shift+P.

Usage

When to use

  • An action on screen has a key or a shortcut, and the user is helped by seeing it beside the action: Stop and esc, a palette command and its shortcut.

When not to use

  • The key should itself be clickable. Use Button instead, and put the cap beside it.
  • The text is a value or a keyword rather than a key (26 objects, a command's option). Use Chip instead.
  • The shortcut is a hint that should show only on hover. Use Tooltip instead.

Rules

  • rule/kbd-beside-action: When a cap is rendered, place it directly after the 1 action its key runs (the button, or the row's label), because a cap on its own names a key without saying what the key does. Evidence: app 2/2 caps follow their action, src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:765 and src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:141. Check: review src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.
  • Don't: <Kbd>esc</Kbd> alone on a status row.
  • Do: <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={stop}>Stop</Button><Kbd>esc</Kbd>
  • rule/kbd-not-a-control: When the shortcut's action must be clickable, put the handler on the Button or Row beside the cap rather than on the cap, because a <kbd> has no role and no tab stop, so a click handler on it is unreachable by keyboard. Evidence: app 2/2 caps take no handler, src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:1022 and src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:145. Check: test src/ui/Kbd.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <span onClick={stop}><Kbd>esc</Kbd></span>
  • Do: <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={stop}>Stop</Button><Kbd>esc</Kbd>

Content

  • rule/kbd-shortcut-label: When a cap shows a combination of 2 or more keys, write it with shortcutLabel(shortcut, mac), because the platform decides between "Ctrl+Shift+Z" and the macOS symbols and a literal string is wrong on one of them. Evidence: single use src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:145. Check: review src/components/CommandPalette.tsx.
  • Don't: <Kbd>Ctrl+S</Kbd>
  • Do: <Kbd>{shortcutLabel("Cmd+S", mac)}</Kbd>

Anti-slop

  • rule/kbd-canonical-element: When a surface shows a key, render Kbd rather than a raw <kbd> with its own class, because the 2 replaced classes drew the same cap in 2 faces and 2 inks. Evidence: app 2/2 hand-built caps replaced (.assistant-key and .palette-key), src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:755 and src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:145. Check: review src/ui/Kbd.tsx.
  • Don't: <kbd class="assistant-key">esc</kbd>
  • Do: <Kbd>esc</Kbd>

Limits

Not applicable: a cap holds the one string shortcutLabel produces or one key name, and the widest rendered so far, the 12-character "Ctrl+Shift+S", measures 69.8px and fits its palette row; no length or count has been seen to break.

Related

  • Button: the action a cap sits beside.
  • Row: a list band whose trailing cap shows the command's shortcut.
  • Chip: when the compact text is a value or a keyword rather than a key.
  • Tooltip: when the shortcut belongs in a hover hint rather than on the surface.

Row

Description

It is the full-width clickable band of a list: a layer, a command in a listbox or an item of a menu, marked current when it is the selected one.

import { Row } from "../../../../src/ui/Row";, source src/ui/Row.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/button-div, trap/role-button, trap/native-control, trap/list-dead-gap, trap/current-unmarked, trap/menu-navigation, trap/control-height, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/disabled-still-hovers, trap/touch-hover-flash, trap/hover-unguarded.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the 22px row, the 4px inset and the .14 selected fill are measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (docs/system/decisions.md and §5), and no registry item ships it.

<Row onClick={pick}>Layer 1</Row> — one layer in the layers list.

Added 2026-11-12.
  • src/components/AssistantPane.tsx — the empty state's example rows (a glyph, the prompt and a chevron; a press puts the prompt in the composer), the setup sheet's provider rows and the composer's slash list (the commands a /word draft matches; selected marks the one the arrow keys are on); the chat tabs in the header moved onto Tab; the transcript's tool rows and the composer's toolbar row stay bespoke (the toolbar is a container, and the tool row carries a disclosure arrow and a note).

Variants

Not applicable

Not applicable: no variant axes — a row is one band; the selected and disabled props are states, and its height, padding and ink come from the one recipe.

States

Example: Rows of a menu: one that runs, one that is not available, one that opens a submenu; none a Tab stop. (docs/system/examples/row/menuitem.tsx)

import { Row } from "../../../../src/ui/Row";

export default function Menuitem() {
  return (
    <div role="menu" aria-label="Edit">
      <Row menuitem onClick={() => undefined} onKeyDown={() => undefined}>Undo</Row>

State precedence

  • Hover and Selected: Selected wins. The .14 selected fill stays under the pointer; hover adds nothing to the fill.
  • Hover and Focused: Focused wins. The ring stays drawn while the pointer is over the row.
  • Hover and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled row keeps its resting look and takes no click.
  • Selected and Disabled: Disabled wins on a button. A disabled row is not the current one to the eye: it drops the .14 fill and shows the disabled ink, and aria-current="true" stays for assistive tech. On an option both show ("Option and Disabled" below).
  • Pressed and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn while the row is held down.
  • Option and Hover: Option wins. An option takes no fill from the pointer; the listbox moves the one highlight to it by setting selected.
  • Option and Selected: both show. The active option takes the .14 fill and the full ink, as the current row does.
  • Option and Disabled: both show. A blocked option still takes the highlight when the keys reach it, at the disabled ink, and takes no click: in a listbox the fill is where the keys are, and a list with no fill has lost its cursor.
  • Clipped and Disabled: both show. The hint still reads the full label under the pointer.
  • Menu item and Selected: Menu item wins. A menu row is never the current row: selected is not read, and no aria-current or .14 fill is drawn.
  • Menu item and Hover: both show. The pointer's row takes the .08 fill, as a plain row does.
  • Menu item and Focused: both show, and unlike a plain row the fill comes with the ring. The focus is the menu's cursor, so the keyboard's row is lit exactly as the pointer's is.
  • Menu item and Disabled: Disabled wins the fill and the click, and the focus still arrives. A row that is not available shows the ring alone when the keys reach it, and neither the pointer nor the keys fill it; Enter, Space and a click do nothing, and the arrow keys move on from it.
  • Menu item expanded and Hover elsewhere: both show. The row whose submenu is open keeps the .08 fill while the pointer is on a row of the submenu, so the path to the open menu stays lit.
  • Menu item and Clipped: both show. A label the menu's box cuts short (the stacked Main menu at 390px) shows in full in the hint, as on every row; a menu row has no other hint unless the caller passes title.
  • Option and Focused: Not applicable: an option is never focused; the listbox's field keeps the focus and names the active option with aria-activedescendant.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
The pointer enters or leavesinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-colorThe fill changes at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] rule removes the transition.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
children?ElementThe row's content: a label, and quiet trailing text such as a shortcut or a value.
describedBy?stringThe id of a line of the caller's that describes the row: aria-describedby, before the hint's own.
disabled?booleanBlocks the click and drops the ink to the disabled step.
expanded?booleanWhether the submenu the row opens is showing: sets aria-expanded, and holds the hover fill while it is.
id?stringThe element's id, for the listbox's aria-activedescendant.
menuitem?booleanThe row is one item of a role="menu" that moves the focus itself: a role="menuitem" button out of the Tab order, in the menu's recipe; disabled becomes aria-disabled.
onClick?((event: MouseEvent) => void)Runs on click.
onKeyDown?((event: KeyboardEvent) => void)A key pressed on a menu row: the menu's walk.
onPointerEnter?((event: PointerEvent) => void)The pointer arrived on a menu row: the menu opens or closes a submenu.
onPointerMove?((event: PointerEvent) => void)The pointer moved over the row: a listbox moves its highlight here.
option?booleanThe row is one option of a role="listbox" that owns the focus and the highlight: a role="option" band, no Tab stop and no hover fill of its own.
popup?"menu"A menu row that opens a submenu: sets aria-haspopup.
selected?booleanThe current row: the .14 fill, the full ink, and aria-current="true" (aria-selected on an option).
title?stringThe hint: what the row's text leaves out.
  • selected: the current row; sets aria-current="true" and the .14 fill. On an option it is the listbox's active option and sets aria-selected.
  • option: the row is one option of a role="listbox" that owns the focus and the highlight; it renders a role="option" band with no Tab stop and no hover fill.
  • menuitem: the row is one item of a role="menu" that moves the focus itself; it renders a role="menuitem" button with tabindex="-1" in the menu's recipe. disabled then sets aria-disabled="true" instead of the native attribute, and selected is not read.
  • popup: "menu" on a menu row that opens a submenu; sets aria-haspopup. It means what it means on IconButton. Pass expanded with it.
  • expanded: whether the submenu the row opens is showing; sets aria-expanded and holds the hover fill while it is.
  • describedBy: the id of a line of the caller's that describes a menu row (the typed command, "Type PL"); it comes first in aria-describedby, before the hint's own line.
  • onKeyDown: a key pressed on a menu row, handed to the menu's walk. A row that is not available hears it too.
  • onPointerEnter: the pointer arrived on a menu row; the menu opens or closes a submenu. A row that is not available hears it too.
  • id: the element's id, for the listbox's aria-activedescendant.
  • onPointerMove: the pointer moved over the row; a listbox moves its highlight here.
  • disabled: blocks the click and drops the ink to the disabled step. A plain row is natively disabled and leaves the Tab order; an option and a menuitem say aria-disabled="true" and stay where the keys can reach them.
  • title: the hint: what the row's text leaves out. It shows in the layer's hint box (after 0.4s under a mouse or a pen, at once when a key moves focus in) and is the row's accessible description (aria-describedby), never its name, and no native title attribute is rendered. A title that repeats the row's text adds nothing and is dropped. A clipped label needs no title: it shows in full by itself, with the title under it.
  • onClick: runs on click; a disabled row never fires it.
  • children: the row's content: a label, and quiet trailing text such as a shortcut.

Usage

When to use

  • One item of a list is clickable and runs one action: a layer, a command, an item of a menu.
  • The current item of that list must be marked for a screen reader as well as the eye.

When not to use

  • The action is a single control with a label. Use Button instead.
  • The row nests its own controls (a toggle cluster, a stepper). Use Button and IconButton in a bespoke band instead, because a button cannot nest buttons.
  • The band is a heading above a list rather than a row in it. Use SectionLabel instead.

Rules

  • rule/row-one-action: When a row runs an action, wire it on Row itself rather than on a label inside it, because a label-only hit area leaves dead space that reads as broken. Evidence: app 6/6 call sites pass onClick on the row itself, rg -n -A14 "<Row" src/components. Check: test src/ui/Row.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Row><span onClick={pick}>Layer 1</span></Row>
  • Do: <Row onClick={pick}>Layer 1</Row>
  • rule/row-option-in-listbox: When rows are the items of a role="listbox" whose field keeps the focus, pass option on each with an id, mark the active one with selected and move it from onPointerMove, because a <button> inside a role="option" adds 1 Tab stop per row and its own hover fill, so two rows are lit at once: the pointer's and the keyboard's. Evidence: single use src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:250, a Row button inside a .palette-option wrapper. Check: test src/ui/Row.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <div role="option" aria-selected={lit}><Row selected={lit} onClick={run}>Line</Row></div>
  • Do: <Row option id="command-0" selected={lit} onPointerMove={light} onClick={run}>Line</Row>
  • rule/row-menuitem-in-menu: When rows are the items of a role="menu", pass menuitem on each and mark the ones that cannot run with disabled, because a native disabled button takes no focus, so the arrow keys skip it and a screen reader never hears that the command exists, and a raw <button role="menuitem"> repeats the hover, focus and disabled recipe by hand (1 raw button and 9 .menu-row rules in src/chrome.css until 2026-11-11). Evidence: single use src/components/Menu.tsx:307, which draws every menu in the shell. Check: lint trap/native-control.
  • Don't: <button role="menuitem" tabIndex={-1} disabled={!item.enabled} onClick={run}>Paste</button>
  • Do: <Row menuitem disabled={!item.enabled} onClick={run} onKeyDown={walk}>Paste</Row>
  • rule/row-current-marked: When a list has a current item, pass selected on it, because the .14 fill alone is colour and a screen reader needs aria-current="true" to hear it. Evidence: app 3/3 list surfaces draw a current row, src/styles.css. Check: test src/ui/Row.test.tsx.
  • Don't: a hand-painted background on the current row with no aria-current.
  • Do: <Row selected>Current layer</Row>

Content

  • rule/row-trailing-quiet: When a row carries a shortcut or a value, put it after the label in the dim ink (--text-faint), because the label is what the user scans and the trailing text is secondary. Evidence: single use src/components/Menu.tsx:394, the shortcut span of a menu row (.menu-shortcut in src/chrome.css). Check: review src/components/Menu.tsx.
  • Don't: a shortcut before the label.
  • Do: <Row>Save<span class="row-shortcut">Ctrl+S</span></Row>

Anti-slop

  • rule/row-canonical-element: When a surface needs a list band, render Row rather than a div with an onClick, because a div has no role, no focus and no disabled state, and the replaced classes repeat hover and selected by hand. Evidence: app 6/6 list bands that run an action are Row (the layers, the palette's and the slash list's commands, the provider rows, the assistant's example rows, the menus' rows), rg -c "<Row" src/components. Check: review src/ui/Row.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="menu-row" onClick={pick}>Open</div>
  • Do: <Row onClick={pick}>Open</Row>

Limits

  • rule/row-label-limit: When a row's label runs past 40 characters at the 252px sidebar, clip it with an ellipsis on the label's own element and leave title for what the hint adds, because the measured row is 22px tall and the sidebar 252px wide, and the hint already reads a clipped label in full on its first line. Evidence: measured 22px row (docs/system/decisions.md) and the 252px sidebar (.sidebar in src/styles.css). Check: review src/styles.css.
  • Don't: a 60-character layer name that overflows the row.
  • Do: <Row><span class="row-label">{name}</span></Row> with overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis on the label, and no title that repeats it.
  • rule/row-touch-target: When rows stack in a list, let the list's height follow its rows rather than fixing it to a multiple of 22px, because under a coarse pointer each row grows from 22px to the 24px control height (rows stack with 0 gap, so an overhanging target would only overlap the next row), a menu row grows from 24px to the 28px button height, and a fixed list would cut its last rows. Evidence: measured 22px row, 24px under a coarse pointer, src/ui/ui.css:1586. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: .my-list { height: calc(var(--control-h-row) * 8); overflow: hidden }
  • Do: .my-list { max-height: calc(var(--control-h-input) * 8); overflow-y: auto }

Rests on the native <button> element: role, Enter and Space, disabled and focus come from the platform.
