Related

  • Button: when the control is an action rather than a list item.
  • SectionLabel: when the band is the heading above a list rather than a row in it.
  • IconButton: when the row's trailing control is a glyph action. A key that opens a menu of menuitem rows carries the same popup="menu" and expanded.
  • Tooltip: the hint box a row's title and its clipped label show in. A Tooltip wrapped around a row with no title still speaks; give the row its title instead of wrapping it.
  • Tab: when the control brings one view of a strip to the front rather than being one band of a list.
  • Kbd: when the text is the key that runs an action, shown at the end of the row.
  • Select: when the list is a short set of values behind one closed control rather than rows on the page.
  • Dialog: when the choice needs several fields and a decision, not one press in a list.

SectionLabel

Description

It names a panel's section as a real heading, so a screen reader can jump between the sections by heading.

import { SectionLabel } from "../../../../src/ui/SectionLabel";, source src/ui/SectionLabel.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/native-control.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the 11px uppercase header is measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (docs/system/decisions.md), and no registry item ships it.

Examples

<SectionLabel>Layers</SectionLabel> — the heading above the layers list.

Real uses, 18 call sites (rg -c "<SectionLabel" src/components → src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:4, src/components/BenchPanel.tsx:1, src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:1, src/components/JewelryDialog.tsx:1, src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:1, src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:1):

  • src/components/JewelryDialog.tsx — the heading over the Ring and Gem dialogs' read-out. Added 2026-11-12.
  • src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:209 — "Snap modes", over the Drafting Settings dialog's grid of object snap boxes.
  • src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:996 — the setup sheet's "Provider" heading over its list.
  • src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:83 — the "Layers" heading.
  • src/components/BenchPanel.tsx — the "Bench" heading over the piece's stones and metal. Added 2026-11-12.
  • src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:87 — the "Properties" heading.

Variants

Not applicable

Not applicable: no variant axes — a section label is one heading; its size, weight and ink come from the one recipe, and anything that looks different is a different role (a pane title, a tab).

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestThe heading is rendered.Read it; jump to it by heading navigation.The bold uppercase label at the faint ink, with no added letter spacing (the measured header).test
Long labelThe section's name is wider than its panel.Read it; the label does not wrap.The label runs to the panel's edge; a longer name is the caller's problem to shorten.by hand

State precedence

  • Rest and Long label: Not applicable: the heading has no other state; a long label is the same resting state with more text.

Motion

Not applicable: no motion — the heading never changes state, and its ink comes from the tokens.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
children?ElementThe section's name.
  • children: the section's name: one or two words, the same noun the panel uses elsewhere.

Usage

When to use

  • A panel or a popover holds more than one group, and each group needs a name a screen reader can jump to.
  • The name sits above a list, a table or a group of controls as their heading.

When not to use

  • The text is an action rather than a name. Use Button instead.
  • The text is a value or a status. Use Chip instead.
  • The text is a list item the user can pick. Use Row instead.

Rules

  • rule/section-label-heading-element: When a section label is rendered, keep it an <h2>, because the element is what lets a screen reader jump between panels and a styled <div> reads as plain text. Evidence: app 3/3 panels draw a section header, src/components/LayersPanel.tsx. Check: test src/ui/SectionLabel.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="section-label">Layers</div>
  • Do: <SectionLabel>Layers</SectionLabel>
  • rule/section-label-not-action: When a heading needs a control beside it, put the control outside SectionLabel rather than inside it, because a button inside a heading joins the heading's name and garbles heading navigation. Evidence: app 2/2 panel heads keep their controls in the bar, src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx. Check: review src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <SectionLabel>Layers <IconButton icon="plus" title="New layer" /></SectionLabel>
  • Do: <div class="head"><SectionLabel>Layers</SectionLabel><IconButton icon="plus" title="New layer" /></div>

Content

  • rule/section-label-one-noun: When the label's text is written, use 1 noun in title case (Layers, Properties, Selection), because the label is uppercased by CSS and a sentence reads as shouting. Evidence: single use src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:79, the label "Layers". Check: review src/components/LayersPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <SectionLabel>Here are your layers</SectionLabel>
  • Do: <SectionLabel>Layers</SectionLabel>

Anti-slop

  • rule/section-label-canonical-element: When a surface needs a section header, render SectionLabel rather than a styled <div> or a bespoke class, because the replaced class is a bare rule with no role and drifts per panel. Evidence: app 3/3 lines across 2 panels and src/styles.css, rg -c "section-label" src/components src/styles.css. Check: review src/ui/SectionLabel.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="section-label">Properties</div>
  • Do: <SectionLabel>Properties</SectionLabel>

Limits

  • rule/section-label-word-limit: When a section's name runs past 2 words, shorten it to 1 or 2 words, because the measured header row is 22px at 11px type and a third word starts clipping in a 260px sidebar. Evidence: measured 22px header at 11px type, docs/system/decisions.md. Check: review src/components/LayersPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <SectionLabel>Layer visibility and lock state</SectionLabel>
  • Do: <SectionLabel>Layers</SectionLabel>

Accessibility

Rests on the native <h2> element: heading role and level come from the platform, and heading navigation works without ARIA.

ARIA

Related

  • Row: when the text is a clickable list item rather than a heading.
  • Chip: when the text is a compact value.
  • Button: when the text is an action.

Select

Description

It lets the user pick one value from a short, known list, and hands the pick back to the caller, who owns the value.

import { Select } from "../../../../src/ui/Select";, source src/ui/Select.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/native-control, trap/control-height, trap/field-label, trap/label-unbound, trap/field-error-link, trap/field-keeps-input, trap/select-value-lost, trap/select-empty-value, trap/select-async (n/a: the choices are a prop, never fetched by the component), trap/touch-input-zoom, trap/touch-hover-flash, trap/hover-unguarded, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/disabled-still-hovers.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — a native <select> under a drawn face in Field's measured recipe (the 24px box, the hairline stroke, the focus edge; docs/system/decisions.md), and no registry item ships it.

Examples

<Select value={layer} options={layers} ariaLabel="Layer" onChange={setLayer} /> — the layer an object is on, picked from the drawing's layers.

Real uses, 18 call sites (rg -c "<Select" src → src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:1, src/components/JewelryDialog.tsx:4, src/components/LayerManager.tsx:4, src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:1):

  • src/components/JewelryDialog.tsx — the Ring dialog's size system and metal, the Gem dialog's cut and stone: each list is the engine's own, named by its row's <label for>. Added 2026-11-12.
  • src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:153 — the Drafting Settings dialog's increment angle (variant="field", size="md"): the usual angles and Custom, named by a visible <label for> through id.
  • src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:200 — the palette's choice rows (layer, linetype, colour): variant="inline" size="sm" align="end", mixed with the *VARIES* placeholder when the picked objects disagree.

Variants

variant

  • field: the form control, stroked and filled at rest, beside a Field. The default. Used at 0 call sites.
  • inline: a value in a dense list row; no stroke and no fill until the pointer or the keyboard is on it, with the arrow always drawn. Used at 0 call sites (the palette's 3 choice rows are planned).

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestThe control holds a value.Open the list, change the value by key, Tab away.The value's label and the chevron; a label wider than the box ends in an ellipsis before the arrow.test
HoverThe pointer is over the control, on a device with a hover pointer.Press to open the list.The pointer cursor; inline also takes the hairline stroke and the field fill.by hand
FocusedThe control takes focus by a press or Tab.Arrow keys and typed letters change the value; Space, Enter or Alt+ArrowDown open the list.The stroke takes the focus ink and the 1px ring draws at offset -1; inline takes the field fill.by hand
OpenThe user opens the list.Pick a choice, or Escape to leave the value as it was.The platform's own list (a popup on desktop, a picker on a phone).by hand
Off-list valuevalue is not among options.Keep it, or pick a listed choice; the off-list value stays the first choice until the caller's value changes.The value itself, shown and listed first.test
MixedThe caller passes mixed.Open the list and pick; the first pick replaces every differing value.The placeholder text (such as *VARIES*) in place of a value; it is not in the list.test
InvalidThe caller passes invalid.Pick another choice; the caller clears invalid when it accepts one.aria-invalid="true", and the caller's error line tied by describedBy; the stroke takes the error ink.test
DisabledThe caller passes disabled.Nothing: no list, no focus.The value and the chevron at the disabled ink; the cursor stays default.test
ClippedThe value's label is wider than the box.Rest the pointer on the control, or Tab to it, to read the whole label in the hint.The ellipsis; the hint's first line is the full label.test

Example: A refused choice at the error stroke, with the line that says why. (docs/system/examples/select/invalid.tsx)

import { Select } from "../../../../src/ui/Select";

const LAYERS = [
  { value: "0", label: "0" },
  { value: "walls", label: "Walls" },
  { value: "doors", label: "Doors" },
  { value: "furniture", label: "Furniture" },
];

export default function Invalid() {
  return (
    <div>
      <Select value="furniture" options={LAYERS} ariaLabel="Layer" invalid describedBy="layer-error" onChange={() => undefined} />
      <span id="layer-error">Furniture is locked. Pick a layer that takes new objects.</span>
    </div>
  );
}

State precedence

  • Focused and Hover: Focused wins. The focus stroke and the ring stay under the pointer.
  • Invalid and Focused: both show. The stroke keeps the error ink and the ring draws one line inside it.
  • Invalid and Hover: Invalid wins. The error stroke stays under the pointer.
  • Invalid and Mixed: both show. The placeholder stays in the quiet ink inside the error stroke.
  • Mixed and Off-list value: Mixed wins. The placeholder shows and value is not listed.
  • Mixed and Focused: both show. The placeholder stays until a choice is picked.
  • Mixed and Clipped: both show. A placeholder wider than the box clips and the hint reads it in full.
  • Disabled and Hover: Disabled wins. A disabled inline control takes no stroke and no fill under the pointer.
  • Disabled and Mixed: Disabled wins. The placeholder drops to the disabled ink.
  • Disabled and Invalid: Disabled wins on the ink, and the error stroke stays; the caller clears invalid before it locks a control nobody can correct.
  • Disabled and Clipped: both show. The hint still reads the full label under the pointer.
  • Open and Focused: both show. The control keeps its focus stroke while the platform's list is up.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
Focus arrives or leavesinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)border-color, background-colorThe stroke and the fill change at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition.
The pointer enters or leaves an inline controlinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)border-color, background-colorThe same: no transition plays.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
optionsreadonly SelectOption[]The choices, in the order the list shows them.
align?SelectAlignThe side the value sits on.
ariaLabel?stringThe accessible name when no visible <label> is tied to the control.
describedBy?stringThe id of the help line or the error line beside the control (several, space-separated): sets aria-describedby.
disabled?booleanBlocks the list and drops the ink to the disabled step.
id?stringThe native control's id, for a visible <label for> beside it: the label is then the name, and no ariaLabel is passed.
invalid?booleanThe value is refused: sets aria-invalid and the error stroke.
mixed?booleanThe selection holds differing values: the placeholder shows in the quiet ink, and the first pick replaces them all.
onChange?((value: string) => void)Runs when the user picks a choice, with its value.
placeholder?stringWhat the control reads while mixed ("*VARIES*").
size?SelectSizeThe box size.
title?stringThe hint: a short line about the value, added to the accessible description after describedBy.
value?stringThe current value.
variant?SelectVariantThe look.
  • value: the current value; the caller holds it. One that is not in options is listed first.
  • options: the choices as data, { value, label, disabled? }[], in list order.
  • onChange: runs with the picked value. A pick the caller does not take is put back.
  • ariaLabel: the accessible name when no visible label is tied to the control.
  • id: the native control's id, for a visible <label for> beside it; the label is then the name and no ariaLabel is passed.
  • variant: field (the default) or inline.
  • size: md (the default) or sm.
  • align: start (the default) or end.
  • mixed: the selection holds differing values; shows placeholder.
  • placeholder: what the control reads while mixed. Never a choice.
  • disabled: the native attribute; blocks the list and drops the ink.
  • invalid: the value is refused; sets aria-invalid="true" and the error stroke.
  • describedBy: the id of the help line or the error line (several, space-separated); sets aria-describedby.
  • title: the hint, in the layer's hint box and in the accessible description after describedBy. Never the name, and no native title is rendered. A clipped value is the hint's first line whether or not title is passed.

Usage

When to use

  • The user picks 1 of a known set of values that all fit in a list: a layer, a linetype, a unit.
  • The current value must stay readable while the list is closed, in a form or in a column of values.

When not to use

  • The value is typed rather than picked. Use Field instead.
  • The value is yes or no. Use Checkbox instead.
  • The picks are actions that run at once rather than a value that is held. Use Row in a menu instead.
  • There are 2 or 3 views to switch between, each always visible. Use Tab instead.

Rules

  • rule/select-options-data: When a surface offers a choice, pass the choices as options and the current one as value, because Select renders 0 children and a hand-written <option> never reaches the list. Evidence: single use src/ui/Select.tsx:117, the one place an <option> is rendered, from options. Check: test src/ui/Select.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Select ariaLabel="Layer"><option>0</option></Select>
  • Do: <Select ariaLabel="Layer" value={layer} options={layers.map((name) => ({ value: name, label: name }))} onChange={setLayer} />
  • rule/select-label-bound: When a select is rendered without a visible <label>, pass ariaLabel, because the value is the only text in the box and a screen reader would announce 1 unnamed combo box. Evidence: single use src/ui/Select.tsx:101, the aria-label the prop sets (the palette's choice rows are named this way today). Check: test src/ui/Select.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Select value={layer} options={layers} />
  • Do: <Select ariaLabel="Layer" value={layer} options={layers} onChange={setLayer} />
  • rule/select-off-list-value: When the current value may not be in the list (a layer deleted while an object still names it), pass it as value unchanged and leave the list as it is, because the component lists it as 1 more choice at the top and a control that shows another value would misreport the data. Evidence: single use src/ui/Select.tsx:85, the extra first choice (the palette adds that option by hand today). Check: test src/ui/Select.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Select value={layers.includes(layer) ? layer : layers[0]} options={options} ariaLabel="Layer" />
  • Do: <Select value={layer} options={options} ariaLabel="Layer" onChange={setLayer} />
  • rule/select-mixed-placeholder: When the selected objects hold differing values, pass mixed with a placeholder, because a placeholder added to options becomes 1 selectable choice that writes itself to every object. Evidence: single use src/ui/Select.tsx:112, the placeholder option, hidden and disabled (the palette's *VARIES* rows are the case). Check: test src/ui/Select.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Select value="*VARIES*" options={[{ value: "*VARIES*", label: "*VARIES*" }, ...options]} ariaLabel="Layer" />
  • Do: <Select mixed placeholder="*VARIES*" options={options} ariaLabel="Layer" onChange={setLayer} />
  • rule/select-described-by: When a line of help or an error sits beside a select, give the line an id and pass it as describedBy, and pass invalid while the value is refused, because a line that only sits near the control is read 0 times by a screen reader that lands on it by Tab. Evidence: single use src/ui/Select.tsx:98, the tie Field makes the same way (rule/field-described-by). Check: test src/ui/Select.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Select ariaLabel="Units" value={units} options={all} invalid /><span>Pick a unit the drawing uses.</span>
  • Do: <Select ariaLabel="Units" value={units} options={all} invalid describedBy="units-error" /><span id="units-error">Pick a unit the drawing uses.</span>
  • rule/select-inline-in-rows: When a select sits in a list row beside a label, use variant="inline" with size="sm" and align="end", because a stroked 24px box in each 22px row draws 1 frame per row and the values no longer share an edge. Evidence: measured 20px box in a 22px row and the value ending 16px before the box's edge, in the browser at 1280 wide, 2026-11-11. Check: review src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="prop-row"><span>Layer</span><Select value={layer} options={options} ariaLabel="Layer" /></div>
  • Do: <div class="prop-row"><span>Layer</span><Select variant="inline" size="sm" align="end" value={layer} options={options} ariaLabel="Layer" /></div>

Content

  • rule/select-option-label-noun: When an option's label is written, use the value's own name as the drawing or the setting spells it (Walls, Continuous, ByLayer), with 0 leading verbs, because the closed control shows the label alone as the current value. Evidence: single use src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:187, the palette's choices: layer and linetype names. Check: review src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: { value: "walls", label: "Move to Walls" }
  • Do: { value: "walls", label: "Walls" }

Anti-slop

  • rule/select-canonical-element: When a surface needs a choice from a list, render Select rather than a raw <select> with its own class or a hand-built listbox, because the replaced class removes the arrow and clips a long value with 0 ellipsis, and a hand-built list loses type-ahead and the phone's picker. Evidence: single use src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:201, which replaced .prop-select (appearance: none, no arrow, a long value cut with no ellipsis). Check: review src/ui/Select.tsx.
  • Don't: <select class="prop-select" onChange={pick}>{options}</select>
  • Do: <Select variant="inline" size="sm" align="end" value={value} options={options} ariaLabel={label} onChange={pick} />

Limits

  • rule/select-label-clip: When an option's label is wider than its box (a 268px label in a 140px box shows 110px of it), let it clip and leave title for what the hint adds, because the value ends in an ellipsis before the arrow and the hint already reads the full label. Evidence: measured 268px label, 110px shown, hint text equal to the full label, in the browser at 1280 wide, 2026-11-11. Check: test src/ui/Select.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Select title={currentLabel} value={value} options={options} ariaLabel="Layer" />
  • Do: <Select value={value} options={options} ariaLabel="Layer" />
  • rule/select-touch-target: When a size="sm" select sits in a list row of 22px, give the row a min-height rather than a fixed height, because under a coarse pointer the box grows from 20px to 24px and a row fixed at 22px would cut it. Evidence: measured 20px box, 24px under the coarse rules, in the browser, 2026-11-11. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: .my-row { height: var(--control-h-row); overflow: hidden }
  • Do: .my-row { min-height: var(--control-h-row) }

Accessibility

Rests on the native <select> element: role, value, the list, type-ahead, the phone's picker and disabled come from the platform. The drawn value and arrow are aria-hidden; assistive tech reads the select itself.

Related

  • Field: when the value is typed rather than picked.
  • Checkbox: when the value is yes or no.
  • Row: when the list is a menu of actions, or a listbox a search field drives.
  • Tooltip: the hint box a clipped value and a title show in; never wrap a select in one.
  • TextArea: when the value is free text over several lines rather than one of a list.
  • Dialog: the surface that holds a form of several choices with its actions.

Tab

Description

It brings one view of a strip to the front: a layout over the drawing or a chat in the assistant, marked selected when it is the one showing.

import { Tab } from "../../../../src/ui/Tab";, source src/ui/Tab.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/button-div, trap/role-button, trap/native-control, trap/current-unmarked, trap/control-height, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/touch-hover-flash, trap/hover-unguarded, trap/link-wraps-button (n/a: a tab is never a link; the close key is a sibling button, not a nested one), trap/disabled-still-hovers (n/a: a tab has no disabled state).

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the editor tab (13px type on a 12px inset in the 35px strip, the active one filled with --tab-active, the .08 fill on hover, a hairline between tabs) is measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (docs/system/decisions.md), and no registry item ships it. It replaces two hand-built tabs: the raw <button class="layout-tab" role="tab"> of the layout strip, and a Row in a width cell beside a close IconButton in the assistant's header.

Parts

  • TabPanels (the same file) is the whole tabs pattern for views that swap in place, a dialog's pages: a role="tablist" strip of sm tabs named by ariaLabel, and one role="tabpanel" per tab, tied both ways (aria-controls, aria-labelledby). The caller passes panels ({ id, label, content }), the selected id and onChange(id). The strip is one Tab stop; Left, Right, Home and End move the focus and bring that page to the front at once (automatic activation: a page is already built, so showing it costs nothing, where the layout strip switches only on Enter because a switch redraws the drawing). A page behind is hidden, not removed, so a field keeps what was typed in it. Used at 1 call site, src/components/DraftingSettings.tsx:259.

Examples

<Tab selected onClick={show}>Model</Tab> — the model-space tab over the drawing.

Real uses, 4 call sites (rg -c "<Tab" src/components → src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:4, src/components/StatusBar.tsx:1):

  • src/components/StatusBar.tsx:80 — LayoutTabs, the editor tabs over the drawing (size="md"): Model, then each layout; selected marks the space in front, title says what the tab switches to.
  • src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:573 — the chat tabs in the assistant's header when more than one chat is open (size="sm"): selected marks the chat in front, onClose closes that chat, closeLabel names it ("Close hello"), title carries the full chat title when the label clips.
  • The menu titles in src/components/MenuBar.tsx stay native buttons: they open menus, a different role.
  • The status bar's drafting toggles in src/components/StatusBar.tsx are Toggle: a drafting toggle is an aria-pressed switch, not a tab.

import { createSignal } from "solid-js";
import { TabPanels } from "../../../../src/ui/Tab";

export default function InTabPanels() {
  const [page, setPage] = createSignal("snap-grid");
  return (
    <TabPanels
      ariaLabel="Drafting settings"
      selected={page()}
      onChange={setPage}
      panels={[
        { id: "snap-grid", label: "Snap and Grid", content: () => <p>The snap and grid spacing.</p> },
        { id: "polar", label: "Polar Tracking", content: () => <p>The increment angle.</p> },
        { id: "osnap", label: "Object Snap", content: () => <p>The running object snaps.</p> },
      ]}
    />
  );
}

Used at 1 call site (the assistant's chat tabs).
  • md: the editor tab; the default: it fills its strip's height (the strip is the 35px band), 13px type on a 12px inset, a hairline on its right, clipped at 24ch; selected, it takes --tab-active. Used at 1 call site (the layout tabs over the drawing).

Never a finger.Read the full label and what the tab switches to; a press, a click or Escape puts the box away.The layer's hint box: the full label when it is clipped, the title under it or by itself, below the tab, inside the window's edges.test

Example: The tab in front at the active fill, announced as selected. (docs/system/examples/tab/selected.tsx)

import { Tab } from "../../../../src/ui/Tab";

export default function Selected() {
  return <Tab selected>Model</Tab>;
}

State precedence

  • Hinted and Hover: both show. The hint follows the hover after its delay.
  • Hinted and Focused: both show. The hint arrives with the ring, with no delay.
  • Hinted and Pressed: Pressed wins. The press puts the hint away.
  • Hinted and Selected: both show. The tab in front hints like any other.
  • Hinted and Closable: both show. The close key shows its own hint (closeLabel) when the pointer or the focus is on it.
  • Hover and Selected: Selected wins. The active fill stays under the pointer; hover adds nothing to the tab in front.
  • Hover and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn over the hover fill.
  • Selected and Focused: both show. The ring draws around the active fill.
  • Pressed and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn while the tab is held down.
  • Closable and Selected: both show. Every closable tab keeps its close key, in front or behind.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
The pointer enters or leavesinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-color, colorThe fill and ink change at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] rule removes the transition.
The tab comes to the front or goes behindinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-color, colorThe fill and ink change at once, by the same rule.

Props

Tab

PropTypeDefaultPurpose

TabPanels

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
ariaLabelstringThe strip's accessible name: what the views are views of ("Drafting settings").
onChange(id: string) => voidRuns when a click or an arrow key asks for another view, with its id.
panelsreadonly TabPanel[]The views, in the strip's order.
selectedstringThe id of the view in front.
  • selected: the tab in front; sets aria-selected="true" (and "false" otherwise) and the selected fill of its size.
  • size: sm or md; defaults to md.
  • title: the hint, shown in the layer's hint box and tied to the tab as its accessible description (aria-describedby): what the tab switches to. It is never the name, and no native title attribute is rendered. A title equal to the label draws no hint and adds no description. A clipped label needs no title: the hint shows the full label by itself, with the title on a second line when it says more.
  • onClick: runs on click; the caller brings this tab to the front.
  • onClose: draws the trailing close key and runs when it is clicked; the tab's onClick does not run.
  • closeLabel: the close key's accessible name and tooltip; defaults to "Close".
  • id: the tab's own id, for the panel it shows to name it (aria-labelledby).
  • controls: the id of the panel the tab shows; sets aria-controls.
  • tabIndex: for a strip that is one Tab stop, 0 on the tab in front and -1 on the others; unset, no attribute is written and every tab is a Tab stop.
  • children: the tab's label.

Usage

When to use

  • Several views share one area and one shows at a time: the model space and the layouts over the drawing, the open chats in the assistant.
  • The view in front must be marked for a screen reader as well as the eye.

When not to use

  • The control runs an action rather than showing a view. Use Button instead.
  • The item is one band of a full-width list (a layer, a menu item, a command). Use Row instead.
  • The control flips a setting on and off (a drafting toggle). Use IconButton with selected instead.
  • The label is a short fact with no view behind it. Use Chip instead.

Rules

  • rule/tab-selected-marked: When a strip has a tab in front, pass selected on it, because the fill alone is colour and a screen reader needs aria-selected="true" to hear which view shows. Evidence: app 2/2 strips mark the tab in front, src/components/StatusBar.tsx:57 and src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:548. Check: test src/ui/Tab.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tab onClick={show}>Model</Tab> for the tab whose view is showing.
  • Do: <Tab selected onClick={show}>Model</Tab>
  • rule/tab-in-tablist: When tabs are rendered, place them in 1 container carrying role="tablist" and an aria-label, because a tab role outside a tablist is announced without its strip and its position. Evidence: app 2/2 strips, src/components/StatusBar.tsx:54 and src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:630. Check: review src/components/StatusBar.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="editor-tabs"><Tab selected>Model</Tab></div>
  • Do: <div class="editor-tabs" role="tablist" aria-label="Views"><Tab selected>Model</Tab></div>
  • rule/tab-close-sibling: When a tab can be closed, pass onClose rather than putting a button in the tab's children, because a <button> cannot nest a <button> and Tab renders the close key as a sibling. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:503, the one closable strip. Check: test src/ui/Tab.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tab onClick={show}>hello<IconButton icon="close" title="Close hello" onClick={close} /></Tab>
  • Do: <Tab onClick={show} onClose={close} closeLabel="Close hello">hello</Tab>

Content

  • rule/tab-close-label-names: When onClose is passed, pass closeLabel as "Close" plus the tab's label ("Close hello"), because 2 close keys both named "Close" in one strip cannot be told apart by a screen reader. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:494. Check: review src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tab onClose={close}>hello</Tab> in a strip of 2 closable tabs.
  • Do: <Tab onClose={close} closeLabel="Close hello">hello</Tab>

Anti-slop

  • rule/tab-canonical-element: When a surface needs a tab, render Tab rather than a raw <button role="tab"> with its own class or a Row in a width cell, because the 2 replaced recipes painted 2 different selected fills and only 1 of them set aria-selected. Evidence: app 2/2 hand-built tabs replaced (.layout-tab and .assistant-tab-row), src/components/StatusBar.tsx:57 and src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:440. Check: review src/ui/Tab.tsx.
  • Don't: <button class="layout-tab is-active" role="tab">Model</button>
  • Do: <Tab selected>Model</Tab>

Limits

  • rule/tab-label-limit: When an sm tab's label runs past 18 characters, pass the whole label as the children and leave the shortening to the tab, because the tab clips at max-width: 18ch with an ellipsis (the 20-character "Summarise the layers" shows as "Summarise the la…") and shows the full label in its hint by itself, while a label cut by the caller has no full text anywhere. Evidence: measured 111.6px clipped sm tab at 1280px, src/ui/ui.css:1224. Check: test src/ui/Tab.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tab size="sm">{title.slice(0, 16) + "…"}</Tab> — the cut label has no full text anywhere.
  • Do: <Tab size="sm">Summarise the layers</Tab>
  • rule/tab-md-label-limit: When an md tab's label runs past 24 characters, pass the whole label as the children and leave the shortening to the tab, because the tab clips at max-width: 24ch with an ellipsis and shows the full label in its hint by itself, and uncapped the 56-character "A1 Ground floor general arrangement plan, sheet 12 of 40" draws a 357.8px tab that pushes the other layouts out of the strip. Evidence: measured 168.2px clipped md tab at 1280px, src/ui/ui.css:1213. Check: test src/ui/Tab.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tab title="A1 Ground floor general arrangement plan, sheet 12 of 40">A1 Ground floor…</Tab> — the label a screen reader hears is the cut one.
  • Do: <Tab>A1 Ground floor general arrangement plan, sheet 12 of 40</Tab>
  • rule/tab-touch-target: When sm tabs are laid out in a pane header, leave the header room for a 24px tab, because under a coarse pointer the 22px tab grows to the 24px control height (it clips its own overflow for the ellipsis, so it cannot take an overhanging target) and a header fixed at 22px would cut it. Evidence: measured 22px sm tab, 24px under a coarse pointer, src/ui/ui.css:1586. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: .my-head { height: var(--control-h-row); overflow: hidden }
  • Do: .my-head { min-height: var(--control-h-button); align-items: center }

Accessibility

Rests on the native <button> element with role="tab": Enter and Space and focus come from the platform. A bare Tab stays in the tab order and has no arrow-key handler of its own: the caller owns the tablist container and its walk (the layout strip roves from its container), and wires a tabpanel through id and controls when it has one. TabPanels does all of it: one Tab stop, the arrow keys, Home and End, and a tabpanel per tab.

Related

  • IconButton: the close key a closable tab draws; and the pick for an on/off toggle.
  • Button: when the control runs an action rather than showing a view.

TextArea

Description

It takes several lines of text, grows to hold them up to a limit, and hands every edit back to the caller, who owns the text.

        ariaLabel="Ask the assistant"
        onInput={() => undefined}
        onKeyDown={(event) => {
          if (event.key === "Enter" && !event.shiftKey) event.preventDefault();
        }}
      />
    </div>
  );
}

Variants

variant

  • field: the form control, with Field's stroke, fill, padding and type; one line is exactly a Field's 24px. Its stroke is the field's own edge ink (--ui-field-edge): the hairline stroke on the dark surfaces and the default stroke on the light ones, where the hairline measured 1.18 against the fill; until 2026-11-12 it drew the hairline stroke in both themes. The default. Used at 0 call sites.
  • bare: no stroke, no fill, no padding and no ring, with the type of the element around it; for an editor inside a card that draws those itself. Used at 0 call sites (the assistant's composer is planned).

Example: The form control: stroked and filled. (docs/system/examples/textarea/variant-field.tsx)

import { TextArea } from "../../../../src/ui/TextArea";

export default function VariantField() {
  return <TextArea variant="field" value={"Walls are drawn to the finished face.
Doors swing into the room."} ariaLabel="Notes" onInput={() => undefined} />;
}

Example: The editor inside a card that draws the box and the focus. (docs/system/examples/textarea/variant-bare.tsx)

import { TextArea } from "../../../../src/ui/TextArea";

export default function VariantBare() {
  return (
    <div class="assistant-composer">
      <TextArea variant="bare" value="" placeholder="Ask, or / for commands" ariaLabel="Ask the assistant" onInput={() => undefined} />
    </div>
  );
}

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestThe control is empty or holds text.Type, select, paste, Tab away.The text at the full ink, or the placeholder at the faint ink; the box is rows lines tall or as tall as its text.test
HoverThe pointer is over the control, on a device with a hover pointer.Click to place the caret.Nothing beyond the text cursor.by hand
FocusedThe control takes focus by click or Tab.Type; Tab away.field: the stroke takes the focus ink and the 1px ring draws at offset -1. bare: the caret alone; the card around it shows the focus.by hand
GrowingThe text needs more lines than are showing, up to maxRows.Keep typing; nothing scrolls.The box is taller by whole lines; what is below it moves down.test
ScrollingThe text needs more than maxRows lines.Scroll inside the control; the caret stays in view.The box stops at maxRows lines and the platform's scrollbar shows.test
InvalidThe caller passes invalid.Correct the text; the caller clears invalid when it accepts it.aria-invalid="true", and the caller's line tied by describedBy; on field the stroke takes the error ink.test
DisabledThe caller passes disabled.Nothing: no typing, no focus.The text at the disabled ink.test
ComposingAn input method is composing a character.Finish or cancel the composition.The platform's own composition underline; onKeyDown hears no key until it ends.test

Example: Locked text at the disabled ink. (docs/system/examples/textarea/disabled.tsx)

import { TextArea } from "../../../../src/ui/TextArea";

export default function Disabled() {
  return <TextArea value="This layer is locked." ariaLabel="Notes" disabled />;
}

Example: Refused text at the error stroke, with the line that says why. (docs/system/examples/textarea/invalid.tsx)

import { TextArea } from "../../../../src/ui/TextArea";

export default function Invalid() {
  return (
    <div>
      <TextArea value="LINE 0,0 10" ariaLabel="Script" invalid describedBy="script-error" spellcheck={false} onInput={() => undefined} />
      <span id="script-error">Line 1 ends before its second point.</span>
    </div>
  );
}

State precedence

  • Focused and Hover: Focused wins. The focus stroke and the ring stay under the pointer.
  • Growing and Scrolling: Not applicable: the text fits within maxRows lines or it does not.
  • Growing and Focused: both show. The box grows under the caret with the focus stroke drawn.
  • Scrolling and Focused: both show. The capped box keeps its focus stroke while its text scrolls.
  • Invalid and Focused: both show. On field the stroke keeps the error ink and the ring draws one line inside it.
  • Invalid and Hover: Invalid wins. The error stroke stays under the pointer.
  • Invalid and Growing: both show. Text past a caller's limit keeps growing the box inside the error stroke; nothing is cut.
  • Invalid and Disabled: Disabled wins. The caller clears invalid before it locks text nobody can correct.
  • Disabled and Hover: Disabled wins. A disabled control takes no caret and no ring.
  • Disabled and Scrolling: both show. Locked text past the cap can still be scrolled and read.
  • Composing and Focused: both show. The focus stroke stays while the input method holds the keys.
  • Composing and Growing: both show. The box grows as composed text is committed.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
Focus arrives or leaves (field)inputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)border-colorThe stroke changes at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition.
The text gains or loses a lineinputnone: the height is set at once, so the caret never waits for the boxheight (not animated)The same in every setting.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
activeDescendant?stringA combobox: the id of the option the arrow keys are on (aria-activedescendant); unset when none is.
ariaLabel?stringThe accessible name when no visible <label> is tied to the control.
autocomplete?stringThe native autofill hint; off for text no form should remember.
autocompleteKind?AutocompleteKindA combobox: what its list does with the typed text (aria-autocomplete).
autoFocus?booleanFocus the control when it mounts.
controls?stringA combobox: the id of its list (aria-controls).
describedBy?stringThe id of the help line or the error line beside the control (several, space-separated): sets aria-describedby.
disabled?booleanBlocks typing and drops the ink to the disabled step.
expanded?booleanA combobox: whether its list is showing now (aria-expanded).
id?stringThe control's id, for a visible <label for> beside it or around it: the label is then the name, and no ariaLabel is passed.
invalid?booleanThe text is refused: sets aria-invalid and, on field, the error stroke.
maxRows?numberThe most lines it grows to before it scrolls.
onInput?((value: string) => void)Runs on every edit with the new text.
onKeyDown?((event: KeyboardEvent) => void)A key went down in the control, outside an input method's composition.
onPaste?((event: ClipboardEvent) => void)Something was pasted: the caller may take what is not text (a picture) from the clipboard.
placeholder?stringThe placeholder.
ref?((el: HTMLTextAreaElement) => void)Hands the element to the caller, to focus it or to place the caret.
role?"combobox"The text drives a list of matches and keeps the keyboard: combobox.
rows?numberThe fewest lines it shows.
spellcheck?booleanWhether the platform's spelling checker runs.
title?stringThe hint: a short line about the text, added to the accessible description after describedBy.
value?stringThe current text.
variant?TextAreaVariantThe look.
  • value: the current text; the caller holds it. It is written to the element only when it differs from what is typed, so a composition is never restarted.
  • onInput: runs on every edit with the new text.
  • placeholder: an example of the text; never the only name.
  • ariaLabel: the accessible name when no visible label is tied to the control.
  • variant: field (the default) or bare.
  • rows: the fewest lines shown; defaults to 2.
  • maxRows: the most lines it grows to before it scrolls; defaults to 8.
  • disabled: the native attribute; blocks typing and drops the ink.
  • invalid: the text is refused; sets aria-invalid="true" and, on field, the error stroke.
  • id: the control's id, for a visible <label for> beside it or around it; the label is then the name and no ariaLabel is passed. Used at 0 call sites: the composer's card is a <label for> and still writes the id on the element through ref, which this prop replaces.
  • describedBy: the id of the help line or the error line (several, space-separated); sets aria-describedby.
  • title: the hint, in the layer's hint box and in the accessible description after describedBy. Never the name, and no native title is rendered.
  • autoFocus: focuses the control when it mounts.
  • autocomplete: the native autofill hint; unset leaves it to the platform.
  • spellcheck: switches the platform's spelling checker; unset leaves it to the platform.
  • onKeyDown: a key went down outside an input method's composition; the caller may preventDefault it.
  • onPaste: something was pasted; the caller may take what is not text.
  • ref: hands the element to the caller, to focus it or to place the caret.
  • role: combobox, while the text drives a list of matches and keeps the keyboard (the composer's slash list).
  • expanded: a combobox's list is showing (aria-expanded).
  • controls: the id of a combobox's list (aria-controls).
  • activeDescendant: the id of the option the arrow keys are on (aria-activedescendant); unset when none is.
  • autocompleteKind: what the list does with the typed text (aria-autocomplete): list, inline, both or none.

Usage

When to use

  • The user writes more than 1 line: a message to the assistant, a note on a layer, a block of script.
  • The text's length is not known ahead, and the control should take the room the text needs before it scrolls.

When not to use

  • The text is 1 line: a name, a coordinate, a keyword. Use Field instead.
  • The value is picked from a list. Use Select instead.
  • The text is a fact to read rather than to edit. Use Chip instead.

Rules

  • rule/textarea-label-bound: When a text area is rendered without a visible <label>, pass ariaLabel, because a placeholder disappears at the first character and leaves 1 unnamed text box. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:1369, the composer's editor, named "Ask the assistant" with a placeholder beside it. Check: test src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <TextArea placeholder="Ask, or / for commands" value={draft()} onInput={setDraft} />
  • Do: <TextArea ariaLabel="Ask the assistant" placeholder="Ask, or / for commands" value={draft()} onInput={setDraft} />
  • rule/textarea-rows-not-height: When a text area needs a smallest or a largest size, pass rows and maxRows rather than a height, min-height or max-height in a stylesheet, because the component sets the height itself from the measured text on every edit and a second height fights it by 1 line or more. Evidence: single use src/ui/TextArea.tsx:115, the one place the height is set. Check: test src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx.
  • Don't: .my-notes .ui-textarea { min-height: 64px; max-height: 240px }
  • Do: <TextArea rows={2} maxRows={9} ariaLabel="Notes" value={notes()} onInput={setNotes} />
  • rule/textarea-enter-in-keydown: When Enter sends the text, handle it in onKeyDown and call preventDefault, leaving Shift+Enter to break the line, because onKeyDown hears 0 keys while an input method is composing and a handler on a wrapper would send a half-composed word. Evidence: single use src/ui/TextArea.tsx:194, the composition guard. Check: test src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <div onKeyDown={(e) => e.key === "Enter" && send()}><TextArea ariaLabel="Ask" value={draft()} onInput={setDraft} /></div>
  • Do: <TextArea ariaLabel="Ask" value={draft()} onInput={setDraft} onKeyDown={(e) => { if (e.key === "Enter" && !e.shiftKey) { e.preventDefault(); send(); } }} />
  • rule/textarea-bare-card-focus: When variant="bare" is used, give the card around it the focus cue with :focus-within, because the bare editor draws 0 rings of its own and a keyboard user would otherwise see no focus at all. Evidence: single use src/ui/ui.css:1094, the bare recipe, which drops the ring. Check: review src/assistant.css.
  • Don't: <div class="card"><TextArea variant="bare" ariaLabel="Ask" /></div> with no .card:focus-within rule.
  • Do: .card:focus-within { border-color: var(--composer-border-active) } around <TextArea variant="bare" ariaLabel="Ask" />
  • rule/textarea-described-by: When a line of help, a count or an error sits beside a text area, give the line an id and pass it as describedBy, and pass invalid while the text is refused, because a line that only sits near the control is read 0 times by a screen reader that lands on it by Tab. Evidence: single use src/ui/TextArea.tsx:169, the tie Field makes the same way (rule/field-described-by). Check: test src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <TextArea ariaLabel="Ask" invalid /><div>120 characters too long to send</div>
  • Do: <TextArea ariaLabel="Ask" invalid describedBy="ask-over" /><div id="ask-over">120 characters too long to send</div>
  • rule/textarea-combobox-while-listed: When a text area drives a list of matches for part of what is typed, pass role="combobox" with expanded, controls and activeDescendant only while the list shows, and drop all 4 when it goes, because a multi-line text box that always says it is a combobox is announced as 1 on every focus, and its arrow keys are then expected to walk a list that is not there. Evidence: app 5/5 combobox props defined together in src/ui/TextArea.tsx. Check: test src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <TextArea ariaLabel="Ask the assistant" role="combobox" expanded={false} value={draft()} onInput={setDraft} /> on a composer with no list open.
  • Do: <TextArea ariaLabel="Ask the assistant" role={listed() ? "combobox" : undefined} expanded={listed() ? true : undefined} controls={listed() ? "slash-list" : undefined} activeDescendant={listed() ? activeId() : undefined} value={draft()} onInput={setDraft} />

Content

  • rule/textarea-placeholder-example: When a placeholder is written, show in 2 to 6 words what goes here or what the control takes (Ask, or / for commands) and put a rule the user must keep in mind in a line tied by describedBy, because the placeholder is gone at the first character. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:1042, the composer's two placeholders. Check: review src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.
  • Don't: <TextArea ariaLabel="Ask" placeholder="Messages must be under 8,000 characters and may not be empty" />
  • Do: <TextArea ariaLabel="Ask the assistant" placeholder="Ask, or / for commands" />

Anti-slop

  • rule/textarea-canonical-element: When a surface needs multi-line text, render TextArea rather than a raw <textarea> with its own class and its own grow function, because the hand-built one fixes its limits in pixels (64 and 240) where the type size they were counted from can change, and every copy re-solves composition and growth. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:104, the composer's own grow. Check: review src/ui/TextArea.tsx.
  • Don't: <textarea class="assistant-input" rows={1} onInput={(e) => grow(e.currentTarget)} />
  • Do: <TextArea variant="bare" rows={2} maxRows={9} ariaLabel="Ask the assistant" value={draft()} onInput={setDraft} />

Limits

  • rule/textarea-max-rows: When text may run past 8 lines, leave maxRows at 8 or set it to the lines the surface can spare (9 in the composer), because past the cap the box stops and scrolls, and a cap the surface cannot hold pushes the send key off the screen. Evidence: measured 72px box, 230px scrollHeight, overflow-y: auto, in the browser at 1280 wide, 2026-11-11. Check: test src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <TextArea maxRows={200} ariaLabel="Ask" /> above a send key.
  • Do: <TextArea maxRows={9} ariaLabel="Ask the assistant" />
  • rule/textarea-one-row-field: When a text area sits on a row with a Field, pass rows={1}, because 1 line of the field variant measures the Field's 24px and the default 2 lines measure 40px. Evidence: measured 24px at rows={1} beside a 24px Field and 40px at the default, in the browser, 2026-11-11. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: <div class="form-row"><Field ariaLabel="Name" /><TextArea ariaLabel="Note" /></div>
  • Do: <div class="form-row"><Field ariaLabel="Name" /><TextArea rows={1} ariaLabel="Note" /></div>

Accessibility

Rests on the native <textarea> element: typing, selection, IME, undo and disabled come from the platform. The height is paint: assistive tech reads the whole text whatever shows.

Keyboard

KeyWhere focus isEffectFocus afterChecked by
TabThe control, in document order.Moves focus in; on field the focus stroke and ring draw. Tab never types a tab character, so the keyboard is never trapped.On the control.by hand
Tab (disabled)A disabled control is skipped.Focus moves past it.On the next control.by hand
EnterThe focused control.Breaks the line and the box grows by one, unless the caller's onKeyDown prevents it (to send).Stays on the control.test
Enter (composing)The focused control, mid-composition.Confirms the input method's candidate; onKeyDown is not called.Stays on the control.test
ArrowUp / ArrowDown, PageUp / PageDownThe focused control.Move the caret; past the cap the text scrolls to keep it in view.Stays on the control.by hand
ArrowUp / ArrowDown, Enter (combobox)The focused control, while its list shows.The caller's onKeyDown moves activeDescendant through the list or runs the active option, and prevents the caret's move; the control moves no focus.Stays on the control.by hand

Related

  • Field: when the text is one line.
  • Select: when the value is picked rather than written.
  • Button: when the text is sent by a control beside it.
  • IconButton: the send key beside a composer's editor.
  • Tooltip: the hint box a title shows in; never wrap a text area in one.

Toggle

Description

It switches one setting on or off in place, under a name that never changes, and says which it is through its pressed state.

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";, source src/ui/Toggle.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/button-div, trap/role-button, trap/native-control, trap/button-icon-name, trap/icon-optical-size, trap/icon-optical-align, trap/control-height, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/disabled-still-hovers, trap/touch-hover-flash, trap/hover-unguarded, trap/touch-tap-highlight, trap/color-only-status, trap/toggle-switch-submit (n/a: type="button", a toggle never submits), trap/toggle-indeterminate (n/a: a toggle is on or off; a value that can be mixed is a Checkbox), trap/weight-shift (n/a: on and off are one weight, so a word never changes width).

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — a native <button aria-pressed> drawn from the layer's tokens; the two faces are the app's own measured ones (the layer list's state keys in src/styles.css and the status bar's drafting toggles in src/chrome.css, moved here value for value on 2026-11-11), and the glyphs are the app's own src/icons.ts paths.

Examples

<Toggle size="sm" tone="info" icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" hint={frozen() ? "Thaw" : "Freeze"} pressed={frozen()} onChange={setFrozen} /> — a layer's freeze key: one name, the state in the glyph and aria-pressed, the action in the hint.

Real uses, 9 call sites (rg -c "<Toggle" src → src/components/LayerManager.tsx:1, src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:3, src/components/StatusBar.tsx:1):

  • src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:127 — a layer row's on key: glyph, sm, tone="absent" (off is the state that explains a missing layer).
  • src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:137 — the same row's frozen key: tone="info".
  • src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:147 — the same row's locked key: tone="caution".
  • src/components/StatusBar.tsx:182 — each of the status bar's 11 drafting settings: text, sm, the function key as shortcut, the hint above the bar, in a toolbar that is one Tab stop.

Variants

variant

  • glyph: an icon that changes with the state (icon off, iconOn on), in the ink its tone picks; the default. Used at 3 call sites (a layer row's on, frozen and locked keys).
  • text: a short word in capitals; on, the full ink on a chip (the .08 fill at the control radius, 3px shorter than the line at each end and 3px clear of the word at each side); off, the quiet ink on nothing. The ink carries the state with the chip taken away (the on word measures 14.1 on its chip and the off word 6.5 on the bar, dark; 14.1 and 5.7, light; the two inks are 2.6 and 2.9 apart, where the secondary ink on the selected fill stood 1.6 and 1.5 from the off word), and a bar that holds a run of them keeps two chips 4px apart. Used at 1 call site (the status bar's drafting settings, 11 rendered).

Example: The glyph face: an icon for each state, the state in the glyph and its ink. (docs/system/examples/toggle/variant-glyph.tsx)

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";

export default function VariantGlyph() {
  return <Toggle variant="glyph" pressed icon="layer.unlocked" iconOn="layer.locked" tone="caution" ariaLabel="Outline locked" hint="Unlock" />;
}

Example: The text face: a word in capitals, on as the full ink on the faintest chip. (docs/system/examples/toggle/variant-text.tsx)

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";

export default function VariantText() {
  return (
    <Toggle variant="text" pressed ariaLabel="Grid" hint="Grid" shortcut="F7">
      Grid
    </Toggle>
  );
}

size

  • sm: the cell of a dense surface. A glyph is 20px wide at the 22px row height with the 12px glyph; a word is 11px type as tall as the line that holds it (--ui-toggle-line, the row height when nothing sets it). Used at 4 call sites (all of them).
  • md: the 24px control beside a field or an icon button, with the 14px glyph or 12px type; the default. Used at 0 call sites: the size for a toggle outside a list row or a bar, which no surface has yet.

Example: The 20 by 22 cell of a list row, with the 12px glyph. (docs/system/examples/toggle/size-sm.tsx)

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";

export default function SizeSm() {
  return <Toggle size="sm" pressed={false} icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" tone="info" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" hint="Freeze" />;
}

Example: The 24px control, with the 14px glyph. (docs/system/examples/toggle/size-md.tsx)

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";

export default function SizeMd() {
  return <Toggle size="md" pressed={false} icon="eye-off" iconOn="eye" ariaLabel="Preview" hint="Show the preview" />;
}

tone

  • neutral: on is the full ink (--text) over the quiet one, on a glyph and on a word (the word on its chip); the default, and the only tone of a text face. Used at 1 call site (the status bar's settings).
  • absent: on is the ordinary state and stays at the glyph ink; off is the one to notice and takes the ink. Used at 1 call site (a layer's on key).
  • info: on is a fact to notice. Used at 1 call site (a layer's frozen key).
  • caution: on blocks something. Used at 1 call site (a layer's locked key).

Example: Neutral: on is the full ink over the quiet one. (docs/system/examples/toggle/tone-neutral.tsx)

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";

export default function ToneNeutral() {
  return <Toggle tone="neutral" pressed icon="eye-off" iconOn="eye" ariaLabel="Preview" hint="Hide the preview" />;
}

Example: Absent: on is the ordinary state and stays quiet; off takes the ink. (docs/system/examples/toggle/tone-absent.tsx)

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";

export default function ToneAbsent() {
  return <Toggle tone="absent" size="sm" pressed={false} icon="layer.off" iconOn="layer.on" ariaLabel="Outline on" hint="Turn on" />;
}

Example: Info: on is a fact to notice, in the frozen ink. (docs/system/examples/toggle/tone-info.tsx)

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";

export default function ToneInfo() {
  return <Toggle tone="info" size="sm" pressed icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" hint="Thaw" />;
}

Example: Caution: on blocks something, in the locked ink. (docs/system/examples/toggle/tone-caution.tsx)

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";

export default function ToneCaution() {
  return <Toggle tone="caution" size="sm" pressed icon="layer.unlocked" iconOn="layer.locked" ariaLabel="Outline locked" hint="Unlock" />;
}

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by

Pressed (on)The caller passes pressed.Press it to ask for off.The on glyph (iconOn) with no fill, or the chip under the word and its full ink; aria-pressed="true".test

Example: The same toggle on: the on glyph in the full ink, no fill, announced pressed. (docs/system/examples/toggle/pressed.tsx)

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";

export default function Pressed() {
  return <Toggle pressed icon="eye-off" iconOn="eye" ariaLabel="Preview" hint="Hide the preview" />;
}

Example: A blocked toggle at the disabled ink, still focusable, saying why. (docs/system/examples/toggle/disabled.tsx)

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";

/** Disabled, and still reachable: the hint says what a press would do and `description` why it cannot. */
export default function Disabled() {
  return <Toggle pressed={false} disabled size="sm" tone="info" icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" hint="Freeze" description="The current layer cannot be frozen" />;
}

State precedence

  • Pressed and Hover: both show. An on glyph keeps its ink and gains the fill; an on word keeps its ink and its chip steps up to the .14 fill.
  • Rest and Hover: both show. The fill arrives, and the quiet ink steps up (a glyph to the full ink, a word to the secondary ink, so an off word under the pointer is never drawn as an on word at rest); an absent toggle that is off keeps its own ink, which is the state.
  • Held and Hover: Held wins. The .14 fill replaces the .08 one while the pointer is down (.20 replaces .14 on an on word).
  • Held and Pressed: both show. The on face stays while the fill is held.
  • Focused and Hover: both show. The ring stays drawn while the fill steps.
  • Focused and Pressed: both show. The ring is on the cell's edge and the state is in the face.
  • Focused and Held: both show. The ring stays drawn while the toggle is held down.
  • Hinted and Held: Held wins. The press puts the hint away.
  • Hinted and Hover: both show. The hint follows the hover after its delay.
  • Hinted and Focused: both show. The hint arrives with the ring, with no delay.
  • Hinted and Pressed: both show. The hint says what a press does now, in either state.
  • Hinted and Disabled: both show. A disabled toggle still says what it is for, and why it is blocked when it has a description.
  • Disabled and Hover: Disabled wins. No fill and no ink change under the pointer.
  • Disabled and Held: Disabled wins. No fill, and the press is refused.
  • Disabled and Pressed: both show. The on glyph stays at the disabled ink, or the word keeps a chip at the .08 fill, and aria-pressed still says the state.
  • Disabled and Focused: both show. A disabled toggle takes focus and the ring, so a keyboard user can reach its hint; Enter and Space do nothing.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
The pointer enters, presses or leaves, or the state changesinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-color, colorThe fill and the ink change at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition (the chip's too). The glyph swaps at once in every setting.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
pressedbooleanWhether the setting is on.
ariaLabel?stringThe fixed accessible name: the setting, not the action ("Outline frozen").
children?ElementThe word of a text face ("Grid").
description?stringA second line under the hint and the toggle's accessible description: why it is disabled.
disabled?booleanBlocks the press and drops the face to the disabled ink.
hint?stringThe hint, for the eye: what a press does now ("Thaw"), or the full name of a terse face.
icon?stringThe glyph shown while off, and while on when iconOn is not given: an id from ../icons.ts.
iconOn?stringThe glyph shown while on.
onChange?((pressed: boolean) => void)Runs on a press, with the state the press asks for.
onClick?((event: MouseEvent) => void)Runs on click, before onChange.
placement?TooltipPlacementThe side the hint prefers; it flips by itself when that side has no room.
shortcut?stringThe shortcut that flips the same setting, as the user reads it ("F9"): a key cap in the hint and aria-keyshortcuts on the button.
size?ToggleSizeThe box.
tabIndex?numberThe toggle's place in the Tab order, for a group that is one Tab stop.
tone?ToggleToneThe ink of the state worth noticing.
variant?ToggleVariantThe face.
  • pressed: whether the setting is on; the caller holds it. Sets aria-pressed.
  • onChange: runs with the state a press asks for. The toggle then shows what pressed says, so a change the caller refuses does not stay drawn.
  • onClick: runs on click, before onChange; a disabled toggle never fires either.
  • variant: the face; defaults to glyph.
  • icon: the glyph shown while off (and while on, when iconOn is not given): an id from src/icons.ts.
  • iconOn: the glyph shown while on.
  • tone: which state is the one to notice, and its ink; defaults to neutral. A text face is always neutral.
  • size: the box; defaults to md.
  • ariaLabel: the fixed accessible name: the setting, never the action. Required on a glyph; on a text face, the full name when the word is short for it.
  • hint: the layer's hint, for the eye only: what a press does now, or the full name of a terse word. It is not exposed to assistive tech, which has the name and the state. No native title attribute is rendered.
  • shortcut: the shortcut that flips the same setting, as the user reads it (F9): a key cap in the hint and aria-keyshortcuts on the button.
  • description: a second line under the hint, tied to the toggle as its accessible description (aria-describedby): why it is disabled.
  • placement: the side the hint prefers (top, bottom); it flips by itself when that side has no room.
  • disabled: blocks the press and drops the face to the disabled ink. It sets aria-disabled="true", never the native disabled, so the toggle stays in the Tab order and its hint still shows.
  • tabIndex: the toggle's place in the Tab order, for a group that is one Tab stop. Unset writes no attribute, so a container that roves through the element (rovingBand) is not undone.
  • children: the word of a text face.

Usage

When to use

  • A setting of the thing in front of the person is on or off and takes effect the moment it is pressed: a layer is frozen, the grid is shown.
  • Several such settings repeat down a list or along a bar: glyphs down a list, where a fill on each would be a column of fills, or short words along a bar, where the ones that are on are chips.

When not to use

  • The value is applied with a form, or can be mixed across several objects. Use Checkbox instead.
  • The glyph runs an action, opens a menu or folds a region. Use IconButton instead.
  • One switch on a tool bar should read as lit while on, with a fill. Use IconButton with selected instead.
  • The control brings one view of several to the front. Use Tab instead.

Rules

  • rule/toggle-name-fixed: When a toggle is rendered, pass 1 ariaLabel that names the setting and is the same string in both states, and put the action in hint, because aria-pressed already says the state, and a name that flips between Freeze and Thaw is heard as 2 different buttons. Evidence: app 3/3 layer state keys, src/components/LayersPanel.tsx. Check: test src/ui/Toggle.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Toggle icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel={frozen() ? "Thaw Outline" : "Freeze Outline"} pressed={frozen()} />
  • Do: <Toggle icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" hint={frozen() ? "Thaw" : "Freeze"} pressed={frozen()} />
  • rule/toggle-state-in-face: When a glyph toggle is rendered, pass 2 icons (icon for off, iconOn for on), because a glyph toggle draws no fill at rest and the ink alone would carry the state by colour only. Evidence: app 3/3 layer state keys pass both, src/components/LayersPanel.tsx. Check: review src/components/LayersPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <Toggle icon="layer.locked" tone="caution" ariaLabel="Outline locked" pressed={locked()} />
  • Do: <Toggle icon="layer.unlocked" iconOn="layer.locked" tone="caution" ariaLabel="Outline locked" pressed={locked()} />
  • rule/toggle-owns-nothing: When onChange runs, set the caller's own value from its argument (or refuse it), because the toggle draws from pressed after every press and keeps 0 state of its own. Evidence: single use src/ui/Toggle.tsx:97, the aria-pressed the prop sets. Check: test src/ui/Toggle.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Toggle icon="eye-off" iconOn="eye" ariaLabel="Preview" pressed={false} onChange={() => save()} />
  • Do: <Toggle icon="eye-off" iconOn="eye" ariaLabel="Preview" pressed={preview()} onChange={setPreview} />
  • rule/toggle-tone-meaning: When a tone is passed, pick it by which state the person must notice (absent for off, info or caution for on) and pass 1 tone per setting across the whole list, because the tone is the only colour in the column and a tone picked for looks makes 2 rows of the same setting read as different things. Evidence: app 3/3 layer state keys, each with its own tone on every row, src/components/LayersPanel.tsx. Check: review src/components/LayersPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <Toggle tone="caution" icon="layer.off" iconOn="layer.on" ariaLabel="Outline on" pressed={on()} /> — on is the ordinary state, and it would be drawn as a warning on every row.
  • Do: <Toggle tone="absent" icon="layer.off" iconOn="layer.on" ariaLabel="Outline on" pressed={on()} />
  • rule/toggle-group-one-stop: When more than 3 toggles stand in one bar, give the bar role="toolbar" with a name and make it 1 Tab stop (the container sets each tabIndex; the arrows, Home and End move), because 11 Tab stops in the status bar stand between the drawing and everything after it. Evidence: single use src/components/StatusBar.tsx:179, the toolbar that roves its 11 toggles. Check: review src/components/StatusBar.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="status-toggles"><Toggle variant="text" pressed={grid()}>Grid</Toggle>…</div> with 11 Tab stops.
  • Do: <div class="status-toggles" role="toolbar" aria-label="Drafting settings" ref={(el) => rovingBand(el, "button")}>…</div>
  • rule/toggle-no-native-title: When a toggle is styled or wrapped, add 0 hints of its own (no title attribute set from outside, no Tooltip around it), because the component already shows hint in the layer's hint box and a second hint stacks on the first. Evidence: app 38/38 toggles in the running shell render no title attribute, measured in the browser 2026-11-11. Check: test src/ui/Toggle.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tooltip text="Thaw"><Toggle icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" pressed /></Tooltip>
  • Do: <Toggle icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" hint="Thaw" pressed />
  • rule/toggle-disabled-reason: When a toggle is disabled by something the person can change, pass the reason as description in 1 short sentence, because the disabled toggle stays focusable for exactly this, and hint is not exposed to a screen reader. Evidence: single use src/ui/Toggle.tsx:91, the description tied to the button. Check: test src/ui/Toggle.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Toggle disabled icon="layer.thawed" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" hint="The current layer cannot be frozen" pressed={false} />
  • Do: <Toggle disabled icon="layer.thawed" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" hint="Freeze" description="The current layer cannot be frozen" pressed={false} />

Content

  • rule/toggle-label-setting: When ariaLabel is written, name the setting as a noun phrase of 1 to 4 words that is true while the toggle is pressed (Outline frozen, Snap mode), in sentence case, because it is read with "pressed" or "not pressed" after it, and a verb there reads as a command. Evidence: app 14/14 toggle names in the layer list and the status bar, src/components/StatusBar.tsx. Check: review src/components/StatusBar.tsx.
  • Don't: ariaLabel="Freeze the layer"
  • Do: ariaLabel="Outline frozen"
  • rule/toggle-text-short: When a text face is written, pass 1 word of at most 6 letters and the full name as ariaLabel and hint, because the bar holds 11 of them on one line at 1280 wide and the capitals are tracked. Evidence: app 11/11 status toggles ("Grid" to "OTrack", 2 to 6 letters), src/components/StatusBar.tsx. Check: review src/components/StatusBar.tsx.
  • Don't: <Toggle variant="text" pressed={on()}>Object snap tracking</Toggle>
  • Do: <Toggle variant="text" ariaLabel="Object snap tracking" hint="Object snap tracking" pressed={on()}>OTrack</Toggle>

Anti-slop

  • rule/toggle-canonical-element: When a surface needs an on-off key, render Toggle rather than a raw <button aria-pressed> with its own class, because the 2 replaced families (.toggle, .status-toggle) each carried their own hover, ring and state inks and neither had a disabled state or a touch target. Evidence: app 4/4 raw aria-pressed buttons in src/components/LayersPanel.tsx and src/components/StatusBar.tsx before 2026-11-11. Check: lint node scripts/check-system.mjs --root ..
  • Don't: <button class="toggle is-frozen" type="button" aria-pressed="true" aria-label="Outline frozen">…</button>
  • Do: <Toggle size="sm" tone="info" icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" pressed />
  • rule/toggle-no-fill: When a toggle should look on, pass pressed and add 0 background rules of the surface's own, because the glyph and its ink, or the word's own chip, already says so, and 1 fill per pressed glyph turns a list where nearly every row is on into a column of fills (an on word's chip is the component's own ::before, never the surface's). Evidence: measured 0 fills on the 38 toggle buttons of the running shell, in both states, 2026-11-11. Check: test src/ui/recipe.test.ts.
  • Don't: .layer-toggles .ui-toggle[aria-pressed="true"] { background: var(--fill-active) }
  • Do: <Toggle tone="info" icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" pressed />

Limits

  • rule/toggle-touch-target: When 2 sm glyph toggles sit side by side, keep at least 4px between them under a coarse pointer, because each 20px by 22px cell keeps its drawn size there and takes a 24px by 24px target from an invisible ::after, and cells closer than 4px overlap their targets. Evidence: measured 20px by 22px cell, src/ui/ui.css:1567. Check: review src/styles.css.
  • Don't: .layer-toggles { gap: 0 } on a touch screen.
  • Do: @media (pointer: coarse) { .layer-toggles { gap: var(--gap-4) } }
  • rule/toggle-line-height: When sm text toggles stand in a bar whose line is not 22px, set --ui-toggle-line on their container to the bar's line, because the word's target is the whole line and a 22px toggle in a 21px line makes the bar 1px taller. Evidence: measured 21px toggles in the 22px status bar under its 1px rule, in the browser, 2026-11-11. Check: review src/chrome.css.
  • Don't: .status-toggles .ui-toggle { height: 21px }
  • Do: .status-toggles { --ui-toggle-line: var(--status-line) }

Accessibility

Rests on the native <button> element with aria-pressed, the drawn glyph hidden from assistive tech. Disabled is the layer's own, shared with Button and IconButton: aria-disabled="true" with the click refused on the button itself (docs/system/decisions.md, "Disabled controls"). The state is never colour alone: the glyph changes, or the word's chip appears.

Related

  • IconButton: when the glyph runs an action, or one switch on a tool bar should read lit (selected).
  • Checkbox: when the yes-or-no is a form's value, or can be mixed.
  • Tab: when the control picks one view of several.
  • Tooltip: the hint box this component shows by itself; wrap another control in it, never this one.
  • Kbd: the key cap the hint draws for a shortcut.
  • Row: the list row a column of small glyph toggles sits beside; a row never nests them.
  • Dialog: where a setting's details are edited; the toggle only switches it.

Tooltip

Description

It is the layer's one hint: a small box beside a control under the pointer or under keyboard focus, saying what the control does not already show. One box serves the whole window. Any element asks for it by carrying data-hint: the layer's components set it from their title, the Tooltip wrapper sets it on a host around another control, and a surface's own element may carry the attribute itself. It is a hint, not the control: the control keeps its own element, its own pointer, its own accessible name and its own description.

import { Tooltip } from "../../../../src/ui/Tooltip";, source src/ui/Tooltip.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/button-div, trap/hover-unguarded, trap/touch-hover-flash.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the hover box is measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (docs/system/decisions.md, measured 2026-10-28): the chrome fill #141414, radius 3, the .15 hairline, the 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.4) shadow, 12px type, and the arrival over 0.1s. The placement, the delay, the dismissal, the key cap and the description are the layer's own (docs/system/decisions.md, "The hint").

Examples

<Tooltip text="Outline, the current layer"><span class="layer-name">Outline</span></Tooltip> — a hint over a control that is not a layer component.

Real uses, 1 call site (rg -c "<Tooltip" src/components → src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:1). The box itself is in use on every IconButton, Button, Chip, Tab, Field, Select, TextArea and Row that has something to say, without the wrapper. No component of the layer renders a native title attribute: Row, the last to do so, moved onto the box on 2026-11-11 (src/ui/recipe.test.ts holds every component's source to it).

  • src/components/LayersPanel.tsx — a layer row's hint.
  • src/components/StatusBar.tsx — the drafting toggles, outside the layer, carry data-hint and data-hint-keys (see "Adopting the hint outside the layer"); no native title is left in the shell.
