Example: The hint over a control of a surface's own. (docs/system/examples/tooltip/default.tsx)

import { Tooltip } from "../../../../src/ui/Tooltip";

/** A fact of the status bar: the hint says what the number counts. Layer components need no wrapper. */
export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Tooltip text="Objects in the drawing" placement="top">
      <span class="status-item status-count">46 objects</span>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}

Example: The full text of a clipped chat title. (docs/system/examples/tooltip/in-assistant-head.tsx)

import { Tooltip } from "../../../../src/ui/Tooltip";

/** The pane's header: a title that clips keeps its full text in the hint, on hover and on focus. */
export default function InAssistantHead() {
  const title = "Summarise the layers and count the objects on each";
  return (
    <Tooltip text={title} placement="bottom">
      <span class="assistant-title">{title}</span>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}

Example: A status-bar fact whose hint opens above it, with a key as a cap. (docs/system/examples/tooltip/in-status-bar.tsx)

import { Tooltip } from "../../../../src/ui/Tooltip";

/**
 * At the window's foot the box has no room below and opens above by itself; `placement="top"`
 * only says so up front. The shortcut is passed by itself and drawn as a key cap, never written
 * into the text in brackets.
 */
export default function InStatusBar() {
  return (
    <Tooltip text="Snap Mode" shortcut="F9" placement="top">
      <span class="status-item">Snap on</span>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}

Variants

One shape. The box prefers the side below the control and takes the side above with placement="top"; either way it flips to the other side when the preferred one has no room (a status-bar control's hint opens above it), and slides along the window's edge rather than cross it.

What the box holds comes from three attributes on the element that asks:

AttributeHoldsDrawn as
data-hintThe hint's text.The first line.
data-hint-keysThe control's shortcut as the user reads it (Ctrl+Z, F9).One Kbd key cap after the text.
data-hint-noteA second thought: why the control is disabled, what it will do.A second line in the quieter ink.
data-hint-labelOn one element inside the control: the label the control shows, where the control's own text holds more than that label (Select holds every choice and shows one). No value.Nothing by itself: it is the text a clipped control's hint reads in full, and the text a repeated hint is compared with.
data-hint-placementtop to prefer the side above.—

A control whose label is clipped by its own box (scrollWidth past clientWidth, on the element or the label directly inside it) gets its full label as the first line by itself, and what data-hint adds drops to the second line. The label is the marked one (data-hint-label), else the part that is cut (a row's label, without the shortcut beside it), else everything the control shows; a field's label is its value, never a password's; and a part hidden from assistive tech (aria-hidden="true") is skipped, so a name drawn in pieces beside its whole text reads once.

A host that carries data-hint empty (a layer component with no title, there for its clipped label) gives way to a host around it that has words: a Tooltip wrapped around a Row still speaks. A hint that only repeats the label the control shows (compared trimmed, white space collapsed), with no shortcut and no note, is not drawn.

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestThe pointer is away and keyboard focus is elsewhere, or the control's hint has nothing to add.Use the control.The box is opacity: 0; visibility: hidden and takes no pointer.test
ShownA mouse or a pen rests on the host for 0.4s (at once, and without the fade, when another hint was up within the last 0.3s), or a key moves focus onto the host (Tab, an arrow key, Home, End, Page Up, Page Down, F6). Never a finger, and never focus that arrived by a click or was handed back by a closing dialog.Read the hint; the control keeps the pointer.The box fades in over 0.1s beside the host, inside the window's edges.test
DismissedEscape, a press, a click, typing, a scroll, a resize, the window losing focus, or any key in a <select> but Tab and a bare modifier (its list opens where the box sits), while the box is shown or waiting to show.Use the control; move the pointer or the focus to another control to see a hint again.The box is gone at once and stays away while the pointer rests on the same host.test
Held backThe host has its own menu or dialog open (aria-haspopup with aria-expanded="true"), or focus is inside a menu or a dialog the host is not part of.Use the menu or the dialog.No box. A control inside the open menu or dialog still hints.test

State precedence

  • Shown and Dismissed: Dismissed wins. A dismissed hint does not come back until the pointer or the focus moves to another control.
  • Shown and Held back: Held back wins. No hint draws over, or behind, the popup the person is using.
  • Dismissed and Held back: Not applicable: both draw nothing.
  • Rest and Shown: Not applicable: the box is one or the other.
  • Rest and Dismissed: Not applicable: both draw nothing.
  • Rest and Held back: Not applicable: both draw nothing.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
childrenElementThe control the hint describes.
textstringThe hint.
placement?TooltipPlacementThe side the box prefers: bottom (the default, where the platform's own hint falls, clear of the bar above a tool row) or top.
shortcut?stringThe control's shortcut as the user reads it ("Ctrl+Z", "F9"): a key cap after the text.
  • text: the hint. A short fragment: "New chat", "Copy the code".
  • shortcut: the control's shortcut as the user reads it (Ctrl+Z, F9); the box draws it as a key cap after the text. Sets data-hint-keys on the host.
  • placement: the side the box prefers, bottom (the default) or top. It flips to the other side when the preferred one has no room.
  • children: the control the hint describes. Give it its own aria-label or visible text — the hint is not the name. Not a layer component: those carry the hint themselves.

Beside the component, src/ui/Tooltip.tsx exports what a surface needs to adopt the hint without the wrapper: installHints() (wires the document once; every layer component calls it), describeByHint(el, text) (ties a hint to a control as its accessible description, from the control's ref), splitHint(title) and ariaKeyShortcuts(keys).

Adopting the hint outside the layer

A surface's own element (a status toggle, a layer key, a clipped value) moves off the native title in three steps, and needs no wrapper and no import unless it has a description to tie:

  1. Rename title to data-hint, and take a shortcut out of the text into data-hint-keys: title="Snap Mode (F9)" becomes data-hint="Snap Mode" data-hint-keys="F9". Leave no title behind. The attributes alone do not split a bracket: only IconButton and Button do that, for their existing call sites.
  2. Settle the accessible name, which the native title may have been supplying. An element with no visible text (an icon key, a colour swatch) takes the same words as aria-label. An element whose visible text is terse (SNAP) takes the full words as aria-label. An element whose visible text is already its name takes nothing.
  3. Settle the description. When the hint says more than the name and a screen-reader user needs it too (why a control is disabled, what a toggle does), tie it: ref={(el) => describeByHint(el, () => hint())}. When the hint is the element's own clipped text, tie nothing: the full text is already in the element, and the layer shows it by itself (data-hint="" is enough to opt a clipped value in). A shortcut goes on aria-keyshortcuts={ariaKeyShortcuts("F9")}.

A fact that is not a control (a <span>) takes no keyboard focus, so its hint is pointer-only: put nothing there that a keyboard user needs.

Usage

When to use

  • A control that is not a layer component needs a short hint: a toggle with a terse face, a key with a shortcut to teach.
  • A truncated value needs its full text on hover and on focus.
  • A disabled control needs to say why.

When not to use

  • The control is an icon-only action. Use IconButton instead: its title already shows in this box.
  • The control is already a layer component with a label. Use Button with its own title instead (and the same on Chip, Tab and Field): it already shows in this box.
  • The text is the control's only name. Use Button with a visible label instead.
  • The content is rich, interactive or long. Use Row rows inside a menu instead.

Rules

  • rule/tooltip-not-a-name: When a control carries a tooltip, give the control its own aria-label or visible text, because the box is aria-hidden and a control named only by its hint has 0 names for a screen reader. Evidence: single use src/ui/Tooltip.tsx:243, aria-hidden="true" on the box. Check: test src/ui/Tooltip.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tooltip text="Close"><button>✕</button></Tooltip>
  • Do: <Tooltip text="Close the panel"><button aria-label="Close the panel">✕</button></Tooltip>
  • rule/tooltip-never-blocks: When the tooltip shows, the box keeps pointer-events: none, because it sits beside the control and a hint that takes the click is worse than 0 hints. Evidence: single use src/ui/ui.css:1502, pointer-events: none on the box. Check: test src/ui/recipe.test.ts.
  • Don't: a tooltip box with a hover handler of its own.
  • Do: pointer-events: none on .ui-tooltip.
  • rule/tooltip-no-touch: When the pointer is a finger, show 0 hints, because a finger has no hover and a tap would leave the box up over the control it just pressed. Evidence: single use src/ui/Tooltip.tsx:327, the pointerType === "touch" guard. Check: test src/ui/Tooltip.test.tsx.
  • Don't: a hint that carries an instruction a touch user needs ("Hold to record").
  • Do: the instruction in the control's label or beside it, and the hint only as a repeat.
  • rule/tooltip-adds: When a hint is written for a control with a visible label, write what the label leaves out and 0 words that repeat it, because the layer draws no box for a hint equal to the label and a description equal to the name is read twice. Evidence: single use src/ui/Tooltip.tsx:203, the comparison of the hint with the label the control shows. Check: test src/ui/Tooltip.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tooltip text="Check connection"><button type="button">Check connection</button></Tooltip>
  • Do: <Tooltip text="Check the address and the key"><button type="button">Check connection</button></Tooltip>
  • rule/tooltip-shortcut-cap: When a hint teaches a shortcut, pass it by itself (shortcut, data-hint-keys) and keep it out of the text, because the box draws 1 key cap for it and text in brackets is read as part of the sentence. Evidence: app 9/31 icon buttons in the running shell end their title in a bracketed shortcut, which IconButton and Button still split off for them, measured in the browser 2026-11-11. Check: test src/ui/Tooltip.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <button data-hint="Snap Mode (F9)" aria-label="Snap Mode">SNAP</button>
  • Do: <button data-hint="Snap Mode" data-hint-keys="F9" aria-label="Snap Mode" aria-keyshortcuts="F9">SNAP</button>

Content

  • rule/tooltip-text-fragment: When the hint's text is written, keep it a fragment of 1 to 4 words in sentence case with no full stop ("Copy the code", not "Click here to copy."), because the box is one 24px line for a fragment and a sentence is read as a paragraph; a reason a control is disabled is the exception and is 1 sentence. Evidence: app 31/31 icon button hints in the running shell are 4 words or fewer before the bracket, measured in the browser 2026-11-11. Check: review src/components/ToolStrip.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tooltip text="This button will close the assistant panel.">
  • Do: <Tooltip text="Close the panel">

Anti-slop

  • rule/tooltip-one-hint: When a control shows this hint, keep it the control's 1 hint: move the text out of the native title into text or data-hint, and leave a layer component unwrapped, because two hints stack: the platform's box arrives on its own delay over the layer's, and a layer component already shows its own. Evidence: app 31/31 icon buttons in the running shell render no title attribute, measured in the browser 2026-11-11. Check: test src/ui/Tooltip.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tooltip text="Snap Mode"><button title="Snap Mode (F9)">Snap</button></Tooltip>
  • Do: <Tooltip text="Snap Mode" shortcut="F9"><button aria-label="Snap Mode">Snap</button></Tooltip>

Limits

  • rule/tooltip-length-limit: When a hint runs past 64 characters, move the explanation into the control's label or help text, because the box wraps at a 32ch measure (207px at 12px type) and a third line reads as a paragraph over the surface it covers. Evidence: measured 207px by 40px box, 2 lines, for the 46-character "To save, choose a provider or type a base URL." at 1280px and at 390px, src/ui/ui.css:1487. Check: test src/ui/recipe.test.ts.
  • Don't: a 120-character hint over the composer.
  • Do: a 3-word hint and a visible line of help for the rest.

Accessibility

The box is for the eye and is hidden from assistive tech; the same words reach a screen reader through the control. Where the hint is the control's name (an icon key), the name is on aria-label. Where the control has a visible label and the hint adds to it, the hint is the control's description: describeByHint keeps the words in a hidden line on <body> and points aria-describedby at it. aria-describedby rather than aria-description, because the second is an ARIA 1.3 draft attribute and the desktop app runs in whatever system webview the machine has (docs/system/decisions.md, "The hint"). The host of the wrapper is a plain <span>, so the child's semantics are unchanged. It meets WCAG 1.4.13 as dismissable (Escape) and persistent (it stays while the pointer or the focus does); it is not hoverable, which the criterion allows for a box that only repeats what the control's own name and description say and takes no pointer.

Related

  • IconButton: shows this box by itself from its title, shortcut and description; never wrap one.
  • Button: shows this box from its title, which is its description; never wrap one.
  • Tab: shows its clipped label in this box by itself.
  • Chip: the pickable keyword form; its title shows here.
  • Field: its title shows here and joins its description.
  • Kbd: the key cap the box draws for a shortcut; and the pick when the key should stay on the surface rather than show on hover.
  • Dialog: when the content is a task with controls rather than a hint.

rule/inline-pxA px, rem or em length for spacing, radius, size or font size in an inline stylenone yetscripts/check-system.mjs

rule/select-touch-targetWhen a size="sm" select sits in a list row of 22px, give the row a min-height rather than a fixed height, because under a coarse pointer the box grows from 20px to 24px and a row fixed at 22px would cut it.components/selectmeasuredreview src/ui/ui.css
rule/stock-editA ui file on the drift list (stock, customized or forked) changed since its hash was recordednone yetscripts/check-system.mjs

What the check can't see

A reviewer or a browser covers these. Passing cd apps/ui && bun run check says nothing about them.

  • Rendered contrast, including non-text contrast of borders, focus rings and checkbox edges. Measure it in a browser.
  • Behavior: what a click, Enter or Escape does, focus order and focus return, and whether Cancel submits.
  • Layout at each viewport, overflow at 390px and touch target sizes.
  • Visual overrides on components the registry does not list, and overrides built at runtime: cn() branches, spread props, a class name held in a variable.
  • A loading state shown some other way than a label ternary on the button, such as a label read from a variable.
  • Class names and values built at runtime, such as template strings, cn() branches or fontSize: size / 2.5.
  • bg-white and text-black when the theme defines no role for their job, their opacity forms such as bg-black/50, and CSS keywords such as white in var() fallbacks.
  • Files outside the include folders, and ui files missing from the drift list (they are scanned, but no hash guards them).
  • Whether a token's role comment still matches how the token is used.
  • Rules the generated rules page marks review, or enforces only through their own Check: clause.
  • Motion that is only measured: exit slower than enter, frequent-surface motion, linear easing, press delay, input lag and jank. Easing set in script or through a variable, and hover reveals written as Tailwind classes (v4 guards hover: itself, v3 does not).
  • Whether a pressed style covers the control whose tap highlight was removed: any pressed style in the repo passes trap/touch-tap-highlight.

The web system's design decisions

The lock for the SolidJS UI (apps/ui), taken in the design-system run of 2026-10-28. The design source is the running Cursor 3.27.22 desktop app, measured live (.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md). The values live in src/tokens.css; this file records the picks and the reasons, so the next surface does not re-litigate them.

Canonical picks

The web UI grows fourteen canonical components under src/ui/, each a thin wrapper over the native element. The per-surface hand-rolled classes they replace are named below; a class loses because it is a one-off with no shared API and no states.

  • Button — pick ui/Button.tsx (native <button>). Variants primary | secondary | ghost | quiet | danger, default secondary (Cursor's own default button); quiet joined on 2026-11-12 ("Inside a field, and the last two inputs" below). Loses: .button (TopBar — one call site), .assistant-send / .assistant-save / .assistant-ghost (assistant-only, their own colours), .assistant-preset (a suggestion chip wearing a button), .tool-button (ToolStrip — a grid cell, no variants), .menu-row (a menu item, not a general button).
  • IconButton — pick ui/IconButton.tsx (native <button>, a drawn icon + label). Variants ghost | soft | inverted; sizes md (24px) and sm (20px). Loses: .assistant-icon (three uses, fixed 24px, no variant), .assistant-attachment-x (one-off). The layer list's state keys and the status bar's drafting toggles were listed here as its losers until 2026-11-11 and never moved: they are Toggle's (below).
  • Chip — pick ui/Chip.tsx (native <button> when interactive, <span> when not). Loses: .chip (TopBar — a static fact, no interaction), .keyword-chip (CommandLine — interactive, no tone/size API), .cmd-chips (a container, not a chip).
  • Field — pick ui/Field.tsx (native <input>, single-line). Variants field | inline | bare, sizes md (24px) and sm (20px), align start | end, as Select ("A value in a dense row" below), and an adornment inside either end (start, end). .cmd-input and the palette's .palette-input moved onto it on 2026-11-12. Loses: .assistant-input, .cmd-input, .prop-input (each one surface's own padding and border), .assistant-field (a label wrapper, not the control). The composer's auto-growing <textarea> and the properties palette's <select> were found-not-fixed here until 2026-11-11; TextArea and Select below are their picks.
  • Select — pick ui/Select.tsx (a native <select> under a drawn face: keyboard, type-ahead, a phone's picker and every system webview's own list are the platform's; no hand-built listbox). Variants field | inline, sizes md (24px) and sm (20px), align start | end. The value is drawn in a <span> over the control, which is what lets it end in an ellipsis before the arrow, end on the arrow's side and read quieter while mixed the same way in all three webviews. Loses: .prop-select (PropertiesPanel — appearance: none with no arrow drawn in its place, a long value cut with no ellipsis, the off-list option and the *VARIES* ink done by hand).
  • Checkbox — pick ui/Checkbox.tsx (a native <input type="checkbox"> inside its <label>, the box and the mark drawn from tokens). No variants; states checked, mixed, disabled. Loses: .prop-check (PropertiesPanel — the platform's own box tinted with accent-color, a different shape and tick in each webview, 13px with no touch target).
  • TextArea — pick ui/TextArea.tsx (a native <textarea> that measures its own height between rows and maxRows). Variants field | bare. Loses: .assistant-input with its grow function (AssistantPane — the limits fixed at 64px and 240px beside a type size that can change).
  • Row — pick ui/Row.tsx (native <button>, the full-width clickable band). Loses: .prop-row, .menu-row (moved on 2026-11-11: "A row in a menu" below), .assistant-row, .assistant-tool (each repeats hover/selected padding by hand). A grid row carrying nested controls of its own (.layer-row with its toggle cluster) stays bespoke — a button cannot nest buttons. The pilot kept .assistant-row (the composer's toolbar is a container with nested buttons) and .assistant-tool (a transcript disclosure row, not a menu band) bespoke for the same reason; row.md records it. Inside a role="listbox" that keeps the keyboard in its own field, the row is <Row option>: the role="option" element itself, with no Tab stop and no hover fill of its own ("A row in a listbox" below). Loses there: .palette-option (CommandPalette — a wrapper div carrying the option role around a Row button).
  • SectionLabel — pick ui/SectionLabel.tsx (native <h2> — a heading, so a screen reader can jump between panels). Loses: .section-label (already shared but untyped — the pick is its typed home), .properties-head / .layers-head (the surrounding bar, not the label), .assistant-title (a pane title, a different role).
  • Tooltip — pick ui/Tooltip.tsx: the layer's one hint, a single box on <body> placed beside whichever control carries data-hint. Every layer component that takes title carries it; the <Tooltip> wrapper (a <span> host; the child keeps its own element and its own accessible name) and the bare data-hint attribute give it to a surface's own element. Placements bottom | top, flipped and held inside the window by itself; it never takes the pointer. Loses: the native title attribute as an icon key's hint (it arrives on the platform's own delay, in the platform's own box, and never on keyboard focus), and any per-surface hover label a panel would draw for itself. The reasons are under "The hint" below.
  • Tab — pick ui/Tab.tsx (native <button> with role="tab", aria-selected on the one in front; an optional close key as a sibling button). Sizes md (the editor tab, selected at --tab-active) and sm (the compact tab of a pane header, selected at --fill-active). Loses: .layout-tab (StatusBar's layout strip — a raw button with its own class), the chat tabs' Row workaround (AssistantPane — a Row in a width cell beside a close IconButton).
  • Toggle — pick ui/Toggle.tsx (native <button aria-pressed>, the state drawn by the face alone). Variants glyph | text; sizes sm (the cell of a 22px row, the status bar's line) and md (24px); tones neutral | absent | info | caution. Loses: .toggle with .is-on / .is-frozen / .is-locked (LayersPanel — three raw buttons per row, the tone picked by :first-child and a class), .status-toggle (StatusBar — a raw button with its own hover, ring and on rule). The reasons are under "A setting switched in place" below.
  • Dialog — pick ui/Dialog.tsx (a native <dialog> opened with showModal(): the focus trap, Escape, the inert page and the top layer are the platform's). Sizes sm | md | lg; a title bar with a close key, a body that scrolls, a footer of actions. Loses: nothing drawn by hand, because the web interface had no dialog (the removed desktop interface's Options, Drafting Settings and Layer Properties Manager were never rebuilt); the command palette's own <dialog> and the assistant's setup sheet stay as they are. The reasons are under "A task over the page" below. With it, ui/Tab.tsx grows TabPanels, the tabs pattern with panels, for a dialog's pages.
  • Kbd — pick ui/Kbd.tsx (native <kbd>, one recipe, no variants). Loses: .assistant-key (AssistantPane — the mono face at the disabled ink), .palette-key (CommandPalette — the recipe kept, now the pick's own).

Prop vocabulary

  • variant: primary | secondary | ghost | quiet | danger (default secondary) — purpose, not appearance. quiet is the action that must read after the text it stands beside; it is a value of variant and not a tone on ghost, because a second prop would give the button two axes of emphasis and four of their eight pairs would mean nothing (a quiet primary).
  • size: sm | md (default md).
  • plus disabled, selected, title.
  • IconButton expanded and controls: a fold key says whether the region it folds is showing (aria-expanded) and which region it is (aria-controls, the region's id). A key is a fold key or a selected toggle, never both.
  • IconButton popup: menu | dialog | listbox (aria-haspopup), beside expanded and controls, on a key that opens something floating over the page. menu when what opens is a list of actions (role="menu": the narrow window's Main menu), listbox when it is a list of values to pick one from (role="listbox": a model picker), dialog when it holds fields or other controls (role="dialog": the provider form). A fold key that shows a region in the page's own flow takes no popup.
  • title is the layer's hint on every component that takes it, and no component renders a native title attribute. What it is to assistive tech depends on whether the control has a visible label: on IconButton (a glyph, no label) it is the name (aria-label); on Button, Chip, Tab, Row, Field, Select and TextArea (a label, or ariaLabel) it is the description (aria-describedby), never the name. "The hint" below has the reasons.
  • Button and IconButton shortcut: the shortcut as the user reads it (Ctrl+Z), drawn as a key cap in the hint and said through aria-keyshortcuts. data-hint-keys is the same thing on an element outside the layer.
  • IconButton description: the second line of the hint and the key's accessible description (aria-describedby): why it is disabled, what it will do. Button needs no such prop: its title already is its description.
  • disabled on Button and IconButton is aria-disabled="true", never the native attribute ("Disabled controls" below). Field, Select, Checkbox, TextArea and Row keep the native disabled; a Row option is not a native control and says aria-disabled="true", and a Row menuitem says it too, because a menu's arrow keys must still reach a command that cannot run ("A row in a menu" below).
  • Field autocomplete and spellcheck: the native attributes, passed through; unset leaves each to the platform, except that a password field is never spell-checked. A secret passes autocomplete="off" and spellcheck={false} whatever type it shows at the moment.
  • Field invalid and describedBy: a refused value says so (aria-invalid="true", the error stroke), and the help line or the error line under a field is tied to it by id (aria-describedby). describedBy is the layer's name for that tie on any component that grows one, as ariaLabel is for the name.
  • Button ariaLabel (the name Field already uses for the same job): the accessible name, only where the visible label is a value rather than the action; it starts with the action and holds the visible text.
  • ariaLabel, describedBy, invalid and title mean on Select and TextArea what they mean on Field; Checkbox takes ariaLabel (when it has no visible label) and describedBy.
  • variant on the value controls names where the control sits, not how it looks: Select and Field field | inline (a form control; a value in a dense list row that reads as text until touched), TextArea and Field field | bare (a form control; the editor inside a box a surface draws, which shows the focus itself).
  • Field start and end: an adornment inside the field's leading or trailing end, as an element. A glyph that says what the value is, or one IconButton size="sm" that acts on it. The field makes room for it; a surface never positions one over a field from outside.
  • Field autocapitalize: the native attribute, passed through, as autocomplete and spellcheck are.
  • Select and Field align: start | end, the side of the box the value sits on (end in a column of values; on Field it also sets lining tabular figures, so a column of numbers lines up).
  • mixed (Select, Checkbox, Field): the control stands for several things whose values differ. Select shows its placeholder, which is never a choice; Checkbox sets indeterminate and aria-checked="mixed"; Field draws the stand-in the caller passes as its value in the quiet ink.
  • Field readOnly, maxLength, inputMode: the native attributes, passed through. readOnly is not disabled: the value can be focused, selected and copied.
  • Field selectOnFocus: the whole value is selected as focus arrives, by key or by click, so typing replaces it; a second click places the caret.
  • Field onKeyDown, onFocus, onBlur, ref: the pass-throughs a value that commits on Enter and on leaving needs. onKeyDown never hears a key an input method is using, as on TextArea.
  • role, expanded, controls, activeDescendant, autocompleteKind (Field, TextArea): a text control that drives a list of matches and keeps the keyboard is a combobox. role takes only combobox; expanded and controls mean what they mean on IconButton (aria-expanded, aria-controls); activeDescendant is the id of the option the arrow keys are on (aria-activedescendant); autocompleteKind is aria-autocomplete (list | inline | both | none), named apart from autocomplete, which is the platform's autofill. They are passed together or not at all: on Field for as long as the field exists (the palette's input), on TextArea only while its list shows (the composer's slash list), and Row option rows are the list.
  • onChange(value) on a control whose value is picked (Select, Checkbox) and onInput(value) on one whose value is typed (Field, TextArea): each hands back the value, not the event. The caller owns the value on all four, and Select and Checkbox redraw from their props after every pick, so a change the caller refuses does not stay drawn.
  • Select options: the choices as data ({ value, label, disabled? }[]), never children; a value that is not among them is listed first by the component.
  • TextArea rows and maxRows: the fewest lines shown and the most before it scrolls; the height between is measured, and no stylesheet sets one.
  • TextArea onKeyDown, onPaste, ref: the pass-throughs a composer needs. onKeyDown never hears a key an input method is using.
  • Row option, with id and onPointerMove: the row is one option of a listbox that owns the focus and the highlight.
  • Row menuitem, with popup, expanded, describedBy, onKeyDown and onPointerEnter: the row is one item of a menu that moves the focus itself. popup and expanded mean what they mean on IconButton (popup takes only menu here), and describedBy what it means on Field.
  • Row title: the hint and the row's description in every form, as on Button; the name stays the row's text.
  • Chip tone: neutral | accent.
  • Toggle pressed and onChange(pressed): the state and the state a press asks for, as checked and onChange on Checkbox; the caller owns it. selected stays IconButton's word for a key that is lit while on.
  • Toggle ariaLabel and hint: the fixed name and the hint are two props because they are two strings ("Outline frozen", "Thaw"). title is not taken: on every other component it is the hint and also the name or the description, and a toggle's hint is neither. description, shortcut and disabled mean what they mean on IconButton, and placement what it means on Tooltip.
  • Toggle variant: glyph | text, the face. Toggle tone: neutral | absent | info | caution, which state is the one to notice and its ink; it names the meaning, and the token layer picks the colour per theme.
  • Toggle icon and iconOn: the glyph of each state. Toggle tabIndex: the one pass-through for a group that is one Tab stop; unset, the component writes no attribute.
  • Dialog open and onClose(reason): the caller owns whether the dialog shows, as it owns every value in the layer; the dialog only asks, and says why (escape | backdrop | close | action). title on Dialog is its visible title and its accessible name, not a hint: a dialog has no hint, and the one string is what the title bar shows and what aria-labelledby names.
  • Dialog describedBy: what it means on Field (aria-describedby). The brief that asked for the component called it ariaDescribedBy; the layer already had a name for the tie, and a second name for it would be the first prop to break "one name per job".
  • Dialog initialFocus (a selector, an element or a function), footer (the actions, or a function handed done) and dismissOnBackdrop (default true).
  • Dialog size: sm | md | lg. The layer's other components stop at sm | md; a dialog's third step is a width, not a control height, and it is the only component that has one.
  • Field, Select, TextArea and Checkbox id: the control's id, for a visible <label for> beside it. A form in a dialog shows its labels, and ariaLabel beside a visible label would say the name twice in two places that can drift. TextArea and Checkbox took it on 2026-11-12: a text area's label is as often around it as beside it (the composer's card), and a checkbox whose label is its children needs none, but one named by a row's label in another column does.
  • Tab id, controls, tabIndex: what a tab with a panel needs (aria-labelledby back from the panel, aria-controls, one Tab stop per strip). TabPanels sets all three; a bare strip may.
  • No boolean style props (round, big, blue): a prop names a purpose; the token layer picks the look.

Motion presets

One job, one preset (durations and easings from tokens.css):

  • press → --dur-press + --ease-standard: the transform channel only (the icon button's scale to .98). A fill that changes under a press takes the hover preset.
  • hover / focus feedback → --dur-fast + --ease-standard: the measured state transition, .1s ease (research §8: 24 declarations in the glass UI, and the button families' color, background-color channels). This line read --ease-out until 2026-11-11; the measurement and src/tokens.css say ease, the layer (src/ui/ui.css) already drew it, and the page was the side that moved.
  • open (menu, popover, composer focus) → --dur-med + --ease-out-quint.
  • close → --dur-fast + --ease-out.
  • panel / larger change → --dur-slow + --ease-out. Reserved: no panel moves yet, and --dur-slow is kept in src/tokens.css for this line alone, so the first panel that moves does not pick its own duration.
  • hint → arrives on the hover / focus preset (opacity), leaves at once. The wait before it is script, not a token: 0.4s under a resting pointer, none on keyboard focus, none for 0.3s after another hint went away; and that next hint arrives without the fade too, because a fade restarting on every key of a row is a flicker.
  • Reduced motion: the app's data-animations attribute already gates motion; the presets keep it — no preset plays when animations are off. The hint also answers the platform's own setting (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce): it is a box the layer hangs on <body> for every surface, so it does not wait for the shell to mirror the setting into the attribute.

Icon sizes

  • 14px glyph in a 24px control — icon buttons.
  • 16px glyph in a 28px control — tool strip / buttons.
  • 12px glyph in a 20px control — chips.
  • Icons stay code-drawn (src/icons.ts); no new icon assets (project rule: no third-party iconography).

What follows the drawing

Tokens left untouched because they describe the document, not the chrome: --canvas, --grid-minor, --grid-major, --axis-x, --axis-y, --icon-layer-*, --icon-locked, --control, --control-hover, --cmd-bg, --cmd-border, and the dark --warn / --error / --toggle-on (already Cursor's, §1). History: --layer-current stood in this list until 2026-11-11 ("The quiet pass" below removed it), --swatch-border stood in it until the same day (it frames a colour of the document but is itself chrome: "Token decisions" above), and the light --control, --control-hover, --cmd-bg and --cmd-border were retuned in the same pass. Geometry that was not re-measured also stays: --dur-med, --ease-out, the other radii, the gaps, control heights, fonts. src/canvas.ts reads the model-space colours (--canvas, --grid-*, --axis-*, --selection) from the CSS custom properties at runtime, so the drawing and the chrome cannot drift.

Removed tokens

Removed on 2026-11-11 from both themes of src/tokens.css and from every page that listed them. Each was searched for by its bare name (with and without var() over src/ (CSS, TS, TSX, the canvas renderer's getPropertyValue reads), index.html, crates/wasm/src, crates/render/src and apps/cadcraft/src, and nothing drew it. A token with no reader is a value nobody checks: it drifts (the light --icon-point had been corrected for contrast on a glyph no surface drew) and it invites a second way to do a thing the layer already does.
