about the next panel that moves, and the decision still stands, so its duration stays.

  • --list-bg: no rule paints it, but src/ui/recipe.test.ts and scripts/contrast-report.mjs

hold every ink to its threshold over it as the command list's surface. It goes when the command list is settled on --surface-elevated, with the two surface lists.

The hint

Decided 2026-11-11. Tooltip had 0 call sites: its only two users had become IconButtons, which showed a native title, and rule/tooltip-one-hint forbids both together. The choice was to retire the component or to make it the hint IconButton shows. It is the hint, for these reasons:

  • A native title never shows on keyboard focus, so a keyboard user of a tool strip of 25 glyphs

had no way to read what a key does short of a screen reader. The layer's box shows at once on focus.

  • The native box is the platform's: its own delay, its own face, in neither theme. One styled hint

everywhere is the measured Cursor box the layer already carried and nothing drew.

  • It costs the call sites nothing: IconButton already took the string as title.

How it is built, and why:

  • One box on <body>, in the viewport's coordinates, not a child of each control: the tool

strip, the sidebar and the assistant's panes clip their overflow, and a box inside them would be cut at the pane's edge. It also keeps IconButton a single <button>, so no surface's layout or selector changes.

  • Placed by script: below the control (where the platform's hint fell, clear of the menu bar

above the tool strip), above it when there is no room below, and slid along the window's edge rather than across it. placement on the wrapper only names the preferred side; the align prop is gone, because the hold inside the window does its job without the caller knowing where the control sits.

  • Timing: 0.4s under a resting mouse or pen; at once when another hint went away within 0.3s,

so sweeping the strip reads every key; at once on keyboard focus (focus a key moved, so a click's focus does not raise it; the second pass below replaced the first pass's :focus-visible test); never under a finger, which has no hover.

  • Dismissal: Escape, a press, a click, typing, a scroll, a resize and the window losing focus put it

away, and it stays away until the pointer or the focus moves to another control. Escape is not consumed: a menu that closes on Escape still closes.

  • Hidden from assistive tech (aria-hidden): the box repeats the aria-label, and a second

announcement of the same words is noise. It is not a role="tooltip" description.

  • The name stays on aria-label, and no native title is rendered, so the two hints cannot

stack.

One hint in the whole layer (2026-11-11, second pass)

Button, Chip, Tab and Field moved onto the box with no call-site change: each still takes title, and none renders the native attribute. What moved with them:

  • The name and the description, per component. The hint is the name only where there is no

other (IconButton: aria-label). A Button, a Chip or a Tab has a visible label and a Field has ariaLabel, so there the hint is supplementary and is exposed as the control's description. It must be exposed somehow: the box is aria-hidden, and with the native title gone a screen reader would otherwise lose the words (the reason Save is disabled, what a tab switches to). A static Chip is a <span> with no role, where a description is not announced; its hint is for the eye only and its spec says to put nothing essential there.

  • aria-describedby, not aria-description. aria-description is one attribute and no

machinery, but it is an ARIA 1.3 working-draft attribute, and the desktop app runs in whatever system webview the machine has (WebKit on macOS, WebView2 on Windows, WebKitGTK on Linux), which is not evergreen everywhere. aria-describedby pointing at text is supported by every engine and screen reader pairing. The text lives in one hidden element on <body> (.ui-hint-descriptions, one <span> per control, removed with it), not beside the control: a hidden child would enter textContent and a hidden sibling would change every surface's :first-child, + and flex-gap arithmetic. A hidden element referenced by aria-describedby is still read as the description. describeByHint in src/ui/Tooltip.tsx is the one place that does this, and a surface's own element can call it.

  • A repeat is nothing. A hint equal to the label the control shows (trimmed, white space

collapsed) with no shortcut and no second line draws no box and adds no description: the chat tabs pass their title as both, and "hello, tab, hello" helps nobody.

  • A clipped label is always reachable. When a control's own box cuts its label (scrollWidth

past clientWidth), the hint's first line is the full label, whether or not the caller passed title, and what title adds drops to a second line. Tab and Chip always carry data-hint (empty when there is no title) so this works without the caller thinking of it. Assistive tech never needed it: the full text is in the element, and the ellipsis is paint.

  • The shortcut is a key cap. The explicit form is the one to write: shortcut on IconButton

and Button, data-hint-keys on any other element; it also sets aria-keyshortcuts. The old form, a title ending "(Ctrl+Z)", is still split off by IconButton and Button so the 9 existing call sites draw the cap today; there the accessible name keeps the bracket (changing a name is a behaviour change the call site should make on purpose), and no aria-keyshortcuts is added, which would say the shortcut twice. Only a bracket that is a key combination is split ("Attach a picture (or paste, or drop one)" stays text), and the attribute form never parses: a chat titled "Option (B)" must not grow a key cap.

  • 32ch, wrapped. The box was one nowrap line clipped with an ellipsis at the window's width;

a reason a control is disabled is a sentence and was cut. It now wraps at a 32ch measure, and is never wider or taller than the window less the gap on each side.

  • Focus a key moved, only. :focus-visible is true for a field on any focus and for a button a

closing dialog hands focus back to, and neither is a person asking what the control is. The hint shows on focus only when the last key pressed was one that moves focus (Tab, the arrows, Home, End, Page Up, Page Down, F6) and no press has followed it. Whichever of the pointer and the focus moved last names the control: a pointer left resting on one key no longer silences the hint of the key the keyboard moves to.

  • Not over a popup. A control whose own menu or dialog is open (aria-haspopup with

aria-expanded="true") shows no hint, and while focus is inside a menu or a dialog only that popup's own controls do. A fold key is aria-expanded too and keeps its hint: its region is in the page's flow and covers nothing. A control inside a modal <dialog> gets the box as a child of that dialog, because the top layer covers <body>.

  • Row, the last native title (2026-11-11, third pass). Row rendered the platform's

title in both forms; it now carries data-hint and ties its title as the description, with no call-site change. Three things came with it. A component with no title carries data-hint empty so its clipped label can show, and the layers panel wraps such a Row in a Tooltip: an empty host now gives way to a host around it that has words. A row's label sits beside trailing text (a shortcut, a path), so the full label a clipped control shows is the part that is cut, not the whole row run together; and a part hidden from assistive tech is skipped, because the layer's name is drawn in two pieces for the eye beside its whole text. A field's label is its value (never a password's), which is what lets Field replace the palette's hintWhenClipped.

  • Not over a select's list. A select's list opens where the box sits. A press already put the

box away; so does every key in a <select> now, except Tab and a bare modifier (Space, Enter and the arrows open the list or change the value).

  • Outside the layer. The delegation never looked at who rendered the element, so

data-hint, data-hint-keys, data-hint-note and data-hint-placement work on any element. About ninety native titles remain in the surfaces' own markup (the status toggles, the layer keys, the properties' clipped values); tooltip.md ("Adopting the hint outside the layer") is the procedure, including what happens to the accessible name each of them was getting from title.

Disabled controls

Decided 2026-11-11. A disabled Button or IconButton is aria-disabled="true" and never carries the native disabled attribute; the component refuses the click.

  • Why. A control that is blocked by something the user can fix should be able to say what

(the setup sheet's Save: "To save, choose a provider or type a base URL."). The native attribute takes the button out of the Tab order, so a keyboard user can never reach the words, and in some engines it also swallows pointer events on the button, so a mouse user cannot either; the desktop app runs in three different system webviews and the layer cannot pick the well-behaved one.

  • How the click is refused. refuseWhenDisabled (src/ui/Button.tsx, used by both) listens on

the button itself and, while aria-disabled="true", calls preventDefault and stopImmediatePropagation. That is before the caller's onClick, before any ancestor's handler (a native disabled button's click reaches nobody, and a row that selects on click must not start hearing its disabled key), and before a form takes a submit button's click. Enter and Space on a button arrive as the same click, so one guard covers the pointer and both keys.

  • What it costs. A disabled button is now a Tab stop. That is the point where it has a reason

to give, and one extra stop where it has none (the ARIA Authoring Practices guide allows keeping a disabled control focusable where a user must be able to find it). It takes the focus ring, no hover fill and no pressed fill. :disabled no longer matches these two components: a surface that styles one writes [aria-disabled="true"] (src/ui/recipe.test.ts holds the layer to it).

  • Scope. Field keeps the native disabled (a field one cannot type in should not take the

caret), and Row keeps it too (a disabled row in a menu or the palette is skipped by the list's own arrow-key handling, and nothing asks a row to explain itself yet).

A setting switched in place

Decided 2026-11-11, with Toggle. The last hand-drawn controls in the shell were the layer list's three state keys per row and the status bar's eleven drafting toggles: four raw <button aria-pressed> call sites in two files, two recipes.

  • Why not IconButton selected. It was tried and does not fit, for four reasons. Its title

is both the name and the hint, and a state key needs a name that never changes ("Outline frozen", with aria-pressed carrying the state) and a different hint (the action, "Thaw"). selected paints the .14 fill, and "on" is pressed on nearly every row, so every row would gain a fill. The state inks (off, frozen, locked, each with a light-theme step) have no prop. And its box is a circle, where the key is a 20 by 22 cell as tall as the row.

  • The state is the face's alone. No fill at rest, on or off. A glyph toggle swaps its glyph

(icon, iconOn) and takes the tone's ink; a text toggle takes the full ink and a hairline rule in --toggle-on under the word (history: the word's rule became a chip later that day, "The quiet pass" below; the glyph face is as written here). Neither is colour alone. The fills are the layer's own: .08 under the pointer and .14 while held, which the layer keys did not have before.

  • tone is a closed set of four, mapped to tokens the app already had. neutral: off

--text-faint, on --text. absent: on --icon, off --icon-layer-off stepped 15% to the ink (light: --text-dim). info: on --icon-layer-frozen (light: --text-accent). caution: on --icon-locked (light: --warn stepped 20% to the ink). The light steps are in src/ui/ui.css under :root[data-theme="light"], the layer's first theme selector: the two mixes are not single token values, and a token per tone and state would have been six new tokens for one component. No colour was added.

  • The hint is for the eye and is not the description. Every other component exposes its hint

to assistive tech, as the name or the description, because the hint box is aria-hidden. A toggle's hint is the action a press takes now, which the name and aria-pressed already say: "Outline frozen, pressed, Thaw" says the state twice. What a screen reader must also hear (why the toggle is blocked) goes in description, as on IconButton.

  • One Tab stop is the container's. The status bar and the tool strip rove from the container

through a ref (rovingBand, src/components/ToolStrip.tsx), which sets tabIndex on each element. Toggle takes tabIndex as a prop for a container that roves through props, and writes no attribute when the prop is unset, so the two never fight.

  • A small word is as tall as its line. The status bar's line is its row less its top

hairline, and it grows under a finger; a component cannot know either. The container sets --ui-toggle-line, and the word falls back to the row height. It is the one custom property a caller sets for a layer component, and it sets a size the component cannot measure, never a look.

  • Under a finger. The small glyph keeps its 20 by 22 cell and takes the rest of 24 by 24 as an

overhang; the layer list keeps its three keys 4px apart there so the targets do not overlap (they stood flush, with 20 by 22 targets). The word is at least 24 by 24.

  • Disabled. As Button and IconButton: aria-disabled, focusable, the click refused, the face

at the disabled ink in every tone. No call site disables a toggle yet.

  • The curve. The hand-drawn keys eased on the shell's button rule (--ease-out); a Toggle

eases on the layer's measured --ease-standard, as every other component. Same 0.1s.

What stays local in a layer row

Looked at with Toggle, 2026-11-11: the row's colour swatch and its "has objects" mark, both role="img" spans drawn by src/styles.css.

  • The swatch stays local. A Swatch needs a second use, and the candidate was the properties

palette's Color row, which shows a colour's name with no colour beside it. A swatch there would help: "ByLayer" says nothing about which colour the object is drawn in. But the row cannot draw one honestly today. The palette's rows carry the colour as a name (COLOR_CHOICES in src/props.ts: ByLayer, ByBlock, Red and the rest) and no RGB, and the layer list's rule is that no colour is invented in the interface: the swatch paints the engine's own colorRgb. A swatch beside "ByLayer" would mean resolving the layer's colour in TypeScript. The component follows the data: when the engine's property rows carry colorRgb beside the name, build Swatch (a role="img" box named by the colour, --swatch-border, 10px) and give it the layer row and the palette row together. Until then one call site is a local rule.

  • The used mark stays local. One use, two states, no interaction, and its only rule is that

the fill carries the state where the two inks are a step apart. If a second list grows a per-row status mark, it is a component then.

Their sizes moved onto the ladder in passing (10px is --gap-10; 7px is --gap-4 plus --gap-3), with no change to what is drawn.

A row in a listbox

Decided 2026-11-11. The command palette and the assistant's slash list are role="listbox" lists driven from a text field (aria-activedescendant); each drew a Row, a <button>, inside or as its option.

  • What was wrong. Every row was a Tab stop in a list whose keyboard lives in the field, so Tab

from the palette's field walked the rows one by one. And a Row paints its own hover fill, so the row under a resting pointer and the row the arrow keys were on were both lit, in two fills.

  • The pick. Row takes option: it renders the role="option" element itself (a <div>, no

button inside it), with aria-selected from selected, aria-disabled from disabled, the id the field's aria-activedescendant names, and onPointerMove so the listbox can move its highlight under the pointer. It takes no focus and paints no hover: the one lit row is the one the listbox set.

  • Why a mode of Row, not a new component. The band is the same band: height, inset, inks and

the .14 fill. A second component would copy the recipe to change one element and two attributes. tabIndex and a hover switch as separate props were the other offer; they would leave a button inside an option, which the option role flattens for assistive tech.

  • A disabled option still takes the highlight. The palette lights a command that cannot run

and says why under the list; the option keeps the fill at the disabled ink and refuses the click.

  • A disabled current button does not (decided 2026-11-11, second pass). row.md said a

disabled selected row drops its fill and the stylesheet kept it. Both were right, each for one form. In a listbox the fill is the cursor: the keys are on that option whether or not it can run, and a list with no fill has lost its place. A button row's fill says "this is the current one, and you can act on it"; blocked, it reads as an active item that ignores the press. So .ui-row:disabled[aria-current="true"] is transparent at the disabled ink, aria-current stays for assistive tech (the row is still the current one), and .ui-row[aria-disabled="true"][aria-selected="true"] keeps --fill-active. src/ui/recipe.test.ts holds both.

A row in a menu

Decided 2026-11-11. The menus (the bar's dropdowns and submenus, the narrow window's Main menu, the tool strip's overflow menu) are one component, src/components/Menu.tsx, and each of its rows was the last raw <button> drawn by hand in the shell (.menu-row, with its hover, focus and disabled rules in src/chrome.css).

  • The pick. Row takes menuitem: a native button that is the role="menuitem" element

itself, with tabindex="-1" (the menu moves the focus), aria-disabled from disabled, aria-haspopup and aria-expanded from popup and expanded, and the caller's description line from describedBy. onKeyDown and onPointerEnter hand the menu its walk and its hover.

  • Why aria-disabled. A natively disabled button takes no focus: Down would skip Paste, and a

screen reader would never hear that the command exists. The row stays in the walk, shows the ring without the fill, and refuses the click.

  • Why a mode of Row. The band is the same band and so are its ring and its disabled ink. What

a menu changes is stated in one rule (.ui-row--menuitem): the control height (24px, 28px under a finger) instead of the list row's 22px, the full ink (no row of a menu is the current one), a corner concentric with the popover's, and the hover fill held on the keyboard's row and on the row whose submenu is open.

  • No visual or behavioural change. The recipe moved value for value. Measured before and

after in both themes: every row's box, ink, fill, radius and ring in the resting, hovered, focused, expanded and disabled states, the accessibility tree with a submenu open at 1280, 800 and 390, and the menus' behaviour table of real keys and pointer moves. One thing differs by design: the fill's transition is the layer's (background-color, --ease-standard), where the shell's blanket button rule also eased color and border-color on --ease-out.

  • The hook. Menu.tsx finds its rows by [role="menuitem"] under a .menu-item, the role

Row renders, not by a class: the layer's class names are the layer's to change. The slots inside a row (.menu-label, .menu-icon, .menu-name, .menu-shortcut, .menu-arrow) are the menu's own children and stay in src/chrome.css, with --menu-row-h restating the row's height for the grid's tracks and the separators.

  • A clipped label shows in the hint, as on every row: the stacked Main menu at 390px cuts

long labels, and the layer's hint reads them in full. A menu row has no other hint.

A value in a dense row

Decided 2026-11-11 (the audit's open gate on the properties palette's typed values). The palette drew its own <input class="prop-input"> because Field was only the 24px form control. Field now carries all of it, in Select's vocabulary, so a typed value and a picked value in the same column are one recipe:

  • variant="inline": no stroke and no fill until the pointer or the keyboard is on it, then the

field (--border-soft, --control). Focus, a refused value and disabled win over the hover.

  • size="sm": the 20px box of a 22px row on the row's 4px inset, 24px under a coarse pointer, with

the hairline of bottom padding that puts a typed value on the label's baseline.

  • align="end": the value ends on the far edge, with lining tabular figures.
  • mixed: the "*VARIES*" stand-in in the quiet ink.
  • invalid: aria-invalid="true" and the error stroke, as before.
  • onKeyDown, onBlur, ref: commit on Enter and on leaving, restore on Escape, from the caller.
  • A value the box cuts short ends in an ellipsis and shows in full in the hint, with no

data-hint bookkeeping in the caller.

  • selectOnFocus is new behaviour, not a carry-over: a property editor wants typing to replace

the value. Leave it out for a like-for-like move.

Two values differ from the hand-drawn input, both to match the inline Select beside it: the corner is --radius-control (2px, was --radius-small, 3px) and the hover stroke is --border-soft (was --border).

The replacement, in src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx (the text / number match):

<span class="prop-choice">
  <Field
    variant="inline"
    size="sm"
    align="end"
    ariaLabel={props.row().label}
    value={draft()}
    mixed={draft() === VARIES}
    invalid={invalid()}
    inputMode={mode() === "number" ? "decimal" : undefined}
    spellcheck={false}
    autocomplete="off"
    selectOnFocus
    onInput={(value) => {
      setDirty(true);
      setInvalid(false);
      setDraft(value);
    }}
    onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
    onBlur={() => commitText(true)}
  />
</span>

The wrapper is the one the palette's Select already sits in (a one-column grid with the overhang to the column's edge: the field stretches to it). What can then be deleted: every .prop-input rule in src/interaction.css (the base rule, its hover, :focus-visible, [aria-invalid="true"] and .is-varies), hintWhenClipped and cuts in the panel if nothing else uses them, and the .prop-input line of src/ui/recipe.test.ts, which already passes with or without the rule.

Controls that hold a value

Decided 2026-11-11, with Select, Checkbox and TextArea.

  • Native underneath, always. Each is the platform's own control with the layer's face. The

desktop app runs in three system webviews and on phones through the web build; a hand-built listbox or tick would have to re-earn type-ahead, the phone's picker, form participation and input-method handling in each.

  • Select draws its value in a span. A <select> styled directly clips without an ellipsis in

one engine, ignores text-align-last in another and takes its open list's colours from the closed control in a third. The native control lies under the face at no opacity and takes every press; the face is aria-hidden. The select stays in the flow, so the box is as wide as its longest choice asks and does not move as the value changes.

  • The mixed placeholder is not a choice. It is a hidden, disabled first option that only

exists while mixed, so it can be shown and can never be picked.

  • The checkbox's edge is the glyph ink. A hairline stroke (--border, --border-soft) is

drawn to separate surfaces that also differ in fill; an empty box differs from its surface by its edge alone, which needs 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11). --icon holds 5.23 at the least.

  • The checkbox's ring stands off the box by a hairline: at the layer's usual offset of -1 it

would be the accent ring on the accent fill.

  • One line of a TextArea is a Field's height (a 16px line, the field's padding less the

hairline: 24px), so the two can share a row.

  • A bare TextArea draws no ring. It was the only control in the layer without one, and only

because its card shows the focus; since 2026-11-12 the bare Field is the second, for the same reason, and src/ui/recipe.test.ts holds ui.css to those two.

  • 16px under a finger. Under pointer: coarse the field, the text area and the select's

native control take font-size: max(16px, 1em), the size below which a phone zooms the page into the control. Field joined them on 2026-11-11 (it was left open here until its one form was looked at). It keeps its 24px box: under a coarse pointer it gives up its 4px of block padding, and the 16px value sits centred in the box. Looked at on the assistant's setup sheet at 390 wide with the coarse rules applied: the three fields keep their width, height and position (24px each, the same tops), nothing below them moves, and the only change is the typed value and the placeholder at 16px (.design-system/review/wE8-setup-390-coarse-*.png).

  • Section labels are not tracked. typography.md asked for 0.05em to 0.06em on uppercase

section labels; the measured header (research §2: 11px, weight 700, capitals) has none and the layer never drew any. The page moved, as it did for the hover easing.

The quiet pass

Decided 2026-11-11 (the tenth pass), after a review of the whole product against the Cursor captures (.design-system/review/wF9-*.png). Its verdict: a real, restrained shell in which the type was not one system, the chrome claimed attention the drawing should have, and the left insets did not agree. Before and after captures are .design-system/review/wE10-*.png.

One type scale

  • Four sizes on screen: 11, 12, 13 and the 12px mono. 11 is --font-chip (section labels,

counts, key caps, chips, the status bar's toggles; the small button stood here until later that day and is 13: "Token decisions" above). 12 is --font-label (secondary text: menu titles, the command centre, the status bar's facts, a hint, the palette's menu path). 13 is --font-body (everything read or typed). The mono is --font-mono.

  • The shell's scale won over Cursor's composer. The tokens were measured from Cursor 3.27.22,

whose composer and transcript are 15px on a 24px line, whose button is 14px and whose small text is 11.5px. That measurement is the history of --composer-font, --composer-leading, --font-button and --font-small. Beside a 13px shell the result was six sizes (11, 11.5, 12, 13, 14, 15) in 19 size, weight and leading combinations, and the assistant read as a second product in the same window. Cursor's 15px sits in an editor whose code is 13 to 14px; ours sits beside a drawing whose chrome is 13px and should stay behind it. The owner has not chosen between the two; the default taken here is the shell's, and the choice is two lines of src/tokens.css to reverse.

  • How. --composer-font is var(--font-body) and --composer-leading is 20px (13px on

20px is the 1.54 ratio of 15 on 24, on a whole pixel). --font-button is var(--font-body). --font-small is var(--font-label): an alias kept for the sheets that name it, holding no size of its own. The status bar's facts and the command line's error moved from 11.5 to 12; the compact tab from 11.5 to 12; the command line's prompt mark from 14 to the mono's 12.

  • Sizes that did not move. Button 28 and 24, Field 24, rows 22, the bars 35, 28, 35 and 22:

every height is a token of its own and none was derived from a type size (measured in the browser before and after).

On is a fill and an ink, never a hue

  • A text toggle that is on is a chip. The on word was the full ink over a 1px rule in

--toggle-on: white text with a green underline, which read as a link and was the brightest text in the status bar. It is now --text-dim on a chip (--fill-active, --radius-control, 3px shorter than the line at each end), and off is --text-faint on nothing. The two differ by the fill and by lightness. The chip is the word's ::before, so the button still takes no state fill and the target is still the whole line; the word's hover and press are drawn on the same chip. Measured on the status bar: off 6.48 (dark) and 5.68 (light), on 7.23 and 6.37. The glyph face is unchanged: a glyph has a second glyph to change to, a word does not.

  • An on word is the full ink on the faintest chip (a second review, the same week). As

--text-dim on --fill-active a bar of on words read as grey slabs: two chips 2px apart (OTRACK and OSNAP, TRANSP and DYN) merged into one bar, and the on ink stood 1.6 from the off ink (1.5 light), so the fill alone carried the state. On is now --text on --hover, and off is still --text-faint on nothing: 14.1 on its chip against 6.5 on the bar (dark), 14.1 against 5.7 (light), the two inks 2.6 and 2.9 apart, so the word says on with the chip taken away. The chip steps to --fill-active under the pointer and --fill-pressed while held. An off word under the pointer takes --text-dim on --hover, a step short of the on word at rest, which it would otherwise be drawn as. The word's inset is 3px, the chip's own distance from the line's ends, and the status bar keeps two words 4px apart: the run is 2px shorter over its eleven words than it was, and wraps at 499px where it wrapped at 501.

  • A light field's edge is the default stroke. Field and Select drew --border-soft at

rest in both themes. On the dark pane that edge measures 1.34 and shows; on the light pane it measured 1.27, and 1.18 against the field's own #F3F3F3, and a form was three grey slabs. The light theme sets the edge's ink (--ui-field-edge) to --border: 1.39 against the pane, 1.28 against the fill. It is an ink and not border-color, so the inline variant's transparent edge, the focus ink and the error ink still win by their place in the sheet. TextArea's field variant drew --border-soft in both themes until 2026-11-12 and reads the same ink now.

  • A selected icon button is the full ink on the .08 fill, squared. It was the .14 fill

at the button's round radius. Its three call sites are the title bar's layout keys, two of which are on at rest: two filled discs were the second most salient thing in the bar. Ink alone was considered (--text against --icon, 14.1 against 9.4 on the bar) and is too close to tell on from off without a second key to compare with, so the fill stays, one step fainter, and takes --radius-control so that on is a shape of its own and not a hover that stuck. It is the layer's one selected recipe, not a variant: no call site wants the louder one.

  • The current layer is the selected fill, the accent bar and --text. Its name was green

too (a third mark in dark; in light the green was mixed toward the ink to pass). Green was also "on" under every toggle. Neither is any more: --layer-current is removed, and --toggle-on is the engine badge's dot alone.

  • The prompt mark takes the accent only while a command runs. At rest it is --text-faint

(6.16 dark, 5.79 light on the band); with a command running, --text-accent (5.98, 6.37).

  • Two ink steps under the text, not three. .74, .66 and .60 could not be told apart.

--icon is var(--text-dim) in both themes. The dark --text-faint was to move to about .52 and could not: it is text on the selected fill (a key cap in a lit row, a neutral chip while pressed), where it measures 4.54 at .60 over the elevated surface, 4.45 at .59 and 3.83 at .52. .60 is its floor, so the ladder is .74 and .60.

Light surfaces

  • --control #e8e8e8 to #F3F3F3: a resting field on the #FCFCFC pane (1.19:1) read as

disabled, and the assistant's queue tray sat grey under a white composer. A placeholder on the new fill measures 5.68. --control-hover takes #e8e8e8 (it was #dedede), which is the .08 hover over the pane, so the properties palette's hovered row matches the layer list's.

  • --cmd-bg is var(--chrome) and --cmd-border is var(--border): as #ebebeb under

#c9c9c9 the command line was the darkest chrome on the page.

The sidebar's columns

  • One text column. A property's label started at 8px while the headings' labels and the

layers' names started at 24px. The rail names the column once (--rail-text on .sidebar: the heading's inset, its fold key and the gap after it) and the property rows start on it.

  • One right edge for values. A choice's value ended 16px before a read-only one (the arrow

and its gap). Every value now ends one arrow's slot before the column's end, and only a choice's arrow stands in the slot. The arrow stays at rest: it was put there so a choice never reads as a fixed value, and hiding it until hover would have undone that.

  • A layer's keys show its unusual states. Each row drew three keys, nearly all in their

ordinary state: twenty-seven glyphs on a nine-layer list, in which the one layer that was off was hard to find. A key in its ordinary state (on, thawed, unlocked) is drawn only on the row under the pointer or holding the keyboard; off, frozen and locked are always drawn. The hidden keys are faded, not removed: they keep their cells, names and Tab stops, and a finger (no hover) gets all of them.

The status bar stands still

The review saw the toggles shift about 59px when the pointer entered the drawing. Measured, the coordinates were not the cause (their box already had a reserved width): the selection count was. It stood after the coordinates and pushed the whole run 60px each time something was selected. It is now the last of the facts at the start of the bar, so nothing that comes and goes sits between the toggles and the bar's end. The order in which the bar gives up room is unchanged, and the sweep was run again from 300 to 1300 wide with ordinary and long content: no toggle is clipped at any width.

A task over the page

Decided 2026-11-11, with Dialog. An audit found the web interface had no dialogs at all: the removed desktop interface's Options, Drafting Settings and Layer Properties Manager were never rebuilt, and the engine's rule ("programmatic calls never open dialogs") makes a dialog an interface surface that reads the engine's state and acts through execute. Captures are .design-system/review/wE12-*.png.

  • Native, shown modally. showModal() gives the focus trap, Escape's close request, the inert

page and the top layer in each of the three system webviews; none of them is rebuilt. The caller owns open, so the dialog cancels the platform's own close and asks through onClose. When the platform closes it without asking (a second Escape in a row), the caller is told, and a caller that keeps open true gets its dialog back.

  • The box is the palette's. --surface-elevated, the --border hairline, --radius-block

and --shadow-popover: the command palette's box, value for value, because the two are the same kind of thing (a box over the page) and a second recipe would be a second elevation.

  • --scrim is new, the layer's first veil: rgba(0,0,0,.4) dark, rgba(0,0,0,.16) light.

The palette leaves the page undimmed because it is a tool over the work; a modal dialog is the opposite, and the dimmed page is what says the page is not taking input. No existing token could be it: the fills are the ink at an alpha (they lighten in dark), and the surfaces are opaque. The colour is the one the shadows already cast with, at the tooltip shadow's alpha in each theme, so no hue and no new value entered the system. Nothing is read through it.

  • Widths are a measure, not pixels. 52ch, 76ch and 104ch of the dialog's own 13px type:

364, 533 and 729px measured. 76ch is the palette's width. The brief asked for about 360, 520 and 720; a ch measure needed no size token and follows the type if the scale ever moves.

  • No motion. The palette's reason holds: it is opened from a key or a menu, and anything that

plays before the first field reads as lag. The "open" preset stays for menus and popovers. The box also carries no transform, which is what lets the layer's hint, a fixed child of the open dialog, be placed in the window's coordinates.

  • Focus. On opening, the first field of the body that is showing (a page behind holds fields

too), or initialFocus; never the close key. With no field, the dialog itself: a question with two buttons does not put the keyboard on either answer, least of all Delete. Under a coarse pointer the dialog itself as well, because focusing a text field there raises the keyboard over a sheet nobody has read yet. Opening waits a microtask, so the caller's own effects (a form read afresh, the page it opens on) have run before the field is chosen. On closing, the focus goes back to what had it.

  • Enter is the form's. The body and the footer are one <form> that submits nothing, and the

primary action is a Button type="submit". Enter in a single-line field then presses it through the platform's implicit submission: no key handler, so a key an input method is using never does it, and an aria-disabled primary refuses it as it refuses any click.

  • A press outside counts only when it began and ended outside the box (a selection dragged

out of a field ends there and is not a decision), and a caller with work to lose turns it off.

  • Under 560px it is a sheet from the bottom, not a page. The actions sit under the thumb and

over an on-screen keyboard (the height follows dvh), the drawing stays in sight above a short dialog, and a question of two buttons is not a screen of empty space. A full-window page was the other offer; it suits a long form and hides what the dialog is about, and a sheet that is tall enough becomes that page anyway, less the tab strip's height it leaves showing so that it still reads as over the page.

  • No landmarks inside. The title bar and the footer are plain boxes: a <header> or

<footer> in a dialog is announced as the page's banner or footer.

  • The palette stays off it. Moving CommandPalette onto Dialog was weighed against "no

change in behaviour or look" and does not fit, in six ways: it has no title bar (its name is an aria-label) and no footer of actions; its page is not dimmed, on purpose; it hangs from the title bar instead of standing in the middle or on the bottom edge; its <dialog> is the whole window with the box inside it, which is how a click beside it is told from one in it; every click inside hands the focus back to its one field; and Escape keeps what was typed for the next opening. A bare variant that removes the title bar, the scrim, the placement, the form and the focus rule is not a variant of this component, it is the palette. What the two share is the box's four tokens and the lines that keep the caller's open true to the platform, and both already agree.

  • TabPanels is automatic. A dialog's page is already built, so the arrow keys show it as

they move; the layout strip over the drawing stays manual, because a switch there redraws the drawing.

The first dialog: Drafting Settings

  • No transaction, so the dialog makes its own order. The engine has no settings object and

no undo-free transaction. planCalls (src/drafting.ts) refuses the whole form when one value would be refused, so nothing is half-applied because of a typing mistake; the calls then all run (they do not depend on one another), each refusal is shown beside its field with a count of what was applied, and the engine is read again and the form planned against it, which also catches a call answered ok and not honoured (dsettings drops a spacing it does not like without saying so).

  • One undo step for the spacings. SNAPUNIT and GRIDUNIT are the drawing's header variables,

so writing them is an undoable edit; both go in one dsettings call. Everything else is session state the engine records no undo for.

  • OK and Cancel. rule/button-label-verb asks for a verb; a form of several settings has no

one verb, "Apply" traditionally keeps a dialog open, and OK beside Cancel is the pair the dialog's users already read (rule/dialog-action-labels). A dialog that does one thing takes its verb.

  • The snap markers are the canvas's. Each box shows snapGlyph(bit) from src/canvas.ts as

SVG paths, at the canvas's 12px and 1.5px stroke: one table of figures, drawn in two places.

Inside a field, and the last two inputs

Decided 2026-11-12. Workers on the two passes before reported what the layer lacked, and each had worked around it in a surface's stylesheet. The gaps are closed in the layer and the workarounds are deleted. Captures are .design-system/review/wE14-*.png.

An adornment inside a field

  • What was wrong. The API key's show and hide key stood inside the field's end from a wrapper

of the setup sheet's own, on a patch of the field's fill. The field could not be given end padding from outside without restyling it, so the last 3 characters of a 203-character key, and the caret after them, lay under the patch.

  • The pick. Field takes start and end. With either, the field is a

<span class="ui-field-box"> around the same <input>, and the input is still the whole box: the adornments stand inside its two ends, over padding the input grows by each one's width. So there is one stroke, one focus ring and one error edge, drawn around the adornments by the rules every field already has, in every variant and size; the clipped-value hint measures the same input; and nothing is duplicated for a second box. A field with neither prop is the bare <input> it was, so no other call site's markup or selectors changed.

  • Why the width is measured. An adornment is a 20px key, a 14px glyph, a mark in a gutter or

a few characters, and the stylesheet cannot know which. Field.tsx writes each slot's laid-out width on the box (--ui-field-start, --ui-field-end) when it is laid out and when it changes; until then the stylesheet's default is one small control, the common case. The other offer was a box that draws the stroke itself around a strokeless input: it needs every state rule twice and :has() to tell the input's focus from the adornment's.

  • The cell. In field and inline an adornment's cell is the small control (20px), centred

in the box and 2px from its edge at md: an IconButton size="sm" is concentric with the 24px field, and a glyph sits in the middle of the cell. The value ends 2px before it. In bare the surface owns the geometry: the cell is the adornment's own width, on the edge, with no gap.

  • A glyph is not a control. The slot passes the pointer through, so a press on a glyph lands

on the input; only a control in the slot takes it. Under a coarse pointer the small icon button takes its 24 by 24 target from the layer's own rule, inside the field's height.

  • Measured. The key field keeps its box (297 by 24 at 962, 238) and the eye its place (20 by

20 at 1237, 240) before and after; the input's end padding is 24px where it was 6px; a 203-character key ends before the eye with the caret after its last character; the eye toggles and keeps the focus.

The quiet button

  • What was wrong. The setup sheet's Change was a ghost dimmed by

.assistant-setup-change .ui-button { color: var(--text-dim) }: a colour set on a layer component from outside, which reached one state.

  • The pick: variant="quiet". No resting fill and the secondary ink; the full ink on ghost's

own fills under the pointer and the press, as the ghost IconButton wakes. One new value on the prop the button already has.

  • Why not tone="quiet" on ghost. A second prop gives the button two axes, and the pairs

it creates mean nothing (a quiet primary, a quiet danger). variant already names purpose, and "must read after the text beside it" is a purpose.

  • Why not link. A button drawn as a link promises navigation, and the action stays on the

sheet (trap/link-as-button is the trap's name). A link ink would also be the accent, which the system keeps for signals.

  • Measured, dark and light. The label 9.17 and 7.82 at rest, 13.35 and 15.24 on the hover

fill, 11.12 and 13.37 on the pressed fill; the focus ring 6.43 and 6.60 against the sheet; the disabled label 3.08 and 2.30 (the layer's one disabled ink). One thing differs from the dimmed ghost: under the pointer and the press the label is the full ink, where it stayed dim.

  • src/ui/recipe.test.ts now fails any surface stylesheet that sets a colour or a fill on

.ui-button.

A bare field, and the two inputs still drawn by hand

  • variant="bare". The command line's input and the palette's search input both sit in a

box their surface draws, and neither is the 24px stroked form control or the inline value of a list row: the command line's is mono on the recessed fill, and the palette's shows no ring, because its field holds the focus for as long as the dialog is open. TextArea already had the answer and the word. A bare Field draws no stroke, no fill, no inset and no ring, takes the surface's face and size, and keeps the control's height and the layer's line. A mono or recessed prop was the other offer and is a style prop.

  • The palette moved with no change to see. The lens at 386.7, 17 and the typed text at 408.7

before and after; the caret in the accent (inherited from the header); role="combobox" with aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-activedescendant, aria-autocomplete and aria-describedby as before; the query kept and selected on reopening. autocapitalize joined the pass-throughs for it. Under a coarse pointer the 16px type is the layer's rule now (pointer: coarse), where the palette's own asked for a fine pointer with hover.

  • The command line moved, and its line became a strip. The prompt mark stood in an 8px

gutter, its own width, so it read as part of the text ("›Command:"), and the box stood 3px from the pane on one side and 8px on the other. Both follow from one constraint: the typed text stays on the editor's column, 12px from the pane, and a box inset from the pane leaves the mark less than that. So the box gave way: the typed line is a strip from one edge of the pane to the other, a hairline above and below it, and the mark has the whole column to stand in. Measured at 1280 (pane at 252): the text at 264 before and after; the mark's cell 256.5 to 263.5 before and 254.5 to 261.5 now, 2.5px and then 4.5px clear of the text and of the edge on its other side; the field 255 to 1272 before (3px and 8px from the pane) and 252 to 1280 now; the panel 37px tall before and after. The strip shows the focus (the focus ink on its hairlines and the ring around it), told by the component, not by :focus-within, because the error beside it takes the focus too. An error still stands on the band, and the strip is closed with a hairline where it stops short of the pane's edge.

  • What held. Typing from the drawing lands its first character in the field; Enter submits;

Escape clears typed text and then cancels the command; Up and Down walk the history; the keyword chips' words are on the column; F6 and Ctrl+J reach the field. The field takes no value: the history writes the element's own, as before, so nothing is assigned back while an input method is composing, and Field no longer hands onKeyDown a key an input method is using (the hand-drawn input did, so Enter that confirmed a composition also submitted).

  • One hook stays. src/app.tsx finds the field as .cmd-input (F6, Ctrl+J, typing from the

drawing). Field takes no class, so the command line adds that name to the element once it is mounted, with no rule on it. When the shell asks for .cmdline input instead, the hook goes.

Two raw buttons that stay

Looked at for Row, Chip and the quiet Button, and left: the checker still pins 2 raw buttons in src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.

  • The tool row (.assistant-tool). Row is a 22px band of one line with a hover fill. The

tool row is a line of prose that wraps to a second line for its note, opens in place, has no fill (its ink steps instead) and carries the transcript's 20px leading and inset. Row could be given expanded, but every other value of its recipe would then be overridden from the assistant's stylesheet, which is the thing a component is for preventing. It is a disclosure row, and it has one use; a Disclosure is a component when a second surface folds a region from a line of text. One thing it lacks today, found and left because the move was to change nothing: it says aria-expanded and names no region (aria-controls).

  • The model slot (.assistant-ghost). It is a pill: 24px tall, 13px type at the secondary

ink, an 8px inset, a round corner, a label that gives way to an ellipsis, a chevron, and a two-line hint. A Chip is 20px at 11px in the quiet ink; a quiet Button size="sm" is the right height, type and ink, but has a 2px corner and a 6px inset, does not shrink, and takes no expanded, controls or second hint line. Adopting either changes the corner and the inset, and the brief was no change. What would make it fit: expanded and controls on Button (small, and IconButton has them), a label that clips inside the button, and a decision that the composer's model key is a 2px-cornered button like the rest of the layer's rather than Cursor's pill.

The hint inside a dialog

Verified in the browser with Drafting Settings open, by the pointer and by the keyboard, on the close key and on an object snap box given a hint for the test: the box is a child of the open dialog, is drawn over its footer and past its edge, and is not clipped. Nothing changed. No object snap box carries a hint today: Checkbox takes no title.

The jeweller's pass (2026-11-13)

Looked at every state at 1280, 1440 and 390, dark and light, and changed what a jeweller would notice first. Local styles only; no token, component or wording changed.

  • The Tech Sheet's paper holds its views. The backdrop is a flex row that stretched the page

to its own height, so the four views ran off the bottom of the paper onto the backdrop. .techsheet-scroll now aligns the page to the top: the page is as tall as what is on it.

  • Proposals take the assistant's height. The cards were capped at two and a half blocks

under an empty transcript, so a decision that waited scrolled inside a strip while the panel above it was empty. While proposals wait, the composer grows and the transcript keeps two lines (proposals.css).

  • Before and After are tags on the pictures. The captions were a line under each tile; they

are now a small tag in the tile's corner (the secondary ink on the elevated surface), so the pair reads as one comparison and each card is a line shorter.

  • A command's JSON answer is quiet in the log. The answers are records, not sentences, and

at full width they buried the commands typed. A line that starts with { or [ keeps the quiet ink even when newest, and an older one is clipped to two lines on screen (the document keeps every character for a copy or a screen reader). The newest answer is whole.

The jeweller's second pass (2026-11-13)

  • Every JSON answer in the log is cut to two lines, the newest too. The first pass left the

newest answer whole, and a propose or piece answer is ten lines of braces that pushed the commands typed out of the panel. Now the newest is cut like the older ones; when the record has a message, that sentence is drawn above it in the words' ink (aria-hidden, not selectable: the record says it already), so the answer reads as a sentence first. A record longer than about two lines has a fold key (IconButton, expanded + controls) that shows it whole. The document keeps every character, so a copy and a screen reader get the whole record as before. This undoes "the newest answer is whole" from the first pass, on purpose.

  • A narrow proposal card puts each figure's name over its values. At the assistant's default

width the four columns left the name a third of the card, and "Metal weight" broke over two lines inside its row. Below 22rem of card (a container query on .proposal) each row is a grid: the name on its own line, then before, after and the change in three fixed columns so the arrows and the changes line up down the card. Because a grid row loses the table's meaning, the table says its roles in the markup (role="table", row, rowheader, cell, ...), and because a browser copies grid rows a cell per line, the table writes its own copy: the rows the selection touches as tab-separated lines (rowsTsv), exactly what the wide table copies.

  • Piece reads as a jeweller's spec, not a property form. Same rows, same controls, same

commands; the change is order and type (PiecePanel.tsx, piece.ts, interaction.css):

  • A summary on top: the size (with the inside diameter), the metal's weight (with the alloy)

and the stones' weight (with the count) as three figures in the text ink at 600, their names and qualifiers in the quiet inks; then the centre stone in words for a solitaire or a three-stone. These are the engine's figures that were the "results" list under the rows, so that list is gone; its "Also" row (the size in the other systems) moved into the Ring group.

  • A failing check stands right under the summary, before any parameter, as the proposal

cards draw a check a change would fail: "Fail" in the warning ink at 600, the sentence in the text ink, behind a warning edge. No inset fill: --warn on the light --surface-inset is 4.19:1, under AA for an 11px word; on the rail's surface it is 4.53:1 light, 10.1:1 dark. Passing checks keep their quiet list at the end.

  • The parameters fall into Ring, Band, Stones and Head (pieceGroups), each under a quiet

11px capital word; each group is a list named "<Group> parameters" (the word itself is aria-hidden, the list's name says it). The Tab order is the rows' order as before.

  • A length's unit moved from the label ("Wall, mm") to a quiet mm inside the field's end

(Field's end slot, aria-hidden); the control's accessible name is still the full label. One shown wording changed because of it: a round stone's diameter would have read as a second "Stone" under the stone's material, so it is drawn "Stone size" (rowShownName).

  • Bench reads as a bench sheet. Its lines fall into Stones and Metal, each under a head line

carrying the part's totals (52 pc, 2.54 ct; 7.39 g) in the same columns as its lines; a line's value is two right-aligned tabular columns (pieces and carats; a band's size and grams), so the figures line up down the sheet (BenchLine.part and .cells, read by parseBench). The cost's total closes the money under a hairline, at the body size. Pressing a line still selects what it counts.

The jeweller's third pass (2026-11-13)

  • The Piece summary is two lines and the parameters get the room. In a window 800 tall the

summary pushed the parameters down to four rows. The figures' names (Size, Metal, Stones) are no longer drawn: "US 6", "3.53 g" and "1.19 ct" say what they are, and each name is still the figure's dt for a screen reader (clipped, not display: none). The centre stone keeps its line (it says the cut, the stone and the prongs, which no figure does). The section's cap is half the rail (it was 44%) and it gives way a quarter as fast as the sections under it (flex-shrink: 0.25): a flex box shrinks by its own height, so the tallest section, the piece, was the one losing rows. While a piece is open the layers pane caps at a fifth of the rail and scrolls (a piece's drawing has the same eight layers); folding the piece gives them their share back. The "Also" row (the size in the other systems) is one line ending in an ellipsis, the whole in its title, where it wrapped to two. At 1280x800 the piece shows eight parameter rows under the summary (four before) and the bench keeps its rows. The failing check still stands under the summary.

  • The passing checks fold to one line. "All 4 checks pass" ("3 checks pass" when one fails;

passingLine) is a quiet Button disclosure with a chevron that turns (no turn under reduced motion); Button gained expanded and controls for it (aria-expanded, aria-controls). Folded by default; the list is hidden when folded, so it leaves the Tab order. Failing checks are never folded. Wording added: the line itself.

  • The bench's money is in the sheet's type, on the sheet's edge. The cost lines were 12px

against the sheet's 13px, so their digits were not the carats' and grams' tabular digits, and their right edge was the text column's width, equal to the lines' end inset only by chance. They are now the body size, end on the lines' own inset (--gap-8 + --prop-arrow-slot), and "Edit prices" ends its label (not its button's inset) on that edge. The amounts keep the secondary ink so the total still leads. Labels: at the rail's default width "Round 6.5 mm" fits beside both columns (measured at 1280 and 1440); a longer label ends in an ellipsis as before. Not changed: the columns' widths, which hold "36 pc" and "2.54 ct" exactly.

  • The title bar's glyphs weigh what the ribbon's do. Measured in the page: every glyph is

drawn with one stroke, 1.25 CSS px (STROKE, non-scaling), at 12, 14 and 16 px alike, so the stroke itself was already consistent and is unchanged. What read heavier was the shapes: the sidebar and panel keys were square-cornered frames filling 16 of the 24 grid at 14 px, a block of ink beside the ribbon's open, round-cornered sheets. Both frames are now 15x13 with the 2-unit round corner the ribbon's sheets use (ui.toggle.palettes, layout.bottom). The assistant's spark was a touch larger than its neighbours' frames and its concave joins piled ink at the centre; it is drawn 13 units across (was 14) with the small plus kept full size, so the plus still reads as a plus at 14 px. Checked as 4x crops at 2x in both themes; the ribbon's glyphs (held to the 16 px pixel grid by icons.test.ts) are unchanged.

The chrome pass (2026-11-13)

  • An empty drawing invites a start. A new drawing showed a bare grid; the only way in was the

Piece section in the rail. A quiet card now sits over empty model space (StartSurface.tsx): the four piece kinds (the piece command, as the rail runs it), Templates..., Open a file... and Ask the assistant, all existing commands. It shows only while the drawing has no entities, the view is model space and no command runs; the layer passes the pointer through, only the card takes it. Colours are existing tokens (--surface-elevated, --border-soft, --text-dim).

  • The Jewelry tab is marked and opens with a way in. The tab carries the stone glyph in

--text-accent (decoration, aria-hidden); its band leads with a Start group holding Templates (ui.dialog.templates, a new code-drawn four-sheet glyph on the strip pixel grid). Wording added: "Start", "Templates" as a tool label.

The assistant and dialogs pass (2026-11-13)

  • A page behind in Drafting Settings no longer draws its ticks through the page in front. The

checkbox's tick sets its own visibility (shown only when checked), which overrode the hidden page's inherited visibility: hidden: the Object Snap page's ticks showed as stray marks over Snap and Grid, one inside the empty Snap box and a doubled tick in Grid. Inside a hidden page the tick stays hidden (dialogs.css). No change to Checkbox itself.

  • Waiting proposals own the assistant when the chat is empty. The empty state's line was

squeezed into a clipped strip over the cards, touching "3 options: accept one". With no messages and proposals waiting, the empty state gives way and the empty transcript takes no height, so the cards start under the title. The group's line is drawn in the secondary ink (was faint).

  • Out of date is said in the warning ink. A stale card's tag was a neutral Chip, read as a

label; it is now a word beside the title in --warn at 600 (8.79:1 dark on --surface-elevated, 4.53:1 light). Same wording.

  • The small field dialogs are small. Ring, Stone and Price book were the medium width, which

put a value 40 characters from its name ("Wall, in mm" ... "1.8"). They are sm (52ch), so the name and value read as one line and the refusal under a field stands near it. Drafting Settings keeps md: its Object Snap page wraps to more rows at sm and every page takes its height.

The four views and the handles (2026-11-13)

  • Four views on one context, not four canvases. The 3D tab tiles Top, Perspective, Front and

Right on its one canvas: each pane is a scissored viewport of a store kept between frames (preserveDrawingBuffer), so a pane is drawn only when its eye or the piece changed. Four contexts would quadruple the programs and the buffers and run into the browser's few contexts; an offscreen cache per pane would be the same saving with more to go wrong. The pane frames and names are DOM over the canvas that take no pointer; the canvas finds the pane itself (fourview.ts, paneAt). The workflow (four tiled views, a double-click maximises) is the jewellers' common one; the look is ours: names in the elevated-surface chip of the region labels, the active pane ringed in --canvas-focus-ring, the hairline between panes in --chrome-dark.

  • The orthographic panes are flat-shaded with edges. Realistic stays the Perspective pane's;

a measuring view wants a sharp, steady silhouette. Edges take --text-faint, the one ink.

  • Controls added to the 3D bar: a Toggle "4 views" (text, a setting switched in place) and,

in four views, a quiet Button "Maximise"/"Restore" for the active pane (M). No new component.

  • A handle is a role="slider" element, not a registry component. It is a grip drawn on the

piece at a projected point, in the drawing's own grip inks (--canvas-focus-ring at rest, --canvas-grip-hover, --canvas-grip-hot while held), with a touch-sized hit area round a 12 px dot. It carries its name, range and value in millimetres; the arrows nudge, Enter commits, Escape puts it back. Only one placing of each handle takes the Tab stop (the Perspective pane's when it is shown); the same handle on another pane is aria-hidden.

  • The number in hand stands beside the pointer on the elevated surface (.view3d-drag), flips

to the other side near the stage's right or bottom edge, and is a polite status: the value, what it was, and the checks it would break in --error, or "Checks pass" in --text-faint. The gizmo hides while a handle is held, so the words are never under it.
